## AFLDB-ISSUE-117 — Retired access keys cannot be removed from the admin UI

- **Status:** **RESOLVED — 2026-09-13.** Implemented, reconciled onto current `main`, and
  **MERGED** (`a0b2ea4`; branch tip `0378180` is an ancestor of `main`). DB-free validation green
  2026-09-06; the DB-backed suites are DONE (`tests/integration/access-codes.test.ts` 8/8 after
  `091` was applied; the `tests/integration/privileges.test.ts` shortfall is `AFLDB-ISSUE-138`, not
  this issue). Migration `091`, `db:privileges` and the code all reached `afldb_dev` in the
  `AFLDB-ISSUE-155` DEV deployment of 2026-09-11 (94/94 applied, 0 pending). The four-state
  `/admin/access` DEV Playwright browser gate has now PASSED; see *Resolution (2026-09-13)* below
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Area:** Admin / Access management / Security
- **Found:** 2026-08-31 (operator report)
- **Branch:** `claude/issue-117` (worktree `D:\dev\afldb-issue-117`), cut from `main` @ `8dd96c5`.
  Supersedes the original, unmerged `claude/issue-116` @ `2344ab5`, which stays as history.
- **Files:** `src/db/migrations/091_access_code_delete.sql` (new);
  `src/db/queries/access-codes.ts` (new — `deleteRetiredAccessCode`, `retirementReason`);
  `src/app/admin/access/actions.ts` (`deleteAccessCode`);
  `src/app/admin/access/AccessManager.tsx` (`DeleteCodeButton`);
  `src/styles/globals.css`; `tools/maintenance/privileges.sql`;
  `tests/admin-access-actions.test.ts` (new); `tests/integration/access-codes.test.ts` (new);
  `tests/integration/privileges.test.ts`
- **Related:** `AFLDB-ISSUE-027` (a required audit commits atomically with its mutation);
  `AFLDB-ISSUE-119` (which built `auditInTransaction`, the mechanism this issue now uses);
  `AFLDB-ISSUE-142` Finding C and `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` (the DEV migration-parity consequence)
- **Runbook:** `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-117.md`

> **ID note.** The operator brief was written as "AFLDB-ISSUE-116" and the original branch is
> `claude/issue-116`. `AFLDB-ISSUE-116` was already allocated to the `player_match_stats` Data QA
> anchor, and `AFLDB-ISSUE-115`'s Resolution cites 116 as its follow-up, so renumbering that would
> falsify a closed issue's history. This work took **117**.

### Problem

`/admin/access` can revoke an access key but never remove one. `revokeAccessCode` sets
`beta_access_codes.revoked_at` and the row survives, which is correct — revocation disables a key
immediately while keeping its record — but nothing then disposes of a key that is finished with.
`src/app/admin/access/page.tsx` selects every code with no state filter, so retired rows accumulate
permanently. A **spent** key is worse than untidy: the table offers Revoke only in the `live`
state, so a spent key could be neither revoked nor deleted.

### Investigation — what had to be true before adding any DELETE

1. **No foreign key references `beta_access_codes`.** Every migration searched for
   `REFERENCES beta_access_codes`: no hits. Deleting a row orphans nothing and needs no cascade.
2. **Two soft references exist, and both are safe.** The redeem path mints a beta session whose
   claim subject is `code:<id>`, but `hasBetaAccess()` and `src/middleware.ts` verify signature,
   kind, expiry and epoch and **never look the id up** — so deleting a key ends no live session,
   exactly as revoking one does not. `auth_audit_log` keeps `codeId`/`label` in its
   `beta.code_redeemed` detail, so redemption history survives the row. `id` is
   `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`, so a freed id is never reissued.
3. **`afldb_auth` held no DELETE on the table** (023 granted `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE`), so the
   feature would have failed closed in production on a permission error while passing every test
   that did not connect as that role.
4. **`privileges.sql`'s `afldb_auth` section is subtractive**, so a grant made only by a migration
   is revoked by the next reconcile or restore. Both files had to change.

### Fix

- **Migration 091** grants `afldb_auth` `DELETE` on `beta_access_codes` and nothing else, under the
  usual `IF EXISTS (afldb_auth)` role guard. Precedent: `data_submission_rows` (023),
  `site_media` (037).
- **`tools/maintenance/privileges.sql`** specifies `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE`, so the
  reconciler preserves the grant instead of revoking it.
- **`deleteRetiredAccessCode`** holds the one destructive statement, with the eligibility rule in
  its `WHERE` clause: `revoked_at IS NOT NULL OR (max_uses IS NOT NULL AND use_count >= max_uses)`.
  A forged POST naming a still-redeemable key matches no row and deletes nothing.
- **`deleteAccessCode`** calls `requireAdmin()` first, then runs the delete and its
  `access.code_deleted` audit inside one `authSql.begin`, so an audit failure aborts the deletion.
  Detail carries `codeId`, `label`, `reason`, `useCount`, `maxUses` — what was destroyed and which
  rule allowed it — and no secret, since only the sha256 was ever stored and it leaves with the
  row. "Not retired", "never existed" and "already deleted" return one message, so the endpoint is
  not an oracle for which ids exist.
- **UI.** A revoked **or spent** row offers **Delete…**, which opens an in-row confirmation naming
  the key and its state before anything submits. Revoke's semantics and visibility are untouched.

### The rule, and why widening it was safe

Every limb of the predicate is a reason `redeemBetaCode` would refuse the code — it redeems only
when `revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()) AND (max_uses IS NULL OR
use_count < max_uses)`. "Revoked or spent" is therefore a **strict subset of "not redeemable"**: no
key that could still admit somebody became deletable. A **partly used** key stays refused (two of
five uses spent still leaves three admissions) and an **unlimited** key is never spent
(`max_uses IS NULL` makes the comparison NULL, not true) — the case only real PostgreSQL
three-valued logic settles. An **expired** key is deliberately still not deletable: expiry is a
moving line that passes on its own, with nobody deciding anything, and deletion is irreversible.
Consequence, unchanged and deliberate: an expired unspent key is offered neither control.

### Consequence for `afldb_dev` and AFLDB-ISSUE-139 — the orphan ledger row survives

`afldb_dev` has `079_access_code_delete.sql` **applied**, from the original branch. Renumbering
does not and cannot remove that row, so the arithmetic after this merge is:

- `tools/db/migrate.ts:192` computes pending as *files not in the ledger*, so an applied row with
  no file is ignored. **`afldb_dev` can safely be migrated forward**, and applying `091` there is
  additionally safe because `GRANT` is idempotent — the grant is already present.
- `tools/db/promotion-check.ts:366` computes `unknown` as *applied names not in files*, and any
  non-empty `unknown` FAILS the gate. After applying `091`, `afldb_dev` would hold 92 applied rows
  against 91 files and still report `UNKNOWN 079_access_code_delete.sql`.

**So merging this issue does NOT clear ISSUE-139's `pre-cutover` parity refusal**, and nothing in
this issue tries to. That refusal is truthful and stays exactly as `AFLDB-ISSUE-142` Finding C
decided it: the checker is not weakened, no ledger row is edited or deleted, and **the promotion
itself is the reconciliation** — the candidate is built from the checkout's migrations, so
`restored`, `candidate` and `production` all read parity clean and the orphan row is gone at the
swap. What this issue does change for ISSUE-139 is that the candidate will now be built *with* the
grant: before this merge, `privileges.sql` lacked the DELETE, so a promotion would have silently
revoked a grant `afldb_dev` depends on.

Three things could clear the orphan row, and **none is taken here**: the promotion (decided,
above); an operator-approved direct ledger `DELETE`, which the brief for this work forbids; or a
tracked forward reconciliation migration carrying a guarded delete of that one row (a no-op on
`afldb_test` and production, where it never existed). The third is not defined anywhere in the
repository today and would be a new, operator-approved mechanism, not an improvisation.

### Resolution (2026-09-13)

**Root cause:** `beta_access_codes` had a revoke path but no delete path, no `afldb_auth` DELETE
grant, and `page.tsx` selected every code with no state filter, so retired keys — spent keys
worst of all, since they could be neither revoked nor deleted — accumulated permanently in the
admin UI with no disposal route.

**Fix:** migration `091_access_code_delete.sql` grants `afldb_auth` DELETE on `beta_access_codes`;
`tools/maintenance/privileges.sql` mirrors the grant so the subtractive reconciler preserves it;
`deleteRetiredAccessCode` carries the "revoked or spent, never merely expired or partly used"
eligibility predicate in its `WHERE` clause (proven a strict subset of "not redeemable," §5 above);
`deleteAccessCode` runs the delete and its `access.code_deleted` audit inside one transaction via
`auditInTransaction`; `DeleteCodeButton` offers Delete only for a revoked-or-spent row, behind an
in-row confirmation naming the key and its state.

**Validation:**

- **DEV Playwright browser gate — PASS.** Active code: Revoke available, Delete not available.
  Revoked code: Delete available. Delete confirmation identifies the key and its state. A revoked
  code deletes successfully and remains gone after reload. A one-use spent code exposes Delete
  directly with no revoke first, deletes successfully, and remains gone after reload. Unlimited
  codes are correctly never treated as spent. No console/runtime errors.
- **Focused DB/test validation — PASS.** `afldb_test` confirmed as target; `npm run db:migrate:test`
  PASS with migration `091` confirmed applied; `tests/integration/access-codes.test.ts` 8/8 PASS;
  the ISSUE-117-specific `afldb_auth` DELETE-grant assertion in `tests/integration/privileges.test.ts`
  PASS.
- **PROD proof (read-only).** `091_access_code_delete.sql` applied on PROD at
  `2026-09-06 10:08:25.329637+10`; `has_table_privilege('afldb_auth', 'beta_access_codes',
  'DELETE')` returns `t` on PROD.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-142 — The promotion checker refuses every real database on `player_match_period_stats`, and the contract reinstates id-keyed ledgers across a lineage change

- **Status:** **Resolved 2026-09-12** — see *Resolution (2026-09-12)* at the foot of this entry. As found and implemented on 2026-09-06 (retained): found during `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` Phase 4C preflight (read-only; no database was written); **implemented 2026-09-06** — (A) decided in the contract, (B) a fail-closed lineage gate with an evidenced per-row remap, (C) an authoritative repository conclusion with no code change. The "five files changed in the `main` working tree, uncommitted" state recorded below is **SUPERSEDED**: the work was committed and merged as `12a3995`, and every validation item it lists has since been executed and recorded elsewhere in this ledger.
- **Severity:** High — (A) blocks `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` at the first checker phase and `AFLDB-ISSUE-137` path (a) on production; (B) would silently misattribute 92 of 94 human link decisions if a DEV promotion followed the contract as written.
- **Area:** Operations / Database tooling / Data integrity
- **Found:** 2026-09-06
- **Resolved:** 2026-09-12
- **Related:** `AFLDB-ISSUE-125` (the contract), `AFLDB-ISSUE-141` (the previous contract gap, same shape as (A)), `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` (blocked on this), `AFLDB-ISSUE-137` (path (a) meets (A)), `AFLDB-ISSUE-138` (a third consumer that reads `import_writable_tables` as a complete classification).
- **Migration:** possibly, for (A) — see scope. None for (B).

### Problem

**(A) `public.player_match_period_stats` is in neither classification set.** Migration `062_player_match_period_stats.sql`
creates the table and never registers it in `afldb_meta.import_writable_tables`; no importer writes it
(`tools/current-season/repair-match-rekeys.ts` and two NL queries only read it); it holds 0 rows on `afldb_dev`
and on the rebuilt `afldb_test`; and `tools/db/promotion-inventory.ts` `publicContractTables()` does not name it.
The fail-closed classification gate therefore refuses **every** phase on **every** real database:

```text
[FAIL] Table classification (fail-closed)
       71 public tables: 44 import-writable (rebuilt data), 26 under the promotion contract
       UNCLASSIFIED public.player_match_period_stats: neither import-writable nor in tools/db/promotion-inventory.ts — decide its treatment before promoting
```

Reproduced 2026-09-06 with `--environment dev --phase source --database afldb_test` (ISSUE-118's rebuild;
every other gate PASS) and `--environment dev --phase pre-cutover --database afldb_dev`. The unit suite does
not catch it because `tests/db-promotion-check.test.ts` pins the table in `PINNED_FOOTBALL_TABLES` — i.e. it
assumes the migrations' non-contract tables are import-writable, while the live gate reads the registry. The
same deliberate-absence-read-as-decision shape as `AFLDB-ISSUE-141`.

**(B) The contract reinstates id-keyed ledgers unchanged, which is only correct when the candidate shares the
old database's id space.** On production it does (the 2026-09-02 cutover restored the rebuilt dump). `afldb_dev`
is the bootstrap lineage. Measured read-only 2026-09-06: `player_link_resolutions` (94 rows) references 36
distinct `player_id`s; 34 exist in the rebuilt lineage and all 34 name a different person (DEV 151 = Craig
Bradley vs rebuilt 151 = Alan McGowan; 318 Gary O'Donnell vs Alex Georgiou; 380 Doug Hawkins vs Alf Copsey).
`target_id` (award_winners 68, draft_picks 20, hall_of_fame 5, honour_team_members 1) and `data_edits.row_id`
(8 `matches`, 16 `players`) are in the same old space. The §7.4 nullable probe nulls only the 2 absent ids;
the contract's `compare: equal` rule then accepts 92 rows that point at the wrong humans. `data_overrides` is
not affected (keyed by `entity_key`). 33 of the 36 players carry an AFL Tables profile url on DEV, so an
evidenced remap exists in principle; name matching is not an option.

### Exact scope (proposed, bounded)

1. **(A)** Decide the table's treatment once, in the contract, with the reason recorded: either register it in
   `import_writable_tables` by a forward migration (it is football data by shape — rebuilt, currently empty,
   and nothing writes it), or add an explicit `rebuilt` / `reset` treatment to `publicContractTables()`. Then
   make the unit suite read the registry-equivalent instead of assuming it: the pinned football list must be
   checked against the migrations' `grant_import_write()` / registry inserts, so a future 062-shaped migration
   fails at test time as `AFLDB-ISSUE-141` intended.
2. **(B)** Decide, in `docs/production-promotion.md` §13 and the contract, how `player_link_resolutions` and
   `data_edits` are treated when the old database and the candidate do not share an id lineage: as historical
   audit ledgers of the replaced database (reinstate, name them in the `database.promoted` marker's recorded
   gaps, never read as live links), or through a tracked, evidenced remap keyed on the AFL Tables profile url
   with NULL where no identity exists. The `restored` phase should detect a lineage mismatch (sampled
   `player_id` → `players` name/dob disagreement) rather than report "0 missing".

Out of scope: any rebuild, candidate or swap; `AFLDB-ISSUE-140`; production.

### Decision A (2026-09-06) — `player_match_period_stats` is decided in the contract as `rebuilt` / `compare: zero`

Evidence, read from the repository only (no database was contacted in this session):

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| Created by migration `062`, which calls **neither** `afldb_meta.grant_import_write()` **nor** `grant_app_read()` | `src/db/migrations/062_player_match_period_stats.sql` (44 lines, whole file) |
| It is the **only** public table any migration creates that is in neither classification set | every post-045 `CREATE TABLE` in `src/db/migrations/` cross-checked against the six `grant_import_write('…')` call sites (045 seed, 053, 074, 086, 087, 089) and `publicContractTables()` |
| The registry it is missing from is seeded from the catalogue **as it stood at 045** minus a hand-typed operational list, so a table created later is registered only if its own migration says so | `045_import_write_is_fail_closed.sql:99-114`, `:119-147` |
| **No writer** anywhere in the tree | the only references are reads: `tools/current-season/repair-match-rekeys.ts:273` (a count), `src/db/queries/nl/player-career.ts:64,67` and `player-game.ts:128,180` |
| Those NL read paths are **unreachable**: the plan validator refuses a non-`FULL_MATCH` period split for any grain but `team_match` — *"Quarter-by-quarter player statistics are not currently available to rank."* | `src/search/nl/plan.ts:1051-1056` |
| No rebuild stage produces it (22 stages) | `tools/db/rebuild-test.ts` `planStages()` |
| 0 rows on `afldb_dev` and on the rebuilt `afldb_test` | `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` Phase 4C, read-only |

The table is therefore **unimplemented canonical schema, end to end**: nothing writes it, nothing can read
it through the app role, and the one query path that mentions it is refused upstream by design. The absence
from the registry was an **omission in migration 062**, not a decision — the `AFLDB-ISSUE-141` shape.

**Decided as a contract entry, not a forward migration.** `grant_import_write()` registers *and grants* in
one statement, so registering it would hand `afldb_import` UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE — restored at every
`privileges.sql` reconcile — to serve a writer that does not exist. That is a privilege broadening for no
behaviour, and it was ruled out. The entry is `treatment: 'rebuilt'` (the candidate's copy stands, exactly
as for a registry table: nothing to reinstate, nothing to reset) with `compare: 'zero'` as the tripwire —
the day a writer exists, the `candidate`/`production` comparison FAILS and the entry must be revisited, at
which point registering it import-writable, with the grant it then genuinely needs, is the right answer.
`category: 'football'` was added to the contract's `Category` union so the inventory report says what the
row is rather than mislabelling it operational.

**The test no longer assumes.** `tests/db-promotion-check.test.ts` now reconstructs
`afldb_meta.import_writable_tables` **from the migrations** — 045's catalogue seed (its exclusion ARRAY
parsed out of the migration, never re-typed) plus every later `grant_import_write()`, minus anything later
renamed or dropped — and runs the real `classifyPublicTables()` over it. `PINNED_FOOTBALL_TABLES` is
asserted **equal to that derived registry** instead of standing in for it. A future 062-shaped migration now
fails at test time, which is what the fail-closed gate was for.

### Decision B (2026-09-06) — lineage is proved from a stable external identity, and anything unevidenced refuses

**The defect, stated precisely.** `gateDanglingReferences` asks whether a referenced id still *exists* in
the candidate. Existence is not identity. When the candidate comes from a different id lineage almost every
id exists and denotes a different row, so `0 missing` is exactly the answer a silent misattribution
produces — the DEV measurement (94 rows, 36 distinct `player_id`, 34 present and **all 34 a different
person**) is that answer.

**Implemented.** The contract gained a `lineageRefs` vocabulary — columns holding ids of the *replaced*
database, each declaring the entity it points at and the stable identity rule for it — and the checker
gained a `restored`-phase gate that:

1. reads the **stable identity** of sampled ids on both databases. Players:
   `external_identities` with source `afltables`, `match_method = 'afltables_profile_url'`, status
   `unique`/`resolved` — the identity every `AFLDB-ISSUE-118` loader and the `AFLDB-ISSUE-113` artefact
   builder already resolve people through (`father_son.py:564`). Matches: `matches.match_key`, NOT NULL
   UNIQUE since migration `003` and the natural key migration `076`'s settle projections link on. The
   identity SQL selects `(id, identity)` and nothing else, in both directions, so a name match is not
   merely forbidden — it is unavailable;
2. PASSES, generating nothing, when every comparable sample agrees (a production promotion: the candidate
   is a rebuild of the same lineage). **Nothing comparable counts as changed**, so a missing identity layer
   can never read as "safe to reinstate by id";
3. otherwise resolves every declared column per row, old id → identity → new id, mapping an id **only**
   when exactly one identity is read for it in the replaced database and exactly one candidate row carries
   that same identity string. `no_identity_in_replaced`, `ambiguous_in_replaced`,
   `identity_absent_in_candidate`, `ambiguous_in_candidate` and `no_stable_identity_rule` each **REFUSE**,
   naming the id, the reason and the ledger rows that carry it. Merges (two old rows onto one candidate
   row — an `AFLDB-ISSUE-136` fold) are surfaced explicitly rather than hidden.

**The remap keys, per column.**

| Column | Key | Remappable? |
|---|---|---|
| `player_link_resolutions.player_id` | AFL Tables profile url | Yes, where the identity exists on both sides. It **cannot** be nulled instead: `plr_action_player_ck` requires a player whenever `action = 'linked'`, so a reinstated decision always asserts a person. |
| `player_link_resolutions.target_id` (`target_table` ∈ 7 honours tables) | **none — declared `'none'`** | **No.** The seven tables are import-writable, the rebuild assigns their ids, and the repository carries no external key for one of their rows. Remapping `player_id` alone is explicitly not an answer: it yields a row that looks resolved, names the right person and points at the wrong honours row. |
| `data_edits.row_id` where `table_name = 'players'` | AFL Tables profile url | Yes. |
| `data_edits.row_id` where `table_name = 'matches'` | `matches.match_key` | Yes in principle. Current-season rows are the normal exception: the rebuild carries seasons to the accepted baseline, so those matches do not exist until the post-promotion settle re-acquires the season — the remap for them is applied after the settle, stated in the record. |

**The artefact.** `--lineage-remap-out <file>` (refused outside `--phase restored`) writes the result as
SQL: one `UPDATE` per **row**, guarded by the value it was proved against so re-running is a no-op, each
preceded by its evidence comment `old id -> identity -> new id`; `-- UNRESOLVED` lines naming the reason and
the rows for everything unevidenced; `-- MERGE` lines; and a trailing verification query that must return
zero rows — the proof that no row changed semantic owner. One column per statement; no INSERT, DELETE,
TRUNCATE or ALTER anywhere, so the append-only ledgers and every audit field are untouched. A table with
more than 5,000 lineage-bound rows refuses instead: a per-row remap nobody can read by hand is not evidence.

**The refusal that remains, deliberately.** Because `target_id` has no stable identity, a DEV promotion
**will** be refused by this gate. That is the correct fail-closed outcome and it is a decided refusal with a
path: `docs/production-promotion.md` §7.4c records the two supportable answers — reinstate the ledger as a
**historical** audit of the replaced database, stating that its links are not live; or **do not reinstate
it** into the candidate and keep it as a recorded gap, the `promotion_decisions` treatment, on the reasoning
that a decision cannot outlive the row it is about. Rows are never dropped: they survive in the pre-cutover
dump and the kept pre-rebuild database either way. `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` Phase 4E picks one and records it, the
same way §7.4b was settled.

### Finding C (2026-09-06) — migration `079_access_code_delete.sql`: authoritative repository state

Established from tracked records and on-disk refs; **no Git command was run** and no ledger row was touched.

* `main` owns `src/db/migrations/079_nl_search_log_head_to_head_grain.sql`. It is applied everywhere,
  production included (`AFLDB-ISSUE-122` closeout: production is at `083` with 0 pending).
* `079_access_code_delete.sql` **exists in no checkout on this machine** — not in `D:\dev\afldb`, not in any
  of the 21 sibling worktrees (checked by filename). The `afldb-issue-116` worktree is on
  `claude/issue-116-query-builder`, an unrelated branch, and its migrations directory has no such file.
* The file is committed only on the branch `claude/issue-116`, whose ref on disk
  (`.git/refs/heads/claude/issue-116`) is `2344ab552da3d3167701a7b5277f5b82897ae74d` — byte-identical to the
  `2344ab5` recorded in `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-119.md` §480 on 2026-09-01, so the branch has not moved

* `IssuesIndex.md`'s 2026-09-02 allocation warning already requires that branch to *renumber* before it

**Conclusion — outcome (3), with (2) as its precondition.** DEV was mutated ahead of `main` by an unmerged
branch, and the migration cannot be merged as numbered. So:

* nothing is merged, renumbered, reversed or deleted under this issue — that is `AFLDB-ISSUE-117`'s work on
  its own branch, and it must claim the next free number (**`091`** as `main` stands) after the usual live
  branch-tip scan;
* the checker is **not** weakened: `UNKNOWN 079_access_code_delete.sql` at `--phase pre-cutover` on
  `afldb_dev` is a truthful report that the live database is ahead of every tracked checkout by a migration
  no checkout can reproduce. No flag, no environment special case, no downgrade to WARN;
* **the promotion is the reconciliation.** The candidate is built from this checkout's migrations, so
  `restored`, `candidate` and `production` all read parity clean and the orphan row is gone at the swap.
  The `pre-cutover` phase still writes its snapshot (the checker writes it after the gates, whatever their
  verdicts), which is what the later phases compare against. `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` records the refusal and its
  reason in the promotion record and continues — a recorded, understood condition, not a bypass.

This is documented for the operator in `docs/production-promotion.md` §13.

### Resolution (2026-09-12)

**Status:** Resolved. Closed on repository evidence alone. This closure ran no test, no build, no
query and no deployment command; every figure below is quoted from evidence already recorded in
this ledger by the sessions that produced it.

**Root cause.** Two independent gaps in the promotion contract, both of the `AFLDB-ISSUE-141`
shape — a deliberate absence read as a decision. **(A)** Migration
`062_player_match_period_stats.sql` created `public.player_match_period_stats` and registered it in
neither `afldb_meta.import_writable_tables` nor `publicContractTables()`, so the fail-closed
classification gate refused **every** phase on **every** real database; the unit suite could not
catch it because it pinned the table in `PINNED_FOOTBALL_TABLES` instead of reading the registry.
**(B)** The contract reinstated id-keyed ledgers unchanged, which is correct only when the
candidate shares the old database’s id space — on the `afldb_dev` bootstrap lineage the
`compare: equal` rule would have accepted 92 of 94 `player_link_resolutions` rows pointing at
different people. **(C)** was not a defect but an authoritative repository conclusion about
`079_access_code_delete.sql`.

**Fix.** (A) `player_match_period_stats` is decided **in the contract** as `rebuilt` /
`compare: zero`, deliberately NOT registered import-writable (`grant_import_write()` would hand
`afldb_import` UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE for a writer that does not exist), and
`tests/db-promotion-check.test.ts` now derives the registry from the migrations and runs the real
classifier, so a future 062-shaped migration fails at test time as `AFLDB-ISSUE-141` intended.
(B) A `restored`-phase lineage gate proves **identity** rather than existence — AFL Tables profile
url for players, `matches.match_key` for matches — passing silently on a same-lineage (production)
promotion and refusing anything unevidenced, with `--lineage-remap-out` writing the evidenced
per-row remap; `player_link_resolutions.target_id` is declared identity `none`. (C) recorded, no
code change. Files: `tools/db/promotion-inventory.ts`, `tools/db/promotion-check.ts`,
`tests/db-promotion-check.test.ts`, `docs/production-promotion.md`, plus the ledgers.

**Resolving commit.** `12a3995` — "Resolve AFLDB ISSUE-142 promotion lineage checks" — on `main`
(7 files, +1,519 / -28). The "uncommitted in the `main` working tree" text above is therefore
historical, not current.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-143 — The promotion contract documents two treatments for lineage-unresolvable ledger rows, but the checker and plan can execute neither

- **Status:** **Resolved 2026-09-06** — the historical-only / recorded-gap disposition is implemented, DB-free validated (73/73), and re-validated read-only against the live DEV databases. Found 2026-09-06 during `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` Phase 4C′.
- **Severity:** High — a DEV promotion (the only real lineage change the contract has met) can never pass `--phase restored`, so `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` Phase 4E cannot start. Production is unaffected: its candidate shares its lineage and the gate PASSES silently (`AFLDB-ISSUE-142` B).
- **Area:** Operations / Database tooling / Data integrity
- **Found:** 2026-09-06
- **Resolved:** 2026-09-06
- **Related:** `AFLDB-ISSUE-142` (the gate and the §7.4c text this completes), `AFLDB-ISSUE-141` (same shape: documented semantics ahead of the executable path), `AFLDB-ISSUE-125` (the contract), `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` (blocked on this at Phase 4E; unblocked by this resolution).
- **Migration:** none — none was needed. No schema, no `privileges.sql` and no grant change.

### Problem

`docs/production-promotion.md` §7.4c and the contract's own remediation strings (`tools/db/promotion-inventory.ts`,
`player_link_resolutions.target_id` and `data_edits.row_id`) name exactly two supportable answers for a lineage-bound
row that cannot be evidenced — **(1)** reinstate the table as a historical, not-live audit ledger of the replaced
database, stated in the promotion record and the `database.promoted` marker, or **(2)** do not reinstate it and keep it
as a recorded gap (the `promotion_decisions` treatment) — and one deferred case, a `data_edits` row about a
current-season match, to be remapped after the post-promotion settle. None of the three has an executable path:

* `gateLineageIdentity` (`tools/db/promotion-check.ts`) reports **FAIL** whenever `unresolvedTotal > 0`, and identity
  `none` makes every `player_link_resolutions.target_id` row unresolved by construction (`resolveLineageRemap`,
  `tools/db/promotion-inventory.ts:646`, reason `no_stable_identity_rule`). So answer (1) still refuses.
* The generated plan (`--plan`) reinstates every `treatment: 'reinstate'` table and has no exclusion; the gate reads the
  lineage-bound rows from the **old** database, so omitting a `pg_restore` line by hand changes the verdict not at all;
  and `--phase candidate --compare` applies `compare: 'equal'` to both tables, so answer (2) would refuse there instead.
* The deferred current-season case is documented as normal, yet it is counted as unresolved and FAILs `restored`.

Measured read-only on `afldb_dev` against the rebuilt `afldb_test` (2026-09-06, `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` Phase 4C′):
`player_link_resolutions.target_id` 94 of 94 unresolved by rule; `player_link_resolutions.player_id` 33 of 36 ids
evidenced, 3 without any identity (1347, 13362, 13363); `data_edits.row_id` `players` 0 of 7 ids evidenced (six
1897–1900 players among DEV's 891 identity-less rows, plus one 2026 debutant); `data_edits.row_id` `matches` 8 of 8
rows unresolvable now (ids 17041 and 17059 were created and then deleted on DEV itself and can never resolve; 17051 is
a 2026 match that resolves by `match_key` only after the season is re-acquired).

### Exact scope (proposed, bounded)

A declared, explicit, audit-marked **lineage disposition** per reinstated table, chosen by the operator and never
defaulted: `historical` (reinstate; the gate reports the declared-unresolvable rows as an accepted WARN with every id
listed; the marker and the promotion record say the links are not live) or `gap` (the plan omits the table's reinstate
line, the `candidate` compare expects zero, the marker records the gap), plus a `deferred` outcome for current-season
`data_edits` match rows that the remap file carries as commented statements to run after the settle. Fail-closed by
default (no disposition → today's refusal), refused under `--environment prod` unless the same evidence applies there,
covered in `tests/db-promotion-check.test.ts`, documented in §7.4c and §13. Do not weaken the identity rules, do not
match by name, do not add a stable identity for honours rows by inference. Design at Fable High / Opus High on a fresh
worktree; `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` records the operator's D1/D2 choices that this issue must honour.

### Operator decisions honoured (recorded by `AFLDB-ISSUE-139`, 2026-09-06)

* **D0** — reuse the current `afldb_test` as the canonical source; no rebuild. Nothing in this issue touches it.
* **D1** — `player_link_resolutions`: §7.4c **option 2**. Not reinstated into live canonical state; preserved as
  historical evidence in the mandatory dump and the renamed pre-rebuild database. No `target_id` mapping by name, by
  integer-id existence or by guessed honours equivalence.
* **D2** — `data_edits`: the same historical-only / recorded-gap treatment. No stale bootstrap id is forced into the
  rebuilt lineage, and the single current-season row that could resolve after the post-swap settle is part of the same
  gap rather than a pending remap, so it cannot weaken the pre-swap gate.
* **D3** — this issue: an explicit, fail-closed contract/tooling mechanism that can represent that disposition.

### Resolution — 2026-09-06

**Root cause.** §7.4c's two answers existed only as prose. `gateLineageIdentity` reported `FAIL` whenever
`unresolvedTotal > 0`; `reinstatedPublicTables()` had no exclusion, so the generated plan reinstated every `reinstate`
table; and `compare: 'equal'` would then have refused the omission from the other side. Both answers were therefore
unreachable, and the deferred current-season `data_edits` case was counted as a plain refusal.

**The fix — a contract declaration, not a flag.** A `TableTreatment` may now carry a `historicalOnly` entry
(`tools/db/promotion-inventory.ts`) naming the `environments` it applies to, **every** lineage-bound column of that
table, the deciding issue, a one-line `summary` and the full `reason`. One declaration drives four things at once, so
the gate, the plan and the comparison cannot disagree:

1. `reinstatedPublicTables(environment)` drops the table, so `reinstatePlan()` emits no `pg_restore --table=` line and
   `resyncIdentitySql(environment)` no sequence — and the plan prints an `INTENTIONALLY NOT REINSTATED` block naming
   the table, the withheld columns, the reason, the dump the rows are in and the retained pre-rebuild database, before
   the restore lines it is missing from;
2. the table is **still truncated** (`truncatedPublicTables()` is unchanged), so the candidate holds none of the
   rebuilt copy either and `effectiveCompare()` expects `zero` instead of `equal` at `--phase candidate`;
3. `--phase restored` reports the column as `hist` with its row count, distinct ids, evidenced/unresolved split and
   per-id reasons, prints the decision in full, and `lineageRemapSql()` writes a `-- HISTORICAL-ONLY` evidence block
   and **no statement** for it;
4. `auditMarkerSql()` writes a `historical_only` array plus one recorded-gap sentence per table into
   `database.promoted`, so the promoted database records what it was not given.

**Fail-closed everywhere else, by construction.** Acceptance is decided per `(table, column, environment)` by the pure
`judgeLineage()`, never by a verdict-level relaxation: another table, another column of the *same* table, or the same
table under an environment the declaration does not list all still refuse exactly as before. There is no command-line
override (`--allow-unresolved`/`--ignore-lineage`/`--force` do not exist and a test asserts they never appear).
`assertContractCoherent()` runs before the checker's first query and refuses a declaration that names only some of its
table's lineage-bound columns, sits on a table that is not `reinstate`, declares no environment or an unknown one, has
an empty `decidedBy`/`summary`/`reason`, or that `reinstatedPublicTables()` would still reinstate — condition (2) of
the scope, proved rather than promised. Adding a new lineage-bound column to a declared table re-opens the decision
instead of inheriting it. The dangling-reference gate reports `info` for a withheld table's own reference (the rows are
never created, so it cannot dangle) and is untouched for every other table; migration parity, classification, fixture
identity, super-admin and privilege gates are untouched.

**What was deliberately NOT built.** §7.4c answer (1) — reinstate the table as a not-live historical ledger — has no
executable path and still refuses. It would mean writing ids that denote different rows into the promoted database and
trusting a note to say so, and both D1 and D2 chose answer (2). If it is ever wanted it is a new decision, not a flag
on this one. No `deferred` third outcome was built either: under D2 the current-season `data_edits` row is part of the
gap, so there is nothing pending to carry.

**Declared today** — `--environment dev` only; production declares nothing:

| Table | Columns | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| `player_link_resolutions` | `player_id`, `target_id` | `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` D1. `target_id`'s seven honours tables carry no external key, so not one row can be evidenced; remapping `player_id` alone is explicitly not an answer. |
| `data_edits` | `row_id` | `AFLDB-ISSUE-139` D2. Every lineage-bound row is in the bootstrap id space; two of its matches were created and then deleted on `afldb_dev` itself. |

One consequence recorded in `docs/production-promotion.md` §7.4d for the DEV promotion record:
`player_link_match_candidates` is regenerated from rebuilt players **plus reinstated resolutions**, so with none
reinstated the admin link queue re-surfaces the previously-decided suggestions for a fresh decision against the new
lineage. That is the honest outcome of a lineage change, not a defect.

### Validation — 2026-09-06

DB-free, on this worktree (`D:\dev\afldb-issue-143`, branch `claude/issue-143`):

* `npx vitest run tests/db-promotion-check.test.ts` — **73 passed / 73**, 0 failures (was 64; 9 added, 2 amended).
  The added block proves: the real contract is coherent and declares nothing for `prod`; a partial, misplaced,

  **accepted under `dev` and refused under `prod`**; another table, another column of a declared table, and a table
  outside the contract all still refuse; `prod` is byte-identical across `reinstatedPublicTables`, `reinstatePlan`,
  `resyncIdentitySql` and `auditMarkerSql`, and the withheld tables are still truncated; the DEV plan carries the
  omission block and generates **no** `--table=`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE` for either table; the DEV marker
  records the gap and no longer claims them as reinstated; the remap file writes the `-- HISTORICAL-ONLY` block for a
  withheld column while an undeclared column **still takes the ISSUE-142 remap path** (guarded `UPDATE` plus its

  The two amended tests are the ISSUE-141/142 ones whose premise moved: the remap test now runs under `prod` (where no

* `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean, repo-wide.

Not run, and not runnable here: `--phase restored`, `candidate` and `production` need a candidate database that only

### Follow-up

### Scope

A new AFL-only public `/clubs/compare` surface with three layers: (1) selected-season comparison
(record, ladder, scoring, team metrics with runtime coverage, player leaders, Brownlow), (2) complete
head-to-head history (meetings, records, streaks, venues, leaders, match-scoped Brownlow), and
(3) connected club history (players who represented both organisations, direction, intervening clubs,
club-attributed Brownlow history).

The binding contract is `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-144.md` (V1.7). Its non-negotiable requirement is that the
implementation is **season-generic**: no hard-coded year, supported-season list, historical cutoff,
metric-year branch or club mapping. Seasons come from canonical `seasons` rows, the default is the
maximum canonical season, and provisionality/coverage are read from `seasons.status` /
`seasons.data_through_date` and `stat_availability.coverage` at request time.

Execution is one runbook stage per session (Stage 0 through Stage 10), each persisting its own
handoff into `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-144.md`.

### Stage 0 evidence (2026-09-06)

Schema semantics were re-verified against the migrations in this worktree and **agree with the
runbook on every load-bearing point**:

* `afldb_identity_for_season(p_organization_id, p_season)` exists (`017_club_organizations.sql:141`),
  `STABLE PARALLEL SAFE`, and deliberately prefers the narrower later-starting identity (Kangaroos
  inside North Melbourne's span).
* `clubs.organization_id` (NOT NULL) is the lineage key; `clubs.current_identity_id` is retained for
  compatibility only. `club_organization_relations` carries `merged_into` / `relocated_to` / `folded`
  as context — its own comment records that a merger does not transfer history.
* `seasons.status` (`season_status` = `in_progress` | `complete`), `data_through_date`,
  `source_built_at`, `last_loaded_round` and `completed_at` all exist (`015_brownlow_grain_and_coverage.sql:53`);
  `is_complete` is now a generated mirror of `status`.
* `coverage_status` = `complete` | `partial` | `not_collected` | `not_applicable` | `pending`
  (`015_…:38`) and `stat_availability.coverage` (`015_…:161`) carry the runtime metric coverage the
  runbook requires, keyed per `(stat_key, season)`. `016_brownlow_grain_availability.sql` populates
  `brownlow_season_total`, `brownlow_round_votes` and `brownlow_match_votes` **computed from loaded
  data, not hardcoded**, and defines a fully polled match as exactly 3+2+1 = 6 votes over
  home-and-away matches — the same rule the runbook's H2H Brownlow coverage disclosure needs.
* `brownlow_season_votes.club_id` is **nullable** (`005_brownlow_awards.sql:15`) with `is_winner` and
  `is_ineligible`; `player_season_stats` carries `primary_club_id` + `club_count` (`015_…:99`); the
  club-grain table is `player_club_season_stats` (renamed from `player_season_stats` by `015_…:83`)
  and carries no award totals by design. `player_career_stats.brownlow_votes` is summed from
  `brownlow_season_votes` and its comment records that summing `player_match_stats.brownlow_votes`
  instead yields 46,979 against the authoritative 79,113 — the runbook's prohibition is materially
  correct.
* `matches` has `season`, `round_type`, `round_number`, `match_date`, `venue_id` (nullable) plus
  `venue_raw` (NOT NULL), `home_club_id` / `away_club_id`, `home_score` / `away_score`, `result`,
  `winner_club_id` (NULL on a draw) and `margin`; `is_finals_series` is added by
  `085_matches_is_finals_series.sql` as the single finals-series definition.
* `club_seasons` carries `played`, `wins`, `draws`, `losses`, `points_for`, `points_against`,
  `premiership_points`, `percentage`, `ladder_rank` and `finals_played`, unique on `(season, club_id)`.
* `player_clubs` is the derived historical-identity stint table with `games`, `goals`, `first_season`,
  `last_season`, `first_match_id` and `last_match_id`.
* `player_match_stats` carries `marks_inside_50` and `brownlow_votes` (constrained 0-3).

1. **Heading hierarchy — a real defect.** The static review above ("confirmed every top-level section

   "Leads, comebacks and turnarounds" (`ClubComparisonRivalryRecords.tsx`, under `<h3>Period

   under `<h3>Connected players</h3>` and `<h3>Player averages in this rivalry</h3>` respectively).
   Root cause: `CollapsiblePanel` (`src/components/CollapsiblePanel.tsx`) hardcoded `<h2
   className="table-details-title">` unconditionally. Fixed with an optional `headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4`
   prop (default `2`, so every other call site across the site — including this surface's own
   Venues/Players/Brownlow/Match history top-level panels — is unchanged), threaded through
   `CollapsibleTable`, with `headingLevel={4}` passed at the three nested call sites. No CSS/visual
   change — `table-details-title` styles the class, not the tag.
2. **Era canonical assertion — a test-only race, not a canonical-implementation defect.** Per
   instruction, `canonicalClubComparePath`/`resolveClubComparisonMetadata` were NOT changed first: the
   dedicated `a club comparison canonicalises to its ordered pair alone` SEO test (full `page.goto`
   loads) already proves era/matchType/page are correctly dropped from the canonical, and it still
   passes. The actual cause is that `/clubs/compare` is `force-dynamic` with an async
   `generateMetadata`, so under Next's streaming metadata (resolved metadata tags are appended once
   `generateMetadata` resolves — see `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/
   generate-metadata.md`, "Streaming metadata") the canonical `<link>` can still be in flight for a
   moment after a client-side era-chip `<Link>` navigation, even though body content has already
   rendered; the SEO test never hits this because a full `page.goto` waits for `load`. Fixed by
   changing the one-shot `getAttribute` read in `tests/e2e/journeys.spec.ts` to a retrying
   `expect.poll`.

**FR-5 — a latent Playwright flake found during FR-5 validation (2026-09-07), NOT an ISSUE-144
application regression.** The operator reported the comparison-focused suite functionally green except
for one non-deterministic test, `the era explorer narrows rivalry records and match history, resets
pagination, and is shareable`, failing intermittently at the same canonical-`<link>` assertion the
previous FR-4 pass hardened (empty href/search instead of `?club1=carlton&club2=collingwood`), moving
between projects across repeated runs — non-determinism tied to contention across parallel
workers/projects, not a stable per-project defect (isolated and light `repeat-each` runs passed
reliably; the heavier multi-test comparison gate occasionally starved it on either project).

Root cause: the prior fix's `expect.poll` wrapped a locator action
(`page.locator('link[rel="canonical"]').first().getAttribute('href')`), and a locator action auto-waits
on its target using the page's own default action timeout — a single slow tick under worker contention
(this route's `generateMetadata` awaits a real DB round trip) can consume the entire outer poll budget
in one attempt, leaving no further retries. Fixed by replacing it with
`expect(locator).toHaveAttribute('href', /\/clubs\/compare\?club1=carlton&club2=collingwood$/, {
timeout: 10_000 })` — a structural, web-first Playwright assertion that re-resolves the locator and
re-reads `href` on its own short internal polling cadence, immune to any single slow query, with the
same exact target string (no weaker) and only a local per-assertion timeout override (no global
Playwright config touched). `tests/e2e/journeys.spec.ts` is the only file changed; no application code
was touched. The behavioural contract this test proves is unchanged: era selection still produces the
shareable `era=1990` URL with `page` dropped, the pair's canonical still asserts exactly
`?club1=carlton&club2=collingwood`, and clearing the era via "All time" still drops `era=` from the URL.

    E. npx playwright test tests/e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "clubs → compare clubs|a club page seeds a comparison|a rivalry renders every section|reversing the pair reverses|the match filter and the history page|explorer narrows rivalry records|era and match type combine|every invalid comparison state|comparison stays inside the viewport|comparison controls are labelled"

2026`). **Since MERGED into `main` as `71f0563` (PR #3) and deployed to DEV; production is untouched.** (As written 2026-09-07: "Not deployed to DEV or production — that is the operator’s decision.") The exact Git handoff

### Resolution (2026-09-13)

Both the core Club vs Club comparison (`2102b51`, PR #2) and the Club Rivalry Explorer follow-up

236.7 ms; threshold < 1,500 ms) all PASS.

A real defect surfaced during final acceptance, after the above was already merged: client-side
soft navigation could desynchronise page metadata from the visible comparison — an era-chip link
could leave the wrong `<title>`/`og:title` in place, and the Swap control could regress the
canonical URL to the bare `/clubs/compare`. Hard navigation was unaffected. Root cause: Next.js
client-router prefetch/cache interaction on the sibling era-chip/Swap/Reset links racing this
route's streaming `generateMetadata`.

**Fix (`b43eb4a`):** `prefetch={false}` on Swap, Reset, and every era-chip link, plus new
soft-navigation metadata regression assertions. No application behaviour beyond the metadata
timing changed; no migration.

  Adelaide/Brisbane Lions Swap soft navigation (repeated twice), both via in-page clicks (no

  canonical remained ordered-pair-only and never regressed to bare `/clubs/compare`; canonical
  continued to exclude era/matchType/page; 0 console errors, 0 console warnings. Three unrelated
  stale `_rsc` prefetch requests for other (home/match) links were cancelled with
  `net::ERR_ABORTED` during navigation — pre-existing Next.js prefetch cancellation noise, not an

from the Open Issues table and `IssuesIndex.md`.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-146 — `code_test_db` as a second explicitly supported disposable full-rebuild target

- **Status:** **RESOLVED — 2026-09-07.** Implemented on `claude/issue-146` and merged to `main`
  (`62e9536`). The first real `code_test_db` rebuild has since been rehearsed to completion — see
  "Rehearsal evidence" below — exposing and fixing one bounded host-bootstrap gap
  (`tools/maintenance/00_install_postgres.sh` never provisioned `code_test_db`).
- **Severity / Area:** Medium / Rebuild tooling — `tools/db/rebuild-test.ts`, migration and privilege
  runners, deployment docs.
- **Reported:** 2026-09-07 (operator request).

### Problem

The canonical rebuild runner (`npm run db:test:rebuild`, AFLDB-ISSUE-093 §10) accepted exactly one
destructive target, `afldb_test`, resolved solely from `AFLDB_TEST_DATABASE_URL` and gated by a
`_test`-suffix rule plus a single-name check. Rehearsing a complete clean rebuild therefore meant
destroying `afldb_test` itself — the database integration tests and the promotion checker depend
on — with no way to prove the real rebuild against a throwaway database. The
MIGRATIONS and PRIVILEGES stages were also hard-bound to `db:migrate:test` /
`db:privileges:test`, which read `AFLDB_TEST_DATABASE_URL` regardless of what the runner had
resolved, so a second target could not be added without touching those runners too.

### Contract (as implemented)

- **Allowlist.** `REBUILD_TARGETS` in `tools/db/rebuild-test.ts` lists exactly `afldb_test`
  (normal test/integration rebuild) and `code_test_db` (disposable full-rebuild rehearsal). The
  former `_test`-suffix rule is subsumed by the allowlist: `random_test` is refused exactly as
  `afldb_scratch` is. `afldb_dev` / `afldb_prod` are still refused by name, anything containing
  `prod` still looks like production, and any `*pre_rebuild*` name is still read-only.
- **Selection.** `--target <database>`; omitted means `afldb_test` (`DEFAULT_TARGET`), so existing
  invocations are unchanged. A bare `--target` is refused rather than falling through to the
  default. The selected name is validated BEFORE any environment variable is read.
- **DSNs.** Each target has its own pair and reads only that pair: `AFLDB_TEST_DATABASE_URL` /
  `AFLDB_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL` for `afldb_test`; `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` /
  `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL` for `code_test_db`. A missing variable is a refusal, never
  a fallback to the other target's DSN. The database named inside the DSN must equal the selected
  target (the target is never inferred from a DSN); the import DSN must name the same database as
  the owner DSN; `--allow-owner-import-dsn` remains the only, explicit, owner substitution.
- **Acknowledgement.** `--acknowledge-destroy` must equal the selected database exactly
  (`assertDestructiveAcknowledgement` is unchanged; it now simply sees the selected target).
- **Stage graph.** `planStages()` is unchanged in shape: the same 22 stage ids, kinds and argv for
  both targets. Only the MIGRATIONS and PRIVILEGES stages differ, binding to the target's own
  package scripts (`db:migrate:code-test` with `AFLDB_MIGRATE_TARGET=code-test`, and
  `db:privileges:code-test`). `tools/db/migrate.ts` and `tools/db/privileges.ts` map the new
  `code-test` target to `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`; in `migrate.ts`, `code-test` joins `test`
  in `DISPOSABLE_TARGETS` (exempt from the shared-ledger cross-worktree guard because it is wiped
  and rebuilt from nothing), and every other rule — filename-collision check, checksum drift refusal,
  the whole tracked set from `001` to the current terminal migration with no hard-coded count — is
  untouched. `--allow-branch-local` is still DEV-only.
- **Leakage.** No refusal or banner prints a DSN, host or credential — database and variable names
  only. `npm run db:test:prove-reset` stays pinned to `afldb_test` through its own
  `PROOF_EXPECTED_DATABASE`.

### Files changed

Original implementation: `tools/db/rebuild-test.ts`, `tools/db/migrate.ts`,
`tools/db/privileges.ts`, `package.json` (`db:migrate:code-test`, `db:privileges:code-test`),
`.env.example` (commented `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_*` lines), `docs/deployment.md` §6a,
`tests/db-test-rebuild.test.ts`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `issues.md`, `IssuesIndex.md`.

Bounded bootstrap follow-up (this worktree, 2026-09-07): `tools/maintenance/00_install_postgres.sh`
(create + provision `code_test_db` alongside `afldb_dev`/`afldb_test`), `docs/deployment.md` §6a
(provisioning note), `CHANGELOG.md`, `issues.md`, `IssuesIndex.md`.

### Validation (2026-09-07, workstation, no database contact)

- `npx vitest run tests/db-test-rebuild.test.ts` — **285 / 285 PASS** (271 pre-existing + the new
  `explicit --target and the code_test_db rehearsal (AFLDB-ISSUE-146)` block: default unchanged,
  explicit `afldb_test` ≡ default, `code_test_db` via its own DSNs, exact acknowledgement both ways,
  identical 22-stage graph for both targets with only the bound scripts differing, by-name refusals
  for `afldb_dev` / `afldb_prod` / `anything-prod` / `random_test` / `*pre_rebuild*` before any DSN is
  read, wrong-database and invalid code-test DSNs, missing code-test DSNs without borrowing the test
  ones, no target inference from a DSN, bare `--target` refused, and no DSN/host/credential in any
  refusal). Three pre-existing prove-reset identity cases were updated for the allowlist wording and
  one new case proves the proof still refuses `code_test_db`.
- `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`) — PASS.
- `npx eslint tools/db/rebuild-test.ts tools/db/migrate.ts tools/db/privileges.ts
  tests/db-test-rebuild.test.ts` — 8 errors / 2 warnings, **all pre-existing on `main`** (identical
  findings at the pre-shift line numbers when linting `git show main:<file>` through
  `--stdin-filename`; none inside an ISSUE-146 hunk). Not fixed: out of scope.
- `git diff --check` — clean; no conflict markers; every touched file is CRLF-only UTF-8 without BOM.
- CLI smoke through `tsx tools/db/rebuild-test.ts` with fake DSNs (no `.env` in the worktree, no
  server): `--target afldb_dev` refused by name with no environment at all; bare `--target` refused;
  `--target random_test` refused as unlisted; default `--plan` with only `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_*` set
  refused (`AFLDB_TEST_DATABASE_URL is not set`, no borrowing); `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` naming
  `afldb_test` refused as a target mismatch; `--target code_test_db --plan` printed the 22-stage
  graph binding `npm run db:migrate:code-test` / `db:privileges:code-test`, and the default `--plan`
  still binds `db:migrate:test` / `db:privileges:test`. No output contained the fake password.
- **No database was contacted, migrated, reset or created.** `afldb_test`, `afldb_dev`, the retained
  `afldb_dev_pre_rebuild_20260906-112500`, production and `code_test_db` are all untouched; no SSH,
  deploy, restart, commit, push or merge.

### Rehearsal evidence (2026-09-07, operator-run, `code_test_db` on the rehearsal host)

The operator created `code_test_db`, set the two `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_*` variables and ran the first
real rehearsal:

```
npm run db:test:rebuild -- --target code_test_db --acknowledge-destroy code_test_db
```

- Source prechecks (fail-closed, pre-destruction) initially refused on missing source artefacts;
  after the operator restored them, all prechecks passed.
- The first destructive run then failed inside stage 3 (MIGRATIONS), migration `008_search.sql`:
  `function public.unaccent(unknown, text) does not exist`. `code_test_db` had been created by hand
  (`createdb`) with no PostgreSQL extensions. A comparison of host state showed `afldb_dev` and
  `afldb_test` both already had `pg_trgm` and `unaccent` — provisioned by
  `tools/maintenance/00_install_postgres.sh` at host bootstrap — while `code_test_db`, created
  outside that script, had neither.
- After the operator manually ran `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;` and
  `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS unaccent;` against `code_test_db`, the complete rebuild
  succeeded: all 91 tracked migrations applied, privileges reconciled, all 22 stages completed, the
  AFLDB-ISSUE-095 ladder witness passed, and final validation **PASSED 85/85** ("Rebuild
  complete."). Total runtime was comfortably inside the one-hour operational target.
- No production database was touched at any point.

### Bounded bootstrap follow-up (implemented 2026-09-07, this worktree)

The rehearsal exposed a real gap, not a defect in the rebuild runner itself: `code_test_db` is
created by the operator outside the runner (§10 point — no DSN in the credential model can
create/drop a database), but the repository's normal host-bootstrap script,
`tools/maintenance/00_install_postgres.sh`, only ever provisioned `afldb_dev` and `afldb_test` —
it never created `code_test_db` or enabled `pg_trgm`/`unaccent` on it, even though
`docs/deployment.md` §6a already pointed to that script as the model for how `code_test_db` should
be provisioned. A database created by hand instead of through the documented bootstrap path was
therefore missing the extensions migration `008_search.sql` requires.

Fix — minimal, host-bootstrap-only, no change to any migration or to the rebuild runner's
guardrails:

- `tools/maintenance/00_install_postgres.sh`: `code_test_db` added to the database-creation loop
  (`for DB in afldb_dev afldb_test code_test_db`, owner `afldb_owner`, same idempotent
  create-if-absent check) and to the extensions/default-privileges loop (`CREATE EXTENSION
  pg_trgm`/`unaccent`, schema ownership, default-privilege reconciliation, and the
  `privileges.sql` reconciler run) — identical treatment to `afldb_dev` and `afldb_test`, applied
  by extending two existing `for DB in ...` loops rather than adding a new one. The closing summary
  banner was updated to list all three databases. `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` /
  `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL` remain commented out in `.env.example` and are still never
  written by the bootstrap script: creating the database and enabling its extensions is now
  automatic, but selecting `code_test_db` as a rebuild target stays an explicit, separate operator
  opt-in, unchanged from the original ISSUE-146 contract.
- `docs/deployment.md` §6a: updated the `code_test_db` provisioning note to state that
  `00_install_postgres.sh` now bootstraps it (including the required extensions) instead of only
  citing the script as a manual model to replicate.
- No change to `008_search.sql` or any other migration, to `tools/db/rebuild-test.ts`'s allowlist,
  DSN handling or destructive guardrails, or to the explicit supported-target contract
  (`afldb_test`, `code_test_db`).

Validation (this worktree, no database contact):

- `bash -n tools/maintenance/00_install_postgres.sh` — syntax OK.
- Manual review confirms both extended loops are DB-name-generic (no `afldb_test`/`afldb_dev`
  literals inside either loop body) and therefore behave identically for `code_test_db`.
- No existing test suite exercises this shell script directly (`tests/db-test-rebuild.test.ts`
  covers `tools/db/rebuild-test.ts`'s TypeScript logic only, which is unchanged here); none added,
  per the "smallest test that proves the change" rule — the change is bash bootstrap SQL, not
  logic under test elsewhere in the suite.

### Follow-up

- None outstanding. `prove-reset` deliberately does not accept `--target`; extend it only if a
  rollback-only reset proof against `code_test_db` is ever needed.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-147 — Public UI responsive design review and remediation

- **Status:** **RESOLVED — 2026-09-13.** See *Resolution (2026-09-13)* at the foot of this entry.
  As it stood earlier (retained): **OPEN — IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE, validated locally against DEV
  data, and MERGED into `main` as `d18a0bd`; deployed on DEV. Outstanding: the gate-off `npm run
  test:e2e` run of the committed `tests/e2e/responsive-nav.spec.ts` on the Linux dev host, and the
  phone-nav / `/clubs` smoke on a real device.** Branch `claude/issue-147-ui` (worktree
  `D:\dev\afldb-issue-147-ui`) is an ancestor of `main`.
- **Severity / Area:** Medium / Public UI — navigation information architecture, responsive layout,
  dense-table affordance.
- **Reported:** 2026-09-07 (operator request — full rendered review of the public UI at all
  supported screen sizes; known defect: Clubs unreachable from the mobile navigation).
- **Claims no migration number.** No schema, query, route, privilege, `.env` or deployment change.

### Problem

A full authenticated rendered audit of the public site against the DEV deployment
(`http://10.0.40.100:8090`) at seven viewport widths (320 → 1440) over 27 representative routes /
layout families found the page-level responsive discipline sound — **zero document-level horizontal
overflow anywhere** — with the defects concentrated in three areas:

1. **P0 — mobile primary navigation is a different, smaller information architecture.** The
   wide-screen masthead (`PRIMARY_NAV`, `src/components/SiteNav.tsx`) carried 11 destinations; the
   phone bottom bar (`TABS`) carried 5, and the two lists were maintained by hand and independently.
   **Unreachable from the phone chrome: Clubs, Venues, Coaches, Brownlow, Awards, Draft, Match
   Search.** The `/aflw` variant had the same gap (`AFLW_TABS` dropped Venues and Match Search from
   `AFLW_PRIMARY_NAV`). The home "Browse the record" grid (`src/app/page.tsx`) was a **third**
   hand-kept list (and had already drifted — no Coaches card). This is the mechanism by which
   AFLDB-ISSUE-145 (Venues) half-landed: added to the masthead and the home grid, never to mobile.
2. **P1 — a phone masthead-nav overflow band.** Between 641 px and ~890 px the 11-item masthead nav
   needed ~635 px of a ~518 px flex track and spilled over / clipped against the wordmark
   (measured `navScrollW 635 > navClientW 518` at 700 px and 820 px). The 640 px bottom-bar
   breakpoint left this band with the full masthead nav and no room for it.
3. **P1 — dense tables scroll with no cue that they do.** Wide statistical tables scroll correctly
   inside `.table-wrap` (`overflow-x: auto`) and the page never overflows, but at phone widths the
   trailing columns — including the sort-header controls on the players index — sit entirely
   off-screen with no visual affordance that horizontal content exists (players index at 320 px:
   `.table-wrap` client width 272, scroll width 828; the Games/Goals/Finals/Prem/Brownlow headers
   start beyond x≈300).

Full findings matrix, viewport list and baseline screenshots: the ISSUE-147 session record and
`artifacts/issue-147/baseline/` (gitignored, not committed).

### Change

Navigation, responsive CSS and regression tests only. No behavioural change to any data path.

- **`src/lib/site-nav-model.ts` (new).** The single canonical public navigation model: `PRIMARY_NAV`
  / `AFLW_PRIMARY_NAV` (unchanged sets — now the one source of truth), `QUICK_TABS` /
  `AFLW_QUICK_TABS` (the four one-tap phone sections: Home, Players, **Clubs**, Seasons),
  `BROWSE_SECTIONS` (derived from `PRIMARY_NAV` + a per-href blurb map, so the home grid can no
  longer omit or drift from a nav destination — **Coaches card added** as a side effect), and the
  `inAflw` / `isCurrentSection` helpers. A plain module, deliberately **not** `'use client'`: a
  Server Component importing a value from a client module gets a reference proxy, so the home grid's
  `BROWSE_SECTIONS.map` fails at build (`k.BROWSE_SECTIONS.map is not a function`) — proven during
  validation, fixed by relocating the data here.
- **`src/components/SiteNav.tsx`.** `PrimaryNav` unchanged in behaviour (maps `PRIMARY_NAV`).
  `TabBar` now renders the four `QUICK_TABS` plus a **"More"** button that opens a bottom sheet
  (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, `aria-label="All sections"`) listing the **entire** active
  primary set (`PRIMARY_NAV` or `AFLW_PRIMARY_NAV`). The sheet: focus moves in on open and returns
  to the trigger on Escape / backdrop / Close; Tab is trapped inside the panel; `body` scroll is
  locked while open; it closes on Escape, backdrop click, a link click, and `popstate`; the current
  destination carries `aria-current="page"`. `PRIMARY_NAV` / `AFLW_PRIMARY_NAV` / `BROWSE_SECTIONS`
  are re-exported from here for continuity.
- **`src/app/page.tsx`.** The "Browse the record" grid maps `BROWSE_SECTIONS` instead of its own
  inline list (import moved to `@/lib/site-nav-model`).
- **`src/styles/globals.css`.**
  - `.tab-more` styled as a bar item; `.nav-sheet` / `.nav-sheet-panel` / `.nav-sheet-head` /
    `.nav-sheet-list` — a phone-only bottom sheet, `z-index: 70` (above the tab bar and the consent
    banner), `max-height: 80vh` with its own scroll, reduced-motion-safe fade. Base
    `.nav-sheet { display: none }` so it can never render on the desktop layout.
  - Masthead nav at `max-width: 1080px` and `min-width: 641px` now `flex-wrap`s to a tidy
    right-aligned second row (`gap: 0.4rem 0.75rem`, `padding-block: 0.5rem`) instead of overflowing
    the wordmark.
  - `.table-wrap` gets a **CSS-only directional scroll shadow** (new theme-aware `--edge-shadow`
    token; light = translucent ink, dark = faint light so it reads on near-black paper) built from
    four background layers — two paper-coloured "cover" gradients `background-attachment: local` and
    two shadow gradients `scroll` — so a shadow appears only on a side that still has hidden columns
    and not at all on a table that already fits. No markup change to any of the ~10 `.table-wrap`
    call sites.
- **`tests/e2e/responsive-nav.spec.ts` (new — committed regression).** The public responsive
  navigation contract: nav parity derived from what the wide masthead actually renders vs the phone
  "More" sheet (so a destination added to one but not the other fails here); the sheet's
  dialog behaviour (open, Escape + focus return, backdrop close, link close, scroll when taller than
  the screen); the `/aflw` sheet carries the AFLW set; no document-level horizontal overflow on 11
  routes × {320, 375}; a wide table scrolls inside its own region and not the page, with its sort
  control reachable after scrolling; the players filter panel and pagination usable at 320 px; the
  club comparison reachable and legible at 320 px.
- **`tests/e2e/journeys.spec.ts`.** The three `test.skip(isMobile, 'the masthead nav is hidden on a
  phone')` navigation tests replaced with a `reachPrimary()` helper that goes via the phone "More"

- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — one `Unreleased` entry under `### AFLDB-ISSUE-147`.
