  migration 101 applied, service healthy). Stage 8 rendered acceptance STOPPED at 8.1 on a genuine
  defect (§20) — a `.admin-cards` CSS class-name collision with the unrelated responsive-table-card
  pattern (`admin/coaches`, `admin/draft`, `admin/fixtures`) hid `/admin/awards`'s three navigation
  cards at every viewport width. The corrective fix (dedicated `.awards-admin-*` classes with their
  own always-visible grid) was reviewed, committed, pushed and redeployed to DEV, and Stage 8
  restarted from 8.1 in full: the Contributor / Admin / Super Admin role matrix, a complete
  create → correct → void → reinstate → replace lifecycle fixture, responsive (1440×900, 375×812),
  accessibility/focus and console/network acceptance are all PASS. See *Resolution (2026-09-13)*
  below and `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-165.md` §21. PROD untouched; PROD status is not otherwise claimed.
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Area:** Admin / Data management
- **Found:** 2026-09-13
- **Resolved:** 2026-09-13
- **Runbook:** `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-165.md` — §§1–16 are the planning deliverable, **§17 is the
  authoritative implementation record for Stages 1–3** (correcting §§3.1, 3.4, 3.7, 8 and 12
  where the planning turned out to be wrong), **§18 for Stages 4–6**, **§19 for Stage 7**, **§20
  for the Stage 8 CSS defect and fix**, and **§21 for Stage 8 final acceptance**.
- **Migration:** `src/db/migrations/101_awards_honours_lifecycle.sql` — applied to `afldb_test`
  (operator, 2026-09-13: `101_awards_honours_lifecycle.sql ... ok`) and applied on DEV as part of
  the Stage 8 deploy (101/101, 0 pending). PROD unapplied; PROD status is not otherwise claimed.
- **Branch:** `sonnet/issue-165-awards-admin`, base `37ac7d3`.
- **Parent:** `AFLDB-ISSUE-156` (umbrella), consuming P5 — Awards/honours correction lifecycle,
  and absorbing the awards/Hall of Fame/honour-team slice of P8 — Data-editor decomposition.
- **Planning model:** Sonnet 5, medium-high. **Implementation model:** Opus 5 (1M context).

### Problem

`/admin/data-editor` can create an award winner, a Hall of Fame inductee and a
representative/honour-team member (`src/db/queries/awards-admin.ts`), but nothing in the
repository can edit, void, replace or restore any of the three once created. There is no
domain-specific capability (all three gate on the single `data.dataEditor`), and — the
load-bearing finding — no reload-survival mechanism exists for a correction to a source-owned
row: `tools/migration/import_awards.py` reloads every award group through `reload_keyed()`,
which overwrites every column in its own explicit column list from freshly parsed source data on
every run, with no `data_overrides` consultation anywhere in the three tables' path. A correction
made today, if a mutation existed to make one, would be silently reverted by the next reload of
that award group.

### Planning findings (2026-09-13, verified natively — full evidence in `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-165.md` §3)

- Three canonical tables, three different identity keys: `award_winners` keys on its own source
  record id (NOT `award, season, player` — the 1984 All-Australian club+state pairing makes that
  key genuinely wrong, migration 042); `hall_of_fame` keys on `(name, inducted_year)`; linked
  `honour_team_members` rows key on `player_id`, unlinked ones on `player_name_raw` (migration
  059). None of the three has a `status`/lifecycle column today.
- Duplicate prevention is inconsistent: `honour_team_members` already runs a pre-insert collision
  check (`AFLDB-ISSUE-025`/`080`); `award_winners` and `hall_of_fame` run none at all.
- `hall_of_fame.removed_year` already exists and already means something (a real, historical
  Hall of Fame removal) — this must not be confused with "voided because the admin record was a
  data-entry error"; the two stay distinct concepts in the plan.
- `data_edits.table_name` already admits all three tables (migration 058) — no widening needed
  for the audit log. `data_overrides.entity_type` does not admit any of the three — widening
  needed if the durable lifecycle record uses it.
- **Central proof (from reading `reload_keyed()` and `import_awards.py` directly, not
  inference):** an ordinary reload's `UPDATE` only sets the columns explicitly listed by the
  caller, so a new column outside that list (like `award_winners.sort_order`, migration 061,
  already) survives an ordinary reload for free. But all three tables carry a foreign key to
  `players`, and `import_awards.py` itself defends elsewhere against a `TRUNCATE … CASCADE` on a
  foundational table emptying tables it does not expect to be touched
  (`import_awards.py:2674-2679`) — direct evidence that a full rebuild truncates `players` with
  cascade, which empties all three award tables regardless of any additive column. A bare
  `status` column is therefore safe from an ordinary reload but not from a full rebuild; only a
  `data_overrides` record replayed by a new `replay_admin_overrides()` branch survives both,
  matching the precedent every other umbrella phase already established for exactly this reason.
- Capability naming convention confirmed exactly from `src/lib/auth/capabilities.ts`:
  `data.<domain>.read` (Admin and up) / `data.<domain>.edit` (Super Admin only) — so
  `data.awards.read`/`data.awards.edit`, not the umbrella's earlier working name
  `data.honours.correct`.
- All public reads for the three tables go through one module, `src/db/queries/awards.ts`, with
  no active/voided filter anywhere today — every consumer needs the same new predicate, with an
  explicit before/after invariance proof that an untouched row's output does not change.

### Recommended design (runbook §6–§12)

`status IN ('active','void')` (two states, no `ended` — an award fact does not "cease" the way an
ongoing appointment does) plus `status_reason`, added to each table by one additive migration
(next free number 101 at this snapshot); identity-bearing fields (`award_id`/`season`/recipient
for `award_winners`; `name`/`inducted_year` for `hall_of_fame`; `team_name`/player identity for
`honour_team_members`) are void + replace only, never corrected in place, matching the
`AFLDB-ISSUE-163` boundary. `data_overrides.entity_type` widened for the three tables, replayed
by new branches in `tools/migration/common.py`'s `replay_admin_overrides()`, called by
`import_awards.py` immediately after each group's own `reload_keyed()` — the durability layer a
bare column cannot provide across a full rebuild. New `/admin/awards` surface (D-3),
`data.awards.read`/`.edit` capabilities, the three existing `data-editor` create forms relocated
(not rewritten) per the umbrella's P8 rule. `rising_star`/`all_australian` CSV acquisition
ownership unchanged (D2); Brownlow untouched.

### Non-goals

Brownlow administration/authority; new award types or definitions; award acquisition/CSV
redesign; player merge; match rekey; public Awards/Hall of Fame/honour-team page redesign beyond
the minimum status filter; destructive rewrite of historical source data.

### Implementation — Stages 1–3 (2026-09-13, uncommitted, unapplied, undeployed)

Full record in `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-165.md` §17. Summary of what changed and what it proves.

**Stage 1 — schema and promotion lineage.** Migration 101 adds `status text NOT NULL DEFAULT
'active'`, `status_reason text` and `updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` to each of the
three tables, with `CHECK (status IN ('active','void'))` and `CHECK (status <> 'void' OR
status_reason IS NOT NULL)`; replaces `hall_of_fame_name_uq` with an ACTIVE-ROW-ONLY partial
unique index preserving `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`; rebuilds both migration-059 `honour_team_members`
partial indexes with `AND status <> 'void'`; and widens `data_overrides.entity_type` by the three
names. No `created_at`, no `CREATE INDEX` (D-8), no `GRANT`, no trigger and no data written — all
three tables predate migrations 039/045, whose catalogue-derived registry seeds already carry
them, so the table-level grants cover the new columns and `privileges.sql` needs no edit (§8
items 4–5 verified, not assumed). `award_winners`' `(source_id, source_record_id)` key is
deliberately untouched and `(award_id, season, player_id)` is deliberately NOT made unique: the
1984 All-Australian records every player under both a club and a state selection, which migration
042 exists to keep representable.

**Stage 2 — `src/db/queries/admin-awards.ts` (new).** Readers and five mutation primitives per
domain — create, correct safe metadata, void, reinstate, replace. `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` plus an
`updated_at` compare-and-swap refuses a stale write before anything is written; `data_edits` is
written in the same transaction as every canonical write and every override write; a refusal
discovered after the first write THROWS so `postgres.js` rolls back instead of committing a
half-done mutation. Identity-bearing fields (`award_id`, `season`, the recipient identity,
provenance; `name`/`inducted_year`; `team_name`/player identity) are refused with one shared
sentence per domain. The AFLDB-ISSUE-080 §5.3 advisory lock is reused unchanged for every
honour-team identity writer, and replacement re-runs the full §4.3/§4.4 collision policy over
ACTIVE rows.

**Stage 3 — replay.** Three new `replay_admin_overrides()` branches in `tools/migration/common.py`
over three field groups: `lifecycle` (status, reason, replacement linkage — unconditional),
`correction` (a DELTA over a source-owned row, `jsonb_exists` semantics so an absent key leaves
the source value and an explicit null clears it) and `record` (the whole durable row of a manual
creation, re-created then restored). Durable keys are natural, never row ids:
`<sources.key>:<source_record_id>`, `<sources.key>:<name>|<inducted_year>`,
`<sources.key>:<team_name>|<player identity>`. Called from all nine `import_awards.py` reload
sites — seven `award_winners` groups, the Hall of Fame reload and the honour-team reload — inside
each group's own transaction and before its commit (R-2). Two further importer changes the
lifecycle made necessary: `reload_keyed()` gained a `lifecycle_column` so a VOIDED out-of-scope
row no longer refuses the whole awards import, and
`_refuse_honour_team_identity_collisions()` ignores voided rows for the same reason — without
them an ordinary, correct administrative decision would brick the importer.

**Operator decisions.** D-8, D-9, D-10, D-11 and D-12 all implemented as specified; B-1 and B-2
closed. B-1's measurement (`source_id IS NULL` = 0, `source_record_id IS NULL` = 0, 3,712 rows on
`afldb_test`) is re-measured by the integration suite rather than trusted, and the defensive
`no_durable_key` refusal is kept anyway in both the writer and the replay.

**Two findings the planning session missed.**

1. **The public read surface is four modules, not one.** §3.7 claimed every public read goes
   through `src/db/queries/awards.ts`. It does not: `src/db/queries/grid-solver.ts` (17
   references), `src/db/queries/nl/player-career.ts` (2) and `src/app/sitemap.ts` (2) also read
   these tables directly. Grid Solver answers award clues off `award_winners`, natural-language
   search counts award wins per player, and the sitemap enumerates award seasons and honour-team
   names. All four need the Stage 4+ status filter, and §12.6's invariance gate must be written
   against all four.
2. **A live promotion-lineage defect, found and fixed.** Migration 058 admitted `award_winners`,
   `hall_of_fame` and `honour_team_members` into `data_edits_table_name_check`, and none of the
   three has ever had a lineage target in `tools/db/promotion-inventory.ts` — while
   `/admin/data-editor` has been creating rows in all three since AFLDB-ISSUE-080. All three are
   import-writable tables a promotion rebuilds, so an honours audit row was reinstated with its
   `row_id` integer unchanged, counted and remapped by nothing, and after a lineage-changing
   promotion named a different award, inductee or selection: the AFLDB-ISSUE-142 (B)
   misattribution, and the fourth instance of exactly the defect AFLDB-ISSUE-160 D-3 found for
   `draft_picks`. Fixed with three new `LineageIdentityRule` values and their `byId`/`byIdentity`
   SQL. A row with no resolvable identity is reported unresolved and never matched by name — in
   particular an honour-team row that is linked but whose player holds no durable identity is
   excluded from the identity SQL rather than falling back to its display name, which would
   re-create the AFLDB-ISSUE-025 defect migration 059 exists to prevent. A new standing contract
   test in `tests/db-promotion-check.test.ts` now reads the allowlist out of the migrations and
   requires every admitted name to carry a target or a recorded exemption, so the next table
   admitted forces the decision at review time.

**Recorded gap that the new standing test surfaces, and it is not this issue's.**
`brownlow_vote_entry_state` is admitted by migration 094 with no lineage target. Its primary key
is `match_id`, so a `data_edits` `row_id` for it is a match id and a lineage change does renumber
it; it needs a `matches`/`match_key` target. That belongs to the Brownlow admin domain
(`AFLDB-ISSUE-155`). `brownlow_season_authority` is a genuine exemption — its `row_id` is a season
year, a permanent natural identity nothing renumbers.

**Validation.** DB-free: 4,552 tests passing over 121 of 122 files (`npx vitest run` excluding
`tests/integration/**` and `tests/nl-ui/**`), `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean on every
changed TypeScript file, `python -m py_compile` clean on both changed Python modules. One
pre-existing, unrelated Windows failure remains and is not touched by this work:
`tests/finals-semantics-contract.test.ts` (the known CRLF split — Linux passes).

**DB-backed: PASSED.** `tests/integration/admin-awards.test.ts` — **24/24, run twice in immediate
succession** against `afldb_test` (`current_database()` proved before either run), leaving the
database exactly as found: `award_winners` 3,712, `hall_of_fame` 343, `honour_team_members` 113,
zero fixture awards, zero fixture players, zero overrides and zero audit rows for the three
entity types. `tests/integration/player-honours.test.ts` and
`tests/integration/club-honours.test.ts`: 14/14.

**One coverage gap, recorded not worked around.** `tests/integration/awards-reload-links.test.ts`
— the suite that exercises the REAL honours reloads, and therefore the closest existing cover for
this issue's `import_awards.py` changes — SKIPS all 107 of its tests because it requires
`AFLDB_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL` (the restricted importer-role DSN) and no `.env` on this machine
defines it. That is a pre-existing environment gap, not a regression. It left the one NEW
`reload_keyed()` code path (`lifecycle_column`) with no cover at all, so the ISSUE-165 suite now
proves it directly under the owner role instead — an ACTIVE out-of-scope Hall of Fame row still
refuses the reload (AFLDB-ISSUE-080 unchanged), and the same row once VOIDED does not, with
`delete_missing=False` so the real 343-row Hall of Fame is untouched. The operator should still
run `awards-reload-links` with the importer-role DSN set before Stage 4 merges.

### The first DB-backed run, and the five failures it found (2026-09-13)

18 passed / 5 failed. Full record in `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-165.md` §17.8.

| # | Failure | Cause | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `applies cleanly` expected 6 CHECK constraints, found 3 | the assertion counted `conname LIKE '%status%'`, which can only ever find 3 — `<table>_void_reason_ck` does not contain "status" | **test defect**; the schema was NOT renamed to suit it, and the assertion now names all six constraints and checks each definition |
| 2 | award span stayed 2026 after a void, expected NULL | the award still had eight ACTIVE winners left by earlier tests in the same file; NULL is only correct when the voided row was the last active winner | **fixture-isolation defect**; `recomputeAwardSpan()` was right and was not weakened |
| 3 | the duplicate test's FIRST create was already refused | earlier tests had recorded that player on that award in that season, so the `(award, season, player)` duplicate check fired — working as designed | **fixture-isolation defect** |
| 4 | Hall of Fame replacement key carried the linked player's display name | `insertHallOfFame()` overwrote the administrator's supplied name with `players.display_name` | **IMPLEMENTATION defect** — see below |
| 5 | destructive-rebuild test's create refused | same as 3 | **fixture-isolation defect** |

**Failure 4 was a real bug, inherited by copying the legacy creator.** `hall_of_fame.name` is not
a display fact: migration 042 keys the table on `(name, inducted_year)` and this issue's durable
key is `<source key>:<name>|<inducted_year>`. Deriving the name from the linked player filed the
induction under a DIFFERENT key from the one the administrator asked for — a silent identity move
on the one table whose name IS its identity, which R-1 forbids — and made the required case
unexpressible: re-entering a voided inductee under the SAME name and year while linking the person
it should have been is exactly how a mis-identified Hall of Fame row is corrected. **Fixed:** the
supplied name is canonical; the player's display name is used only when no name was supplied.
`award_winners` and `honour_team_members` keep the legacy behaviour deliberately, because on those
two the display name sits beside a separate identity and moves nothing that decides which row it
is; a source-contract test pins the asymmetry so it reads as a decision, not an oversight.

**Isolation and repeatability.** Every test that writes now owns its own identity — its own award
(`afldb-issue-165-test-<tag>`), its own Hall of Fame name, its own team name. Cleanup
(`purgeFixtures()`) runs in `beforeAll` AND `afterAll` and keys on two STABLE prefixes, never a
per-run nonce, so it also clears debris a crashed run left behind. The first run proved the need:
exactly one durable record leaked, a manual award winner's `record` override keyed
`manual_admin_edit:award_winner:<uuid>`, which carries neither prefix and names an award that had
since been deleted — left alone it would have failed the next run's replay closed with "award_slug
does not resolve to an award". The sweep now matches the override payload as well as the key.

### Stages 4–6 (2026-09-13, later session)

Full record in `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-165.md` §18. The ordering rule §17.7 set was honoured: every public
status filter landed before any mutation surface became reachable, and until Stage 5 there was no
route, action or capability that could void a row at all.

**Stage 4 — the exhaustive consumer audit.** A fresh symbol search confirmed §3.7's corrected
four-module list and added nothing. Every scan now carries `status = 'active'`: `awards.ts` 19,
`grid-solver.ts` 17 (including the nested `award_winners w2` subquery that decides which seasons
count as All-Australian squad seasons), `nl/player-career.ts` 2, `app/sitemap.ts` 2. The Query
Builder's `player.awards` and `player.hall_of_fame` relations carry it in their CORRELATION, not
as a column, so no future column can bypass it and the QA tool cannot contradict the public page
about who is in the Hall of Fame. `hall_of_fame.removed_year` is untouched and still public — a
formally removed inductee WAS inducted, and only `status = 'void'` hides a record.
`db-health.ts` is deliberately unfiltered, with the reason written into the source so a future
"make it match the public queries" cleanup meets the answer first. **R-3 is closed by a counting
contract, not by the list above**: `tests/honours-lifecycle-public-contract.test.ts` asserts per
module that scans equal lifecycle predicates, with comment lines stripped so prose explaining the
rule cannot stand in for the rule.

**Two defects in the Stages 1–3 code, found by Stage 4's own work.** (a)
`readHonourOverrides()` read `data_overrides` on the APPLICATION pool. Migration 073 grants
SELECT on that table to `afldb_import` and nobody else — it carries no `grant_app_read()`,
deliberately — and app reads have been fail-closed since migration 039, so the function worked
for a database OWNER (which is what the integration suite connects as, which is why 24/24 missed
it) and would have failed closed on the first `/admin/awards/*/[id]` page load. Moved to
`withImportConnection`, matching `readDraftOverrides()`. (b) The revalidation set was short by
three cached pages, and Stage 4 is what made them movable: `/awards` (ISR 24h, renders winner and
season counts that now exclude voided rows), `/seasons/<year>` (ISR 1h, club best-and-fairest and
Hall of Fame inductees) and `/sitemap.xml`.

**Stage 5.** `data.awards.read` (ADMIN_AND_UP) / `data.awards.edit` (SUPER_ADMIN_ONLY), following
the capabilities-file convention letter for letter; `/admin/awards` added to the Data group after
Fixtures. The AFLDB-ISSUE-158 source contract was extended rather than duplicated — both names
placed in the typed `EQUIVALENT_ROLE_GUARD` record, nav order assertions updated, a visibility
test added — and its existing rules then cover all ten pages, the route handler and all fifteen
Server Actions mechanically. The three `new` pages assert `.edit` rather than `.read`, following
the `/admin/draft/new` precedent: strictly narrower, so no boundary is widened.

**Stage 6.** Ten routes, three domains kept separate (D-5 answered in favour of sub-routes).
Provenance is a column in every list, because whether a row is source-owned decides whether
correcting it needs a durable override to survive the next reload. Identity fields are shown
read-only with the reason beside them; row ids are labelled "renumbered by a rebuild; not a
stable identifier" and the durable natural key is what is presented as identity, with
replacement linkage rendered from the override payload's `replaced_by_key`/`replaces_key`.
Replacement is two steps with an explicit "void this, then record that" preview. History reuses
the AFLDB-ISSUE-157 viewer's own `listDataEditHistory` and `ValueDiff`. The three forms were
MOVED and rewired, not rewritten, with their field sets lifted into shared `*Fields` components
so a creation and the replacement half of a replacement ask for the same facts in the same words.
`/admin/data-editor` lost the three forms and the three Server Actions and carries the
Draft-precedent pointer. `src/db/queries/awards-admin.ts` now has no application caller; it is
retained with a header forbidding one, because three contracts are currently pinned only through
it, and porting them is closeout work.

**The importer-role gate §17.8 could not run has been run.** A valid DSN was derivable from the
operator's existing configuration — every DSN in `.env` shares the `afldb_test` endpoint, so the
existing importer credential repointed at the test database is exactly the required DSN. It was
built in memory, passed to the child process environment only, and never printed or written to
disk; `current_database() = afldb_test` and `current_user = afldb_import` were proved first.
**96 passed / 1 failed / 10 skipped.** The single failure is the `captaincies` manifest assertion
(expects `records_read = 1375`, observes 1,774; `data/awards/captaincies.csv` has held 1,774 data
rows since `d08591f`), on a table explicitly out of scope here and untouched by this diff. Not
opened as a new issue: it is a stale assertion with a one-line fix, not a defect.

### Stage 8, restart and genuine acceptance failure (2026-09-13)

Full record in `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-165.md` §20. The operator committed and pushed Stages 4–6 and deployed
to DEV (`8250abe`/`main`, migration 101 applied, service healthy); Stage 8 rendered acceptance then
found a genuine defect at gate 8.1 before role-boundary or lifecycle testing could proceed —
`/admin/awards`'s three navigation cards were invisible at every viewport width, root-caused to a
`.admin-cards` CSS class-name collision with the unrelated responsive-table-card pattern shared by
`admin/coaches`/`admin/draft`/`admin/fixtures`. A source-only corrective fix (dedicated
`.awards-admin-*` classes with their own always-visible grid, §20.3) was written and validated but
left uncommitted for operator review, per the session brief's stop-on-genuine-defect instruction.

A second, unrelated finding from the same Stage 8 role-matrix pass was opened as
`AFLDB-ISSUE-166` (streamed admin denials returning HTTP 200 + meta-refresh instead of an HTTP
redirect). It was not caused by this issue and was resolved independently 2026-09-13 (see the
`AFLDB-ISSUE-166` entry above); it held nothing against this issue's own closure (§20.4).

### Resolution (2026-09-13)

**Resolved.** The operator reviewed, committed, pushed and redeployed the §20.3 fix; Stage 8
restarted from 8.1 in full and every remaining acceptance gate is PASS. Full record in
`issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-165.md` §21.

**Contributor — PASS.** Awards navigation is absent from the sidebar; the Contributor's Data group
exposed only its permitted surface. Direct navigation to `/admin/awards` was denied with a genuine
HTTP 307 to `/admin/upload`; direct navigation to `/admin/awards/winners`,
`/admin/awards/hall-of-fame` and `/admin/awards/honour-teams` was denied in every case, with the
honour-teams denial explicitly confirmed as a genuine HTTP 307 and not the former `AFLDB-ISSUE-166`
meta-refresh behaviour. No lifecycle control was reachable and no mutation request was crafted.
Console: 0 errors/warnings; network clean.

**Admin — PASS.** `/admin/awards` is available and renders normally; award winners, Hall of Fame
and honour-team list/detail surfaces are all readable, with observed record counts of **3,712
award winners / 343 Hall of Fame / 113 honour-team records**. All mutation controls (record new,
correct, void, reinstate, replace) are absent, and DOM inspection confirmed the server-rendered
markup omits them outright rather than merely CSS-hiding them; detail pages show explanatory
read-only text instead. Direct navigation to the three create routes
(`/admin/awards/winners/new`, `/admin/awards/hall-of-fame/new`, `/admin/awards/honour-teams/new`)
was denied and redirected to the Admin dashboard. 1440×900 PASS on the remaining list surfaces;
keyboard focus order logical with a visible focus outline. Console/network: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

**Super Admin — PASS.** Landing, winners, Hall of Fame and honour-team surfaces all load; "Record
a winner" / "Record an induction" / "Record a selection" links are present; active records expose
Correct / Void / Replace across all three domains, and a voided award row exposes Reinstate as
expected. Direct navigation to the three create routes loads populated forms. No mutation was
submitted during this final acceptance pass — the earlier lifecycle fixture already covers
mutation behaviour. 1440×900 PASS; 375×812 PASS with no page-level horizontal overflow
(`scrollWidth === clientWidth === 360`) — one provenance/state table cell uses contained
`.table-wrap` horizontal scrolling by design at this width, expected behaviour and not a defect.
Keyboard focus order between lifecycle controls PASS with a visible focus outline. Console/network:
0 errors, 0 warnings; requests successful.

**Lifecycle fixture.** A full DEV-only fixture lifecycle — create → correct → void → reinstate →
replace — passed with public visibility and durable history/override behaviour both checked, and
zero active fixture residue at the end. **Award-winner row #3714 remains voided with the Stage 8
lifecycle-fixture reason**, as intentional durable audit/history evidence under the non-destructive
lifecycle design (§6); it does not contradict "zero active fixture residue" and no cleanup was
required or performed.

**Conclusion.** Stage 8 complete: the Contributor / Admin / Super Admin role matrix, responsive
acceptance, accessibility/focus acceptance, console/network acceptance and lifecycle behaviour are
all PASS. `AFLDB-ISSUE-165` is Resolved. `CHANGELOG.md` already carries the correct, DEV-scoped
entry under `Unreleased` (13 September 2026) and needs no change: it states migration 101 is
applied on DEV and deliberately does not claim a PROD status. Residue recorded rather than fixed,
carried as follow-up under the parent umbrella rather than blocking this issue:
`src/db/queries/awards-admin.ts` stays retired-with-no-caller (porting its twenty mocked-unit tests
is a rewrite, not a move, and `awards-reload-links.test.ts` holds the only real-contention
advisory-lock proof; its three contracts are now each proved against the live module too), and the
`captaincies` manifest assertion (expects 1,375; the tracked CSV has held 1,774 since `d08591f`) is
pre-existing `AFLDB-ISSUE-112` debt untouched by this diff. Following the sibling convention
(160–163), PROD promotion is not this issue's own gate and is carried on the `AFLDB-ISSUE-156`
umbrella.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-166 — Streamed admin denials return HTTP 200 + meta-refresh instead of an HTTP redirect

- **Status:** **RESOLVED 2026-09-13** — root cause proven, fix implemented and validated, committed
  as `aaa24f8`, deployed to DEV as `d0b522a85e357aa41a0058f11ab23eba6f637a6e`, and accepted on DEV
  by the plain-Admin and Super Admin probes. See *Resolution (2026-09-13)*. PROD untouched.
- **Severity:** Low
- **Classification:** HTTP denial-signalling defect. **Not an authorization bypass. Not
  information disclosure. Not a mutation bypass.**
- **Area:** Admin / Auth / Next.js rendering
- **Found:** 2026-09-13, during `AFLDB-ISSUE-165` Stage 8 rendered-acceptance role-matrix testing
  on DEV. Confirmed **not** caused by or specific to ISSUE-165 — it reproduced identically on
  pre-existing admin routes and its cause predates that work.
- **Branch:** `opus/issue-166-admin-fetch-auth-bypass`, base `77c03e9`.
- **Investigation model:** Opus 5 (1M context).

### Withdrawal of the initial report

The first triage opened this issue at **High** severity and described it as a systemic
authorization bypass. Investigation disproved that. The following claims are **withdrawn in
full** and must not be carried forward into any summary, handoff or release note:

1. **"`requireCapability()` was bypassed."** Withdrawn. It was never bypassed. Every admin page,
   Route Handler and Server Action calls its guard before it awaits anything else, and the
   `AFLDB-ISSUE-158` capability-enforcement source contract in `tests/auth.test.ts` already held
   that property across all 77 admin entry points throughout. The guard ran, denied, and called
   `redirect()` exactly as designed; only the *transport* of that denial was wrong.
2. **"Full privileged page content was returned."** Withdrawn. No privileged page body was ever
   rendered on a denied request, and no privileged query was issued. The markers that suggested
   otherwise in the first probe were the pages' compile-time `metadata.title` constants
   (`'Site settings'`, `'Data QA search'`, `'Record an award winner'`) rendering into `<title>` —
   source strings, not data. The probe was badly designed and proved nothing.
3. **"`/admin/admins` leaked other administrators' session IP and device data to the Admin
   role."** Withdrawn, and it was never true. `people.admins.read` is `ADMIN_AND_UP` by design
   (`src/lib/auth/capabilities.ts`), the page is in the Admin sidebar, and
   `listAdminAccounts()` (`src/db/queries/admin-users.ts`) scopes `auth_sessions` rows —
   `ip`, `user_agent` — to the viewer's own unless the viewer is `super_admin`. An Admin seeing
   their **own** session IP on that page is designed behaviour, not a leak.
4. **"Caused by a per-worker in-memory cache artifact in `deploy/server-cluster.mjs`."**
   Withdrawn. Not a cache artifact of any kind: the responses carry
   `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, and the behaviour
   reproduces deterministically on a single worker. `deploy/server-cluster.mjs` is not implicated
   and was not changed.

A fifth item from the initial report — "whether mutating Server Actions are similarly reachable
is untested and is the single most urgent follow-up" — is now **answered: they are not
reachable.** See *Evidence* below. No privileged mutation was performed to establish this.

### Root cause

`src/app/admin/loading.tsx` placed a route-level Suspense boundary above every guarded page under
`/admin`. React commits the HTML shell — the HTTP status line included — as soon as that
boundary's fallback is available, which is **before** the page component runs and therefore
before the page's `requireCapability()` runs. By the time the guard called `redirect()`, the
status was already sent and Next.js 16 could no longer express it as a `307` + `Location`.

Next's two shell-error recovery paths
(`node_modules/next/dist/server/app-render/app-render.js`, the `isRedirectError` branches) are
the only places a redirect becomes a status code, and a redirect thrown inside an
already-flushed Suspense boundary never reaches them. It is collected instead by
`make-get-server-inserted-html.js`, which injects

```html
<meta id="__next-page-redirect" http-equiv="refresh" content="1;url=/admin">
```

into the already-committed **200 OK** body. A browser obeys that tag — one second later, per the
`1;` delay — so interactive navigation still denied correctly and the defect stayed invisible
during ordinary use. `fetch()`, `curl`, a crawler, an uptime monitor or any other non-browser
client obeys nothing and records a denied admin route as a success.

### Evidence

Measured against DEV build `77c03e9`, by an authenticated lower-privileged Admin session and by
credential-free probes:

- Denied `/admin/settings`, `/admin/query-builder` and `/admin/awards/winners/new` each returned
  `200` with `metaRefresh=1;url=/admin`, and `.admin-main` contained only `"Loading…"`.
- **Zero** forms, inputs, selects, textareas, tables, rows or buttons in `.admin-main` on every
  denied render.
- **One** Flight chunk on a denied render versus **three** on the permitted `/admin/awards`;
  denied bodies ~25.4 KB against ~35.0 KB permitted and ~24.5 KB for the anonymous
  `/admin/login`.
- Every privileged page and query path guards before privileged data access. A static ordering
  check over all 77 admin entry points found the guard to be the first `await` everywhere except
  the intentionally public surfaces (`admin/login`, `admin/invite/[token]`, and the
  `admin/grid-solver` redirect stub, which reads nothing). All five admin `generateMetadata()`
  functions guard first too — including `fixtures/[season]/[fixtureKey]`, the only one that
  reads the database, which calls `readFixture()` after its guard.
- **Route Handlers return real HTTP redirects.** `/admin/nl-search/export` denied with a genuine
  3xx (`type=opaqueredirect`) in both document and RSC request shapes; all eight admin Route
  Handlers call `requireCapability()`.
- **Server Actions remain independently capability-guarded.** All 24 `'use server'` modules under
  `src/app/admin` guard each exported action; `brownlow/actions.ts`'s five exports funnel through
  one `mutate()` that guards first. A Server Action POST is not a streamed HTML render, so the
  degradation studied here cannot reach it.
- **Control:** `/seasons?from=1990` — a page-level `redirect()` on a `force-dynamic` route with
  **no** loading boundary above it and no `<Suspense>` in the root layout — returned a genuine
  HTTP redirect (`type=opaqueredirect`), while plain `/seasons` returned `200`. This isolates the
  boundary as the cause rather than anything about `redirect()`, the guards or the deployment.
- The precondition was reproducible with no credentials at all: the public
  `/admin/invite/<bogus-token>` route returned `200` with the `aria-busy` "Loading…" fallback at
  byte ~7,378 and the real page content at ~22,516 inside a `<template>`, proving the admin
  segment commits its shell before the page resolves.
- A synthetic `RSC: 1` probe was run and is recorded here as **not meaningful**: it redirected
  identically on denied and permitted routes, so it carries no authorization signal. It is an
  artifact of a hand-made header lacking the router-state parameters a real client sends.

### Scope

All 47 admin `page.tsx` routes sat under the boundary. The degradation applied to the **46** that
can emit a page-level redirect: the 44 capability/role-guarded pages, plus `admin/login`
(redirects when already signed in) and `admin/grid-solver` (`permanentRedirect`, `content="0;…"`,
so no delay). `admin/invite/[token]` renders and never redirects, so it was unaffected. The
`mustChangePassword` bounce to `/admin/password` degraded the same way, so an account holding a
temporary password got a one-second view of other admin routes' loading shells — shells only, with
no content, for the same reason as above. Route Handlers, Server Actions and `/api/*` were never
affected.

### Fix

1. **Delete `src/app/admin/loading.tsx`.** One deletion repairs all 46 routes at once. Guards then
   run during the shell render, so `redirect()` is a shell error and Next emits a real `307` +
   `Location`. Deliberately not a per-page patch and deliberately not a `/admin/admins` one-off:
   the audit proved the cause was one shared boundary, not a per-route omission.
2. **`useLinkStatus()` in `src/app/admin/AdminNav.tsx`** for navigation feedback, with the pending
   indicator rendered inside the relevant `<Link>`. This preserves what the boundary was added for
   on 2026-08-19 ("I clicked it and nothing happened") without opening a server boundary above the
   guards, and puts the feedback on the link that was actually clicked. Supporting
   `.admin-nav-pending` rule in `src/styles/globals.css`, inline inside the existing anchor so no
   existing link rule changes.
3. **Structural regression contracts in `tests/auth.test.ts`** (`describe('denial reaches the HTTP
   layer (AFLDB-ISSUE-166)')`): no `loading.tsx` at or above any guarded admin page, no
   `src/app/loading.tsx`, and no `<Suspense>` wrapping an admin layout's children — so the defect
   cannot be reintroduced under the same name or a different one. Proven RED before the fix
   (restoring the boundary fails the first assertion with the explanatory message) and GREEN after.

No caching was weakened, no capability changed, no mutation guard touched, and no per-page
`<Suspense>` was added speculatively.

### Validation (workstation, 2026-09-13)

`npx vitest run tests/auth.test.ts` 146/146 passed, including the three new contracts; RED
demonstrated by temporarily restoring the boundary. `npm run typecheck` clean. `npm run build`
full pass, standalone bundle ready, with no `loading` chunk left under `.next/server/app/admin`.
`git diff --check` clean. ESLint on the changed files reports one **pre-existing**
`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` error in `AdminNav.tsx`'s `localStorage` effect — proved
pre-existing by linting an untouched copy of the file from a sibling worktree, which reports the
identical error — and it was left alone under the scope rule. `src/styles/globals.css` is not
linted: ESLint here has no CSS configuration.

### Test-harness limitation (recorded, not worked around)

**No harness can assert the streamed HTTP status without a running server.** `tests/admin-nav/`
is a genuine authenticated Playwright harness — `auth.setup.ts` signs in through the real
`/admin/login` form with a freshly computed TOTP code — but it requires a running deployment, its
`playwright.admin-nav.config.ts` pins the project to `testMatch: /admin-nav\.spec\.ts/`, and its
account is the **super-admin** diagnostic one, which is denied nothing and so cannot demonstrate a
denial at all. Closing the gap properly needs a lower-privileged admin credential set plus a
`testMatch` widening; a cheaper variant needing no new credentials would assert that
`/admin/grid-solver` returns `308` + `Location: /grid-solver` rather than `200` + meta-refresh,
using the existing super-admin state. Neither was built under this issue's scope.

**Consequence: DEV Probe 1/2 are mandatory acceptance evidence for this issue, not a formality.**

### Acceptance criteria — MET on DEV 2026-09-13

These were the criteria that kept the issue open. They were run on DEV against
`d0b522a85e357aa41a0058f11ab23eba6f637a6e` and are **PASS**; the per-criterion evidence is in
*Resolution (2026-09-13)* below. Pass criteria as originally written:

1. `/admin/settings`, `/admin/query-builder` and `/admin/awards/winners/new`, requested by a plain
   Admin session, return a genuine HTTP redirect (`307` + `Location: /admin`).
2. No `__next-page-redirect` meta tag appears in any admin response body.
3. `/admin/awards` and `/admin/admins` still return `200` with full content and three Flight
   chunks for that same Admin session.
4. `/admin/nl-search/export` is unchanged.
5. A Super Admin session still reaches all three formerly denied pages with content.
6. Clicking an admin sidebar link still shows visible pending feedback.

### Resolution (2026-09-13)

**Resolved.** The fix is committed, deployed to DEV and accepted on both sides of the
authorization boundary.

**Commit and deployment.** Committed as `aaa24f8` ("AFLDB-ISSUE-166: deny admin routes at the HTTP
layer, not by meta-refresh") on `opus/issue-166-admin-fetch-auth-bypass`, base `77c03e9`. DEV
deployed at `d0b522a85e357aa41a0058f11ab23eba6f637a6e`: production build PASS at **1,534/1,534**
pages, migration ledger **101/101 with nothing applied** (this fix carries no migration),
`afldb.service` healthy, `/api/health` `status=ok` / `database=ok`.

**Probe 1 — plain Admin session, after deploy.** Documents under `/admin`, `fetch()` with manual
redirect handling:

| Route | Result |
|---|---|
| `/admin/settings` | `status=0`, `type=opaqueredirect` |
| `/admin/query-builder` | `status=0`, `type=opaqueredirect` |
| `/admin/awards/winners/new` | `status=0`, `type=opaqueredirect` |
| `/admin/awards` | `status=200`, `type=basic` |
| `/admin/admins` | `status=200`, `type=basic` |
| `/admin/nl-search/export` | `status=0`, `type=opaqueredirect` |

**No denied document response returned `200` + `__next-page-redirect`.** An `opaqueredirect` result
is what a redirect looks like to a manual-redirect `fetch()` — the redirect is made at the HTTP
layer, which is the property this issue is about. The exact status line and `Location` value are
deliberately not claimed here: an opaque redirect does not expose them to the probe, so the
recorded evidence is that the denial reached the transport, not that it was specifically a `307`.
Before the fix these same six requests returned `200` with a `__next-page-redirect` meta tag.

**Probe 2 — Super Admin session, immediately preceding.** `/admin/settings`, `/admin/query-builder`
and `/admin/awards/winners/new` each rendered the full page, and `/admin/nl-search/export` returned
its CSV successfully. Authorization behaviour is therefore correct on **both** sides of the
boundary: the permitted role is not over-denied by the fix, and the denied role is refused at the
HTTP layer.

**Against the six pass criteria.** 1 — PASS as recorded above, with the status-code caveat stated.
2 — PASS, no `__next-page-redirect` in any denied response. 3 — PASS, `/admin/awards` and
`/admin/admins` still `200` `type=basic` for the same Admin session (the Flight-chunk count was not
re-counted in this probe and is not claimed). 4 — PASS, `/admin/nl-search/export` behaves as the
route requires on each side: refused at the HTTP layer for the Admin session, CSV for the Super
Admin session. 5 — PASS, Probe 2. 6 — PASS, operator visual confirmation on DEV (below).

**Criterion 6 — sidebar pending feedback, operator-confirmed on DEV 2026-09-13.** The
`useLinkStatus()` pending dot rendered beside the clicked **Player links** nav entry while the RSC
navigation was in flight, and the destination page then completed normally. Confirmed visually and
by screenshot, with the pending window made observable under network throttling:

| RSC request | Duration |
|---|---|
| `player-links?_rsc=17qrm` | ~2.03 s |
| `player-links?_rsc=tg9kl` | ~2.05 s |
| `player-links?_rsc=72j5p` | ~3.64 s |

This is the criterion that replaces what the deleted `loading.tsx` was originally added for on
2026-08-19 — navigation feedback — and it confirms the feedback now appears on the specific link
that was clicked rather than by blanking the page behind a server boundary above the guards. The
throttled durations are evidence that the indicator was observable during a real pending window,
not a timing measurement of the route.

**All six pass criteria are MET.**

**Classification retained, unchanged by acceptance:** **Low — HTTP denial-signalling defect. Not an
authorization bypass, not information disclosure, not a mutation bypass.** The four withdrawn
claims of the initial High triage stay withdrawn in full.

**Root cause, as fixed:** `src/app/admin/loading.tsx` — one shared route-level Suspense boundary
above all 46 redirect-capable admin pages, which committed a `200` shell before any page-level
`redirect()` could run. Deleted. Navigation feedback moved to `useLinkStatus()` in `AdminNav`, and
three structural contracts in `tests/auth.test.ts` refuse a restored boundary (proven RED before
the fix, GREEN after).

**Follow-ups, neither a blocker and neither allocated an ID:** the test-harness limitation recorded
above (no harness asserts a streamed HTTP status without a running server; closing it properly
needs a lower-privileged admin credential set plus a `testMatch` widening in
`playwright.admin-nav.config.ts`), and the pre-existing Next 16 `middleware` → `proxy` deprecation
noted below.

**Not done:** no PROD deployment, no PROD probe, and no PROD claim of any kind. Reaching production
is the normal release-lifecycle step for this branch, not an open defect.

### Files

- `src/app/admin/loading.tsx` — **deleted**
- `src/app/admin/AdminNav.tsx` — `useLinkStatus()` pending indicator inside the nav `<Link>`
- `src/styles/globals.css` — `.admin-nav-pending`
- `tests/auth.test.ts` — the ISSUE-166 structural contracts

### Incidental observation, not tracked here

The production build emits a pre-existing Next 16 deprecation: `The "middleware" file convention
is deprecated. Please use "proxy" instead.` It is unrelated to this defect and out of scope, but
it will matter on a future Next upgrade and `src/middleware.ts` is a security-relevant file. It is
recorded here only so the observation is not lost; it has no ID and no owner.

### Objective

One authoritative, audited, capability-gated, replay-safe Admin surface for the two Phase E
special-record families, so that a wrong source fact can be corrected without touching identity, a
fact that should never have been published can be suppressed without a destructive `DELETE` and
cannot be resurrected by any importer or rebuild path, a genuinely manual record can be created
under `manual_admin_edit` provenance, and a suppressed record disappears from every public read
model while staying fully visible in admin and audit history.

### Current-state findings

**Family A — first-kick goal (`player_achievements`, migration 053).** Source
`wikipedia_first_kick_goal`; `source_record_id` is `fkg-NNN`, assigned in the **tracked, committed**
manifest `data/records/first-kick-goal-ids.csv`, under
`player_achievements_source_uq UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (source_id, source_record_id)`. Importer
`tools/records/import-first-kick-goal.ts` (TypeScript) scopes ownership by
`achievement_type AND source_id`, aborts via `ReloadAbort` before writing anything in the owned
scope, and deletes on retirement only behind `--accept-retirement`. It is a `LINK_TARGET_TABLE`, so
unlinked rows reach `/admin/player-links`.

**Family B — after the siren (`after_siren_kicks`, migration 089).** Source
`wikipedia_after_siren_kicks`; `source_record_id` is the tracked artefact's `event_key`, under the
same `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT` discipline. Loader `tools/migration/after_siren.py` upserts on
`(source_id, event_key)` and rewrites a column only when it differs. It is **not** a
`LINK_TARGET_TABLE`, so an unlinked after-siren row has no admin queue anywhere.

**Neither family lacks stable identity.** That stop condition is **not triggered**.

**Neither table has any correction, lifecycle or override seam today.**
`data_overrides.entity_type` (073, widened by 095/096/097/098/101) admits neither, and neither table
carries `status`, `status_reason` or `updated_at`.

**Three destruction paths exist, not one.** The first-kick retirement `DELETE`
(`import-first-kick-goal.ts`); the after-siren
`DELETE FROM after_siren_kicks WHERE source_id = %s AND NOT (source_record_id = ANY(%s))`
(`tools/migration/after_siren.py:992`, broader and less guarded — no acknowledgement flag); and
**`src/db/queries/match-admin.ts:401`**, `DELETE FROM player_achievements WHERE match_id = $1`,
which runs when an admin deletes a match and is outside both importers and outside every
reload-survival mechanism.

**Three apparently-manual fields are actually derived** and are therefore classified read-only
rather than designed around — this stop condition **was triggered and is resolved in the plan**:
`link_status_value` / `candidate_count` are owned by the link pipeline and bound by the
`*_link_ck` CHECKs on both tables; `player_achievements.match_id` is *"resolved by career game
position (1 + kickless_matches_before_first_kick), never by season/round/club lookup"* (053's own
column comment), so the real correction is to `kickless_matches_before_first_kick`; and
`after_siren_kicks.club_id` is taken from the resolved match wherever there is one
(`after_siren.py:554-559`), so it is editable only on a match-less row.

**Nothing is retired from `/admin/data-editor`.** A repository search for
`achievement|first_kick|firstKick|siren` under `src/app/admin/**` returns only the player-link queue
label and two unrelated Hall-of-Fame form fields. Unlike P5, P4 takes over no existing action.

**Promotion inventory is incomplete for both tables.** `after_siren_kicks` does not appear in
`tools/db/promotion-inventory.ts` at all — the file's own `unclassified` problem class plus umbrella
R-3 make that a stop-before-merge. `player_achievements` appears only as a
`player_link_resolutions.target_id` target classified `identity: 'none'`, whose remediation text
(*"nothing in the tree carries an external key for one of their rows"*) is **now factually wrong for
this table**: the tracked `fkg-NNN` manifest is exactly such a key.

**`privileges.sql` is subtractive and hand-typed for `afldb_auth`.** The admin pages read both
tables on the auth pool, so both need an explicit `afldb_auth` SELECT entry in the same change
(umbrella R-2). This is the umbrella's own recorded class of defect — an admin page reading an
operational table on the wrong pool, which only a real role catches.

### Design summary

Reuses the `AFLDB-ISSUE-165` two-layer model, which matches this grain genuinely: lifecycle columns
(`status IN ('active','void')`, mandatory `status_reason` on void, `updated_at` as the
compare-and-swap column) are the cheap read-path cache that survives an ordinary scoped reload for
free, and the durable record is a `data_overrides` row replayed by `replay_admin_overrides` with
three field groups — `lifecycle` (warn-and-retain when the target row is absent), `correction`
(fail closed), `record` (re-create then restore, fail closed). `entity_key` is
`'<sources.key>:<source_record_id>'` for both families, which is **simpler** than ISSUE-165's shapes
because both tables already carry a real tracked source record id on every row.

**Adds no new table** (Phase E §12 forbids a parallel records table) and **no `data_overrides`
structural change** — `field_group` + `override_values` already carry the suppress operation.
Capabilities follow the ISSUE-165 precedent: `data.records.read` (Admin-and-up),
`data.records.edit` (Super Admin only). Route is `/admin/records` with per-family subroutes, per
ISSUE-155 §12 verbatim. The "delete" control is presented as **Suppress record**; physical deletion
stays operator CLI repair only.

### Operator decisions — all four recorded 2026-09-13, none open

- **D-1 — APPROVED, EXCLUDE.** Family/father-son is outside ISSUE-167 entirely; P4 is limited to
  first-kick goal and after-the-siren. The evidence: ISSUE-156's route parenthetical implied three
  domains, but the authoritative ISSUE-155 §12 names two and closes *"No other record family is added
  merely because it is manually curated."* Migration 088 adds no table — it constrains
  `father_son_selections`, a migration 006 draft-relationships table with plain nullable
  `source_record_id text UNIQUE`, no provenance quartet and two independent person links: materially
  weaker identity, in P3b/P9 territory. The `/records/family` namespace is left unclaimed.
- **D-2 — APPROVED, DEFER.** P4 may display current linkage state but must **not** create another
  player-link queue or authority, and must not collide with the uncommitted `AFLDB-ISSUE-164`.
  `LINK_TARGET_TABLES` is **not** modified. The admin row shows `link_status_value`,
  `candidate_count` and the resolved player read-only, so the gap stays visible rather than silent.
- **D-3 — APPROVED WITH MODIFICATION: one durable authority, two replay adapters.** `data_overrides`
  remains the sole durable authority. After-siren uses the existing Python `common.py` replay
  contract; `tools/records/import-first-kick-goal.ts` gets an explicit TypeScript replay adapter
  implementing the same `lifecycle`/`correction`/`record` semantics; **both adapters are pinned by
  parity/contract tests**; **replay must be atomic with the owning importer**; first-kick is not
  ported to Python merely to share `common.py`; no second authority table or mechanism is introduced.
  The modification draws the right line — *one authority* is a property of the durable store and the
  semantics, not of the implementation language, and two adapters over one authority is not two
  authorities provided the semantics are pinned.
- **D-4 — APPROVED, TWO capabilities.** `data.specialRecords.read` (Admin + Super Admin) and
  `data.specialRecords.edit` (Super Admin). Create, correct, void, suppress, reinstate and replace
  are all writes under `.edit`; there is **no separate `.suppress`**. This supersedes ISSUE-156 §2's
  written `data.records.edit` / `.suppress`: both writes would be Super-Admin-only, so a split
  separates nobody, and ISSUE-165 and ISSUE-160 D-6 both refused the extra capability on the same
  reasoning. The `specialRecords` segment also avoids colliding conceptually with
  `src/db/queries/records.ts`, which in this codebase means computed leaderboards and nothing stored
  — the naming hazard migration 053 called out at `:21-23`.

### D-3 atomicity — structurally feasible, proven from source

D-3's escape clause (*"if the current TypeScript importer cannot replay overrides atomically within
its existing transaction structure, STOP and report rather than weakening the contract"*) is **NOT
invoked**. Evidence from `tools/records/import-first-kick-goal.ts`:

- `postgres(dsn, { max: 1, onnotice: () => {} })` at `:740` — a single pooled connection, so there
  is no second implicit session to diverge.
- `await sql.begin(async (tx) => { … })` opens at `:888` and closes at `:1353`. **One transaction
  wraps the entire apply phase**: the `import_batches` insert (`:892-896`), every preflight
  `ReloadAbort` (`:916, :936, :947, :1136`), the retirement `DELETE` and all upserts
  (`:1174-1301`), the `data_issues` refiling (`:1309-1336`) and the batch completion
  (`:1339-1344`).
- `ReloadAbort` is the documented ISSUE-078 contract at `:94-98` — raised *before anything in the
  owned scope is written*, so the surrounding transaction rolls back untouched.
- `await sql.end({ timeout: 5 })` sits in a `finally` **outside** `begin` (`:1354-1356`), so
  connection teardown commits nothing.
- `rowIds`, the stable-key→surviving-row-id map, is already in scope at `:1308-1319`.

A TypeScript adapter placed on that same `tx` handle between the upsert phase (`:1301`) and the
`data_issues` refiling (`:1309`) is therefore atomic **by construction**: it sees the same
uncommitted state, has the key→id map it needs, and can throw `ReloadAbort` to roll everything back.
**No change to the transaction structure is required and nothing is weakened.**

Two supporting facts. First, **the replay contract is read-only against `data_overrides`** — every
one of `common.py`'s override references is a `FROM data_overrides` read; none writes, updates or
deletes one. That matches migration 073's `GRANT SELECT ON data_overrides TO afldb_import` and its
comment *"SELECT only: `data_overrides` is not importer-owned"* (`073:29-38`). Neither adapter may
write it, including the `lifecycle` warn-and-retain branch, whose whole point is that it does not
delete the override. Second, the `record` group's INSERT into `player_achievements` is already
covered by `grant_import_write` (`053:152`), so the replay needs no privilege change.

Gate **G-5** is revised accordingly — it no longer asks whether `rebuild-test.ts` can sequence a
subprocess call, but requires the adapter to run on the importer's own `tx` with a RED-then-GREEN
atomicity test — and a new gate **G-9** covers the adapter parity suite.

### Probe environment — corrections recorded

Corrected against the actual run, so the earlier wording is not re-derived:

- **Worktrees do not carry their own `.env`.** Use the established shared env at
  `D:\dev\afldb\.env`.
- **Do not hard-code port 55432.** That was one historical tunnel arrangement, not a property of
  `afldb_test`. Take the port from the configured DSN.
- **Safety contract:** a `_test` database name **plus** a `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` host **plus** a
  live listener on the configured local port. Proven endpoint: `127.0.0.1:5432/afldb_test`.
- **PowerShell scratch-SQL generation must write UTF-8 without BOM** —
  `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText(path, sql, [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))`. `Out-File`
  and `Set-Content` add a BOM or the ANSI codepage, and psql fails on a BOM before the first
  statement.
- **Retain** `--single-transaction`, `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, `-X` and `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`.

### Stop conditions at end of planning

Not triggered: missing stable identity; general player merge or fixture rekey required; provenance
cannot distinguish source-owned from manual (it can — `source_id`, and `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT`
forces a manual row to carry a real source); migration conflict with `main`; privileges/promotion
cannot be made fail-closed. **Also not triggered:** suppression surviving importer and rebuild —
D-3 is settled and its atomicity requirement is proven structurally feasible from source (above), so
the Phase E stop condition and D-3's own STOP clause both stand down. **Triggered and resolved in
the plan:** an apparently manual field is actually derived elsewhere — three of them, now classified
read-only. No stop condition remains open.

Full evidence is `issues/closed/AFLDB-ISSUE-167.md` §22. The checkpoint was re-proven before anything was edited:

`data.specialRecords.read` is declared; `.edit` is declared at Stage 6 beside its first guarded
mutation. `tests/auth.test.ts:1040-1046` fails any capability declared but awaited by no

own terms. The contradiction was raised before implementation rather than worked around. **D-4's

**The collision rule was defined rather than assumed.** §8.4's literal reading — two rows resolving
to one `entity_key` — is structurally unreachable: the first-colon split is injective and both tables
carry `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (source_id, source_record_id)`. What *is* reachable is two overrides
on one key, since `data_overrides_uq` is `(entity_type, entity_key, field_group)`. Both adapters
therefore fail closed when a **`record`** override — which owns the whole row including its `status` —
shares a key with any second authority, and deliberately do **not** treat `correction` + `lifecycle`
as a collision, because those own disjoint fields and replay in a defined order. Both halves are
corpus cases.

**Both importer refusals implemented, neither reachable past a flag.** `--accept-retirement`
authorises losing a durable *reference* and `--allow-link-loss` a *link decision*; neither is
authority to destroy the row a lifecycle or correction decision is attached to, because a

row, which carries a different `source_id` and is outside every source-owned retirement scope.

write is guarded by `IS DISTINCT FROM` over the tuple it would assign. `hall_of_fame`'s replay is
unguarded, which on an ordinary reload would bump `updated_at` on every override-bearing row every
run — the lifecycle columns are Layer 1 and already carry the decision — and invalidate a concurrent
administrator's compare-and-swap for no actual change. `updated_at` is the CAS column Stage 6 depends
on. **Flagged for Stage 6:** the replay still sets `updated_at` when a value genuinely changes, which
is correct, so Stage 6's CAS contract should state that a reload re-asserting a decision can
legitimately invalidate an in-flight edit.

### Stage 6 — the mutations, the atomic audit, CAS and bounded revalidation — PASS (2026-09-14)

**Checkpoint before anything was edited.** Worktree clean; branch, HEAD and upstream all
`c5a0df7a64663bfe8dbfbeb56d65e0a5879defc0`; migration **102 applied and checksum-clean** on
`afldb_test` (`migrate.ts --status --target test` → `0 pending`; the runner's drift check runs
before the status branch, so a clean status run is the proof) and **unedited** (one commit,
`8d9ac74`; sha256 `dec12080…f5f173`); target proven `127.0.0.1:5432/afldb_test`, loopback, live
listener. Mutations ran as **`afldb_import`**, proven by `createImportRoleParityHarness` before a
row was written — not as the database owner, which can do anything.

**The capability.** `data.specialRecords.edit` is declared `SUPER_ADMIN_ONLY` in
`src/lib/auth/capabilities.ts` **in the same change as its first guarded mutation** (D-4 as
clarified by runbook §9.1), with the `EQUIVALENT_ROLE_GUARD` entry `'requireSuperAdmin'` beside
it. `tests/auth.test.ts` was not weakened and no declared-ahead-of-enforcement exemption was
added. Final role matrix, asserted: Contributor neither; Admin `.read` only (including an Admin
carrying `can_manage_admins`); Super Admin both.

**The write boundary is the server, not the button.** One `'use server'` module,
`src/app/admin/records/actions.ts`, holds all ten mutations, and every one of them asserts
`await requireCapability('data.specialRecords.edit')` **before it awaits anything else** —
which is what `tests/auth.test.ts`'s ISSUE-158 contract detects. The two `/new` routes and
`/admin/records/revalidate` take the same capability. The five read routes keep `.read`; an
Admin sees every record, its provenance and its whole history, and no mutation control — and a
direct POST still fails at the guard.

**One mutation contract.** `runSpecialRecordEdit()` does lock → compare-and-swap on
`updated_at` → precheck → apply → `data_overrides` → `data_edits`, in one `afldb_import`
transaction. Every refusal reachable before the first write RETURNS; every refusal after it
THROWS (`RollbackRefusal`), because `postgres.js` commits when the `begin()` callback resolves —
returning past the first write would commit a half-done, unaudited mutation while reporting
failure.

**What a correction may touch is not a judgement call.** The correctable columns are asserted
**exactly equal, both directions, to the Stage 4 replay adapter's own `COLUMNS` lists** (12 for
`player_achievements`, 21 for `after_siren_kicks`), which are in turn §3.4's amendable
classification. A column the replay cannot carry would be silently reverted by the next rebuild;
a replay column the surface cannot reach would be an amendable field with no way to amend it.
Every derived, link and identity field is refused twice — excluded by the typed parameter, and
refused again at run time so a crafted POST naming `matchId`, `playerId`, `clubId`,
`linkStatus`, `candidateCount` or `sourceRecordId` gets a sentence rather than silence.

**Family B's coupled fields are checked as a combination.** New pure module
`src/lib/special-records/after-siren-rules.ts` transcribes migration 089's `_effect_ck`,
`_regulation_ck`, `_match_ck` and `_points_ck`, and is used in three places and implemented
once: the correction panel as the operator types, the mutation before any SQL is issued, and the
CHECK constraints inside the same transaction. The row is validated **as it will stand once the
delta lands**, never field by field, because three of the four constraints are broken by a
*combination*. No refusal ever names a constraint — asserted.

**Suppress / reinstate / replace / create.** The button reads *"Suppress record"*; the reason is
mandatory; the row is kept so its `data_edits` history stays resolvable through the next
promotion's lineage remap. Reinstate appends a second audit row and erases nothing. Replace is
suppress + manual create **in one transaction**, cross-referenced by natural key
(`replaces_key` / `replaced_by_key`) and sharing one `replacement_id` across both audit rows —
never an identity edit, never a delete-and-reinsert under the original source identity. Manual
creation mints `manual_admin_edit` + `<family>:<uuid>` and carries the player and the match as
**natural identities** (`player_identity`, `match_key`), which is what lets a rebuild resolve
them back after every id has been renumbered. A source-owned row's decisions are
`correction` + `lifecycle`; a manual row's live inside its single `record` payload, because
`record` + anything is the collision the replay fails the whole reload closed on —
`refuseOverrideCollision()` refuses it at mutation time so an administrator meets a sentence now
rather than an operator meeting a refused rebuild months later.

**The third destruction path is closed.** `DELETE FROM player_achievements WHERE match_id = $1`
is **gone** from `src/db/queries/match-admin.ts`. Both families are inspected before anything
destructive runs, and a match carrying either is refused by name, in the shape the Brownlow
refusal already established — including when the curated record is already **suppressed**,
because suppression says the record should never have existed, not that the row may be
destroyed. `after_siren_kicks.match_id` was never deleted there at all: migration 089 declares
it `REFERENCES matches(id)` with no `ON DELETE` clause, so the same delete had been raising a
raw foreign-key violation, which is not control flow a Data Editor user can act on.

**Two design contradictions found against current source, both resolved by NARROWING.** Neither
weakens the authority, audit, CAS or replay contracts.

- **F-1 — `player_achievements.match_id` is not derived from what §3.4.1 says it is.** Migration
  `053:103-105` says *"resolved by career game position (1 + kickless_matches_before_first_kick),
  never by season/round/club lookup"*. `tools/records/import-first-kick-goal.ts:797-808` does the
  opposite and says so: *"The match is the one the SOURCE says it happened in — the player's game
  in that season at that round — not one inferred from career position"*, with Brent Harvey's
  1996 debut as the recorded reason; `findMatchForRound(sql, playerId, season, roundRaw)` at
  `:607-647` is the real resolver. §10.3's consequential sentence (*"editing
  `kickless_matches_before_first_kick` re-derives `match_id`, and the form says so"*) is wrong on
  both halves. **`match_id` stays derived and never editable**, exactly as §3.4.1 requires; what
  changed is that a correction does **not** re-derive it, because the replay carries a correction
  as a delta over the amendable columns and touches no link column — so a re-derived link would
  be state a rebuild cannot reproduce. Leaving it alone is the only outcome identical before and
  after a rebuild, and the detail page and correction panel say so. No migration is edited: 102
  is immutable and 053's comment is a pre-existing documentation defect in a migration that has
  already run.
- **F-2 — a manually created record carries no club link, by construction.** The replay's
  `record` INSERT sets no club column, so a manual row created with a `club_id` would not be the
  row a rebuild reconstructs — which the Stage 6 contract forbids outright. The creator therefore
  sets none; the club travels as `club_name_raw`, which is in the replay's column list and is
  what every public read already falls back to (`COALESCE(cl.name, a.club_name_raw)`). Giving
  manual records a durable club identity is a change to **both** replay adapters and their shared
  parity corpus — Stage 4 work, outside Stage 6's contract — and is recorded as a follow-up
  candidate.

**Four Stage 3 source-contract assertions were about a read-only stage, not about the design,
and were replaced by the precise form of the same rule** rather than deleted: *"five routes and
no `/new`"* → the five read routes and the two creation routes exactly; *"every route enforces
`.read`"* → read routes `.read`, creation routes the narrower `.edit`; *"no edit seam, no
`'use server'` anywhere"* → exactly one `'use server'` module and every guard in it `.edit`; *"no
control on a detail page"* → no control **named after** a derived, link or identity field
anywhere, with `matchId`/`playerId` admitted only in a creation field set; *"no `UPDATE
player_achievements`"* → no statement anywhere in the domain **assigns** a link column; *"no
`status = 'active'`"* → every occurrence is a `SET` assignment, none is a filter, and the
assertion fails vacuously if the assignment disappears. No regression coverage was deleted,
skipped, disabled or weakened.

**Two RED assertions were tightened rather than satisfied**, and the distinction is recorded
because it matters: `not.toContain('revalidatePath')` failed on the action module's own header
sentence *explaining* that it never calls it, and the match-admin assertion failed on the
refusal's own comment *quoting* the statement it replaced. Both now read code rather than
prose — a call, not a mention; a comment-stripped source, not the raw file.

**RED → GREEN.** `tests/auth.test.ts` 5 failed / 149 passed → **155 passed**;
`tests/special-records-admin.test.ts` 22 → **42 passed**;
`tests/integration/admin-special-records.test.ts` 14 → **33 passed** (as `afldb_import`);
