## AFLDB-ISSUE-207 — Numeric operator ownership crossing between having-clause threshold and margin filter

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator). Severity was high — silent wrong answer, 281 known corpus rows. Area: deterministic NL search parser (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`, `src/search/nl/plan.ts`). Implementation commit `4ecdd77a`, parser v55, unmerged on `sonnet/issue-207-numeric-operator-ownership`.
- **Baseline:** `51e94370` (main), parser v54, worktree `sonnet/issue-207-numeric-operator-ownership`. Follow-on item (1) of `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md`'s six proposals.
- **Root cause (source-verified):** `extractHavingClause` (`parser.ts`, around the wins/losses/draws/games loop) builds a `±20`-character `window` around the matched result noun, then searches `COMPARE_OP_WORDS` (`vocab.ts`) against the *entire* window for an operator word. On a short question this window reaches past the noun's own number across `by ... points` into the adjacent margin clause and can match ITS operator word (e.g. "over" in "by over 50 points"), which is then claimed and stripped for the wins/losses threshold. `extractMatchFilter` then sees a bare margin number with no operator word left and falls back to its own default (`gte`) — the two clauses' comparators end up silently swapped. A second, independent mechanism produces the same symptom even when the window is wide enough to contain both clauses' operator words intact: `COMPARE_OP_WORDS` is tested in a **fixed vocabulary order**, not leftmost-in-text order (e.g. `at least` is listed before `more than`), so "more than 7 wins by at least 50 points" matched `at least` (belonging to the margin clause, listed earlier) for the wins threshold instead of `more than` (belonging to the wins clause itself, listed later), even though "more than" appears first in the sentence. Both fields still passed validation, so this scored `clean` under ISSUE-206's grain/metric-only checks — 281 corpus rows verified as confirmed silent wrong answers, not merely a display difference.
- **Fix:** the operator search inside `extractHavingClause` is now bounded to `window.slice(0, countEnd)` — the text up to and including the count this clause already matched, never past it. Every `COMPARE_OP_WORDS` phrase governs a number that follows it immediately (including the `over`/`under` entries' own digit lookahead), so a genuine operator for this clause can never sit to the right of its own count; this eliminates both the character-window spillover and the fixed-list-order precedence bug in one change, since the competing clause's operator word is no longer present in the searched substring at all. `extractMatchFilter` itself is untouched. No vocabulary was added; no parser stage was reordered; no default changed. `PARSER_VERSION` 54 → 55 (`plan.ts`).
- **Scope note (pre-existing, separate gap, NOT fixed here):** `extractMatchFilter`'s regex has no form for a trailing "or more"/"or fewer" after the margin number ("by 50 or more points" declines today with no `matchFilter` match — `points` left unconsumed). Confirmed via direct parser probe before and after the fix: identical decline behaviour both times, unaffected by this change. Documented per ISSUE-207's scope boundary; not a tracked issue on its own (not requested, and no corpus evidence of its real-world frequency was gathered).
- **RED evidence:** 11 new regression tests added to `tests/nl-parser.test.ts` under `describe('AFLDB-ISSUE-207: ...')`, covering all four required wording families plus `over`/`over`, `fewer than`/`at least`, two no-margin controls, two already-declining controls, and the documented out-of-scope gap. Run against the reverted (pre-fix) operator-search line: **4 of 11 failed for the exact predicted reason** (`teams with 7 or more wins by over 50 points` → havingClause `op: 'gt'` instead of `'gte'`; `more than 7 wins by at least 50 points` → havingClause `op: 'gte'` instead of `'gt'`; `7 or more losses by over 50 points` and `fewer than 7 losses by at least 50 points` likewise), 7 passed as pre-existing controls. The existing `teams to lose 5 times by more than 100 points` regression (added under ISSUE-188) was also strengthened with an explicit `matchFilter` assertion (`loss_margin`, `gt`, `100`) per this issue's requirement that field-blind checks are insufficient.
- **Focused validation (this workstation, worktree-scoped `npm ci` — no shared checkout touched):** `npx vitest run tests/nl-parser.test.ts` → **457/457 passed**; `npx vitest run tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` → **53/53 passed**; `npm run typecheck` → clean (`next typegen` + `tsc --noEmit`, 0 errors). A disposable direct-parser probe (deleted after use, not committed) confirmed all 12 of the issue's example phrasings resolve to the intended operator pairing after the fix, with zero change to the two already-declining controls and the one documented out-of-scope gap.
- **Operator validation (streamanator):** frozen V5 stable-corpus rerun (`/home/arm/nl-stress-corpus-v5.csv`, parser v55) = **12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed**, no regression. ISSUE-206 exploratory 281-row family: direct structured-plan comparison between the retained pre-fix (v54, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v1-validation/results.jsonl`) and post-fix (v55, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v55-validation/results.jsonl`) runs (both 29,030 rows / 29,030 unique IDs) found exactly **281 changed plans**, all `havingClause.op: "gt" -> "gte"` paired with `matchFilter.op: "gte" -> "gt"` — the intended pairing — and no other field changed anywhere in the 29,030-row corpus (zero collateral movement). The aggregate exploratory scorer total was unchanged (27530 scored / 10874 clean / 15275 soft / 1381 failed), as expected, since that scorer does not assert comparator fields; the field-level diff is the decisive evidence, not the scorer's aggregate counts. Full evidence in `AFLDB-ISSUE-207.md`.
- **Resolution:** both required checks confirmed the fix with zero collateral movement. Resolved 2026-09-16. Known out-of-scope gap (undisturbed): `extractMatchFilter` has no form for trailing "by 50 or more/fewer points" — pre-existing, not introduced by this fix, not opened as a separate issue (no corpus evidence of real-world frequency gathered).

## AFLDB-ISSUE-208 — Club-role ownership: `extractClubs`'s lookback window is not anchored to the nearest preposition

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator). Severity was high — silent loss of the subject club, 251 known corpus rows (134 `after_siren`, 117 `team_checkpoint_collision`). Area: deterministic NL search parser (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`, `src/search/nl/plan.ts`). Implementation commit `70b72df`, parser v56, unmerged on `sonnet/issue-208-club-role-ownership`.
- **Baseline:** `ca17277f` (main), parser v55, worktree `sonnet/issue-208-club-role-ownership`. Follow-on item (2) of `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md`'s six proposals, directly from that issue's final triage.
- **Root cause (source-verified, both families reconcile to one mechanism):** `extractClubs` (`parser.ts`) decided each club mention's role by testing `AGAINST_PREPOSITION.test(before)`, where `before` was a fixed 20-character slice of text preceding the mention — i.e. "does an against-like token (`against`/`versus`/`vs`/`v`/`to`/`over`) exist ANYWHERE in this window", not "what actually governs this mention". Two independent-looking defect families both trace to that one broad test:
  - **Family A (134 rows, "after-siren" wording):** "after the siren **to** win **for** North Melbourne" — "for" is the word immediately before the club and is the true governor, but the fixed window also reached back far enough to contain the earlier, unrelated "to" (from "to win"), and `AGAINST_PREPOSITION.test` cannot tell the two apart since it only asks whether the pattern matches anywhere in the slice. The club was wrongly marked `governedAgainst`, so it was assigned `clubAgainst` and `clubFor` came out `undefined` (intended: `clubFor = Club`, `clubAgainst = absent`).
  - **Family B (117 rows, leading-opponent wording):** "**Against** Fremantle, ... what was **Melbourne**'s largest lead ..." — `extractClubs` finds and strips club mentions from a mutable working copy of the text one at a time (`stripMatch`, which also collapses whitespace). Once "Fremantle" was spliced out, Melbourne's own 20-character lookback window shrank enough to newly contain "against" — a word that governed the *already-consumed* Fremantle mention, not Melbourne. Melbourne was wrongly marked `governedAgainst` too, so BOTH mentions ended up in the `clubAgainst` bucket, `clubAgainst` kept only the first (Fremantle), and `clubFor` came out `undefined` (intended: `clubFor = Melbourne`, `clubAgainst = Fremantle`).
  - Confirms `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md`'s diagnosis (independently re-derived from current source, not taken on trust): one shared mechanism — a "does this window contain a token" test standing in for "what is the nearest governing phrase" — with the mutation of the working copy as the specific reason Family B's window can absorb an unrelated, already-resolved club's preposition.
- **Fix:** a new `nearestGoverningPreposition(before)` helper (`parser.ts`) replaces the window-existence test with a window-anchored one: it strips at most one trailing determiner (`the`/`a`/`an`) then checks whether `AGAINST_PREPOSITION`/`FOR_PREPOSITION` matches at the very END of the preceding text (`${source}$`), i.e. whether that preposition is the token immediately governing the mention — not merely present somewhere earlier in the window. `extractClubs` also now computes `before` from the text it was originally handed (`text`, via the same `phrasePosition` offset already used for word-order tiebreaking) instead of from the internally mutated `working` copy, so a later club's role decision can no longer be disturbed by an earlier club having been spliced out. This single change fixes both families: Family A because "for" (immediately adjacent) now wins over the more distant, no-longer-relevant "to"; Family B because the check no longer depends on what `stripMatch` has or hasn't removed yet. No vocabulary was added, no parser stage was reordered, and the unordered `scope.matchup` ("A versus B") detection (a separate code path in the same function, keyed on the literal text between two mentions) was not touched. `PARSER_VERSION` 55 → 56 (`plan.ts`).
- **Scope note (adjacent, NOT touched):** `assignCrossDomainClubs` (`parser.ts`, AFLDB-ISSUE-152 Phase F cross-domain played/coached role assignment) contains its own, structurally similar `AGAINST_PREPOSITION.test(scanText.slice(at - 20, at))` window check to refuse an opponent-governed club. It was not analysed for the same defect shape and was not changed — out of scope for ISSUE-208, which is limited to `extractClubs`. Flagged here for a future, separately-scoped look, not opened as a tracked issue (no corpus evidence gathered for it).
- **RED evidence:** 15 new regression tests added to `tests/nl-parser.test.ts` under `describe('AFLDB-ISSUE-208: ...')` (3 Family-A defect rows + 1 explicit-opponent control + 3 Family-B defect rows + 8 unaffected controls: plain `against`/`versus`/`vs`/`v`, a genuine `to`/`over` opponent governor, a single ungoverned club defaulting to the subject side, and a trailing `for` still governing the subject). Run against the reverted (pre-fix) lookback line: **exactly the 7 rows tied to the diagnosed mechanism failed** (all with the subject club's `scope.clubFor` coming back `undefined`, matching the predicted failure mode precisely), and all 8 unaffected controls stayed green under the unfixed code — confirming the new tests fail for the diagnosed reason, not an unrelated one, before any fix was applied. Fix reapplied: 15/15 pass.
- **Focused validation (this workstation, worktree-scoped `npm ci` — no shared checkout touched):** `npx vitest run tests/nl-parser.test.ts` → **472/472 passed**; `npx vitest run tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` → **53/53 passed**; `npm run typecheck` → clean (`next typegen` + `tsc --noEmit`, 0 errors). Additional DB-free adjacent-suite check (not required by the issue, run for extra collateral-regression confidence): `nl-plan.test.ts`, `nl-semantic-mapping.test.ts`, `nl-regression-corpus.test.ts`, `nl-audit-acceptance.test.ts`, `query-intent.test.ts` → 574/574 passed, no collateral movement.
- **Operator validation (streamanator, commit `70b72df`, `PARSER_VERSION` 56):** frozen V5 stable-corpus rerun (`/home/arm/nl-stress-corpus-v5.csv`) = **12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed**, no regression. ISSUE-206 exploratory 251-row family: direct structured-plan comparison between the retained pre-fix (v55, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v55-validation/results.jsonl`) and post-fix (v56, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v56-validation/results.jsonl`) runs (both 29,030 rows / 29,030 unique IDs) found exactly **251 changed plans** — 134 `after_siren` + 117 `team_checkpoint_collision`, matching AFLDB-ISSUE-206's family split exactly — with no other structured-plan field changed anywhere in the corpus (zero collateral movement). Family A representative ("... to win for North Melbourne between 2005 and 2015"): `clubAgainst=North Melbourne/clubFor=absent` → `clubFor=North Melbourne/clubAgainst=absent`. Family B representative ("Against Fremantle, what was Melbourne's largest lead ... since 2000"): `clubAgainst=Fremantle/clubFor=absent` → `clubAgainst=Fremantle/clubFor=Melbourne`. Aggregate exploratory scorer totals moved exactly as expected: pre-fix v55 27530 scored/1500 audit-required/10874 clean/15275 soft/1381 failed (97 diagnostic groups) → post-fix v56 27530 scored/1500 audit-required/**11125 clean**/15275 soft/**1130 failed** (95 diagnostic groups) — clean +251, soft 0, failed −251. The remaining 1130 hard failures are the already-audited ISSUE-206 corpus/scorer artifacts (496 symmetric-versus, 283 achievement-summary aggregation, 351 Gary Ablett identity), out of scope here.
- **Resolution:** both required checks confirmed the fix with zero collateral movement, clearing all 251 confirmed parser-defect hard failures. Resolved 2026-09-17. Known out-of-scope, undisturbed finding: `assignCrossDomainClubs` (`parser.ts`) contains a structurally similar fixed-window `AGAINST_PREPOSITION.test` check for its played/coached opponent refusal; not analysed for the same defect shape, not fixed, no separate issue opened for it yet. Full evidence in `AFLDB-ISSUE-208.md`.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-209 — Head-to-head "has more wins" wording answered with a generic record instead of naming the leader

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator). Severity was medium-high — wrong answer shape (not numerically wrong; both clubs' true counts are still returned), 173 known corpus rows per ISSUE-206's direct estimate, 199 validated. Area: deterministic NL search parser (`src/search/nl/semantic-intents.ts`, `src/search/nl/plan.ts`). Implementation commit `f2e067f`, parser v57, unmerged on `sonnet/issue-209-head-to-head-more-wins`.
- **Baseline:** current clean `main` after ISSUE-208, parser v56, worktree `sonnet/issue-209-head-to-head-more-wins`. Follow-on item (3) of `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md`'s six proposals.
- **Root cause (source-verified):** `extractHeadToHeadCue` (`semantic-intents.ts`) tries an ordered list of `[pattern, kind]` families and returns on the first match. Its `compare_wins` entry recognized only past-tense `who has/who's/who/which team has won more`. Present-tense "**has more wins** ... head to head" did not match, so the loop fell through to the generic `/\bhead[- ]to[- ]head.../` → `record` pattern, which matches unconditionally on any "head to head" mention. `tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus.mjs`'s `head_to_head` template index 2 ("Which of A and B has more wins head to head [temporal]") is the entire source of the corpus family — verified 100% of the wording, no "the most"/"between"/"against the other" variant exists in the generator.
- **Fix:** two `extractHeadToHeadCue` family-list entries, both checked before the generic record families: a new `/\b(?:has|have)\s+(?:more|the most)\s+wins\s+head[- ]to[- ]head\b/` → `compare_wins`, and the existing "won more" entry extended to optionally absorb a trailing "head to head" (`(?:\s+head[- ]to[- ]head)?`), fixing a related atomic-consumption gap found during RED reconciliation. Neither match spans the club-name tokens, so `extractClubs` still resolves the two real clubs afterwards; the comparison only commits once that two-club resolution succeeds — the existing safety net against a lone "most wins" ranking question being misread. `PARSER_VERSION` 56 → 57.
- **Scope note (investigated, NOT fixed here):** "has more wins between A and B" and "has more wins against the other" were tried in the RED matrix and found to fail via a different mechanism — `extractClubSeasonMetric`'s "most wins" club_season ranking cue (`parser.ts`) claims bare "wins" first and declines, never reaching `extractHeadToHeadCue` at all. Not represented in the actual 173-row corpus. Fixing it would mean changing club_season cue-ownership logic, a different subsystem; left undone and documented, not opened as its own issue.
- **RED evidence:** regression tests added to `tests/nl-semantic-mapping.test.ts` under a new `AFLDB-ISSUE-209:` `it.each` block, varied club pairs. Initial run: 177 tests, 168 passed, 9 failed. That run exposed two proposed assertions as invalid before implementation: a generic-record control ("Show the head-to-head record between Richmond and Carlton") was itself pre-existing unsupported behaviour (`unsupportedTerms = ["show between"]`), and a proposed "already-supported" control ("Which team has won more head to head, Carlton or Richmond?") was also pre-existing unsupported — the old "won more" cue left a trailing "head to head" unconsumed, causing a decline. Both were reconciled (the record control removed; the won-more-head-to-head case folded into the fix as the same atomic-consumption defect) rather than used to broaden the fix. Final matrix: 8 of 9 comparison rows failed for the predicted reason pre-fix, 1 pre-existing control passed.
- **Focused validation (this workstation):** `npx vitest run tests/nl-semantic-mapping.test.ts` → **174/174 passed**; `npx vitest run tests/nl-parser.test.ts` → **472/472 passed**; `npx vitest run tests/nl-describe.test.ts` → **89/89 passed**; `npx vitest run tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` → **53/53 passed** (788/788 total); `npm run typecheck` → clean (`next typegen` + `tsc --noEmit`, 0 errors). Zero regressions among pre-existing head-to-head tests.
- **Operator validation (streamanator, commit `f2e067f`, `PARSER_VERSION` 57):** frozen V5 stable-corpus rerun (`/home/arm/nl-stress-corpus-v5.csv`) = **12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed**, no regression. ISSUE-206 exploratory corpus: direct structured-plan comparison between retained pre-fix (v56, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v56-validation/results.jsonl`) and post-fix (v57, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v57-validation/results.jsonl`) runs (both 29,030 rows / 29,030 unique IDs) found exactly **199 changed plans**, all `headToHead.kind: record -> compare_wins` in the same "has more wins head to head" wording family, zero collateral movement elsewhere. 173 of the 199 changed only `headToHead.kind`; the remaining 26 also contained a trailing `between YEAR and YEAR` clause and, under v56, had additionally been malformed by `extractHavingClause` misreading the unconsumed "wins" noun plus the end year as a grouped threshold (`seasonMax` truncated to `seasonMin`, spurious `havingClause: {metric: wins, op: gte, value: <endYear>}`); under v57 the new pattern consumes "wins" atomically as part of the cue, so that misreading no longer occurs and the full season range parses correctly — a direct side effect of the one fix, not a second correction (`extractHavingClause`/`extractMatchFilter` untouched). Independent classification of the 26-row subset: `between-year-range: 26, other: 0`. **The validated affected surface is 199 rows, not ISSUE-206's original 173-row estimate** — both figures share one root cause and one fix, but ISSUE-206's field-level pass had not separated the 26-row subset's *additional* `havingClause`/`seasonMax` corruption from the primary `headToHead.kind` defect it was counting. Exploratory scorer movement: v56 `27530 scored / 1500 audit-required / 11125 clean / 15275 soft / 1130 failed` → v57 `27530 / 1500 / 11151 clean / 15249 soft / 1130 failed` (clean +26, soft −26, failed 0 — the 173 primary rows stay scorer-`clean` in both runs since the scorer never asserted `headToHead.kind`; the 26 date-range rows moved from soft to clean because their `havingClause`/`seasonMax` corruption resolved).
- **Resolution:** both required checks confirmed the fix with zero collateral movement outside the wording family. Resolved 2026-09-17. Known out-of-scope, undisturbed finding: `extractClubSeasonMetric`'s "most wins" club_season ranking cue claims "has more wins between A/B" and "has more wins against the other" before `extractHeadToHeadCue` ever sees them; not fixed, not opened as its own issue. Full evidence in `AFLDB-ISSUE-209.md`.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-210 — Leading imperative/request-wrapper phrasing ("find", "show", "list", "give me") declines otherwise-supported questions

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator). Severity was the largest single soft-decline mechanism found by ISSUE-206 (~10,000+ of 15,275 soft-decline exploratory rows, spanning nearly every grain family), not a wrong-answer defect — an honest, fail-closed decline of an otherwise-supported question. Area: deterministic NL search parser canonicalisation (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `src/search/nl/plan.ts`). Implementation commit `8324d2a`, parser v58, on `sonnet/issue-210-imperative-nl-phrasing`.
- **Baseline:** current clean `main` after ISSUE-209, parser v57, worktree `sonnet/issue-210-imperative-nl-phrasing`. Follow-on item (6) of `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md`'s six proposals.
- **Evidence-first inventory:** the two retained exploratory artifacts the issue brief named (`/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v1.csv`, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v57-validation/results.jsonl`) are not present on this Windows workstation (confirmed by `ls` before any implementation work); per the issue's own instruction, no row-count inventory was invented from the rough "10,000+" estimate. `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md` §5 item 1's own source-verified mechanism description plus a direct grep-audit of the current vocabulary tables was used instead: `find`, bare `show` (no "me"), `list`, `give me` are confirmed absent from `CONVERSATIONAL_FILLER`, `STOPWORDS`, and every extraction stage; the **only** literal-word collision found anywhere in `vocab.ts`/`parser.ts` is `/\bfind the (?:big )?sticks\b/` (the AFL-slang goals idiom). The full per-family row-count breakdown remains an outstanding operator task against the retained host artifacts (see below), not assumed here.
- **Root cause (source-verified):** `canonicalise()` (`vocab.ts`) strips `CONVERSATIONAL_FILLER` phrases globally (already covers `show me`, `(please )?tell me`, `please`) but had no entry at all for a leading `find`/bare `show`/`list`/`give me`. The unmatched verb survived into the extraction pipeline as a leftover token, and the generic unmatched-token confidence gate declined the question even when grain/metric/scope resolved completely from the rest of the text.
- **Fix:** one new anchored regex, `LEADING_REQUEST_PREFIX_RE = /^(?:give me|find(?!\s+the\s+(?:big\s+)?sticks\b)|show|list)\b\s*/` (`vocab.ts`), applied in `canonicalise()` after the existing filler loop and before `canonicaliseStatWords()`. Anchored to the very start of the string, consumed at most once — the same words elsewhere in the text are untouched, no `STOPWORDS`/`AGG_WORDS`/other table changed, no extraction stage reordered. `find`'s negative lookahead is the one guard required by the vocabulary audit above, protecting the "find the (big) sticks" goals idiom from being broken by the new stripper. Only the issue brief's own "likely safe" set was implemented (`find`, bare `show`, `list`, `give me`); `tell me about`, `can you find`, `could you show`, `I want`, `find me`, `list me`, and generic conversational/fuzzy parsing were deliberately left unsupported, per the issue's explicit scope boundary and the absence of corpus/vocabulary evidence for them. `PARSER_VERSION` 57 → 58.
- **Files changed:** `src/search/nl/vocab.ts` (fix), `src/search/nl/plan.ts` (`PARSER_VERSION` bump + history entry), `tests/nl-parser.test.ts` (new `describe('17. AFLDB-ISSUE-210 ...')` block). No change to `parser.ts`/`semantic-intents.ts` — the fix is entirely upstream, in canonicalisation.
- **RED evidence:** 8 wrapper/core pairs covering all 7 domains the issue asked for (season query, club-scoped season leaderboard, club result/extrema x2 — one bare `show`, one pre-existing `show me` regression guard, career threshold, venue/opponent-scoped named-player stat, head-to-head `compare_wins`, coach record), each asserted with full `NlQueryPlan` structural equality (`toEqual`), not just `status === 'plan'`. Plus 3 negative controls: the `find the big sticks` idiom at the leading position (must still resolve `metric: 'goals'`), a gibberish-wrapped fail-closed control, and an unanswerable-topic-wrapped fail-closed control. Every pair/control was hand-traced against the exact current source and independently confirmed with a disposable Node regex probe against all eleven representative strings before implementation.
- **Focused validation (worktree-local `npm ci`):** `tests/nl-parser.test.ts` 483/483, `tests/nl-regression-corpus.test.ts` 163/163, `tests/nl-semantic-mapping.test.ts` 174/174, `tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` 53/53 (873/873 total); `npm run typecheck` clean (`next typegen` + `tsc --noEmit`). The ISSUE-210 describe block itself: 11/11 passed.
- **Operator validation (streamanator, commit `8324d2a`, `PARSER_VERSION` 58):** frozen V5 stable-corpus rerun (`/home/arm/nl-stress-corpus-v5.csv`) = **12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed**, no regression. ISSUE-206 exploratory corpus: direct structured-plan comparison between retained pre-fix (v57, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v57-validation/results.jsonl`) and post-fix (v58, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v58-validation/results.jsonl`) runs (both 29,030 rows / 29,030 unique IDs) found exactly **1408 changed plans**, distributed `663 find / 378 list / 367 show / 0 other` — no unrelated wording family changed; `give me` produced zero exploratory changed-plan rows (the generated corpus's templates don't happen to use it), left covered by the focused tests instead of assumed. Full reconciliation of all 1408: **1288 `soft_fail -> clean`** (663 find + 319 show + 306 list, the direct usability improvement); **48 `soft_fail -> fail`**, all `prefix: show` / `category: player_game_single`, all the pre-existing Gary Ablett Jnr/Snr canonical-display-name scorer artifact already named in `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md` (26 `Gary Ablett Snr -> Gary Ablett`, 22 `Gary Ablett Jnr -> Gary Ablett`) — the parser now reaches a valid `player_game` plan a leftover `show` previously blocked outright, and the scorer's suffixed-label-vs-canonical-name comparison is exposed by that new reachability, not caused by a v58 regression, and is not fixed here; **72 audit-required `decline -> success`**, all `List sons of <PLAYER> with <career condition>` (category `relationship_conditions`), now producing a typed `player_career` plan (`agg: list`, `relationshipSubject`, `careerPredicates: [son_of_player(<id>)]`, requested `careerConditions` preserved — representative: "List sons of Patrick Dangerfield with zero goals" -> `relationshipSubject = Patrick Dangerfield`, `careerPredicates = son_of_player(10244)`, `careerConditions = [goals eq 0]`) that remain intentionally audit-required by corpus design, not reclassified, exploratory V1 not modified. Aggregate exploratory scorer totals moved v57 `11151 clean / 15249 soft / 1130 failed / 1500 audit-required` -> v58 `12439 clean / 13913 soft / 1178 failed / 1500 audit-required` (93 diagnostic groups).
- **Resolution:** both required checks confirmed the fix — 1288 genuine usability improvements, zero unrelated wording-family movement, and both non-improvement buckets (48, 72) traced to pre-existing, already-documented corpus/scorer conditions rather than new defects. Resolved 2026-09-17. Known carried-forward findings, not fixed here: the Gary Ablett Jnr/Snr scorer artifact (now visible on 48 more rows because they are newly reachable), and `relationship_conditions` composition remaining intentionally audit-required (72 more rows now reachable as typed plans). Full evidence in `AFLDB-ISSUE-210.md`.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-211 — Implement `after YEAR` as an exclusive season lower bound

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator). Product-gap fix (not a wrong-answer defect): `after YEAR` was a documented, correctly-labeled decline until this session. Area: deterministic NL search parser season extraction (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`, `src/search/nl/vocab.ts`). Parser v58 → v59, implementation commit `c113e6a`, unmerged on `sonnet/issue-211-after-year-season-bound`.
- **Baseline:** current clean `main` after ISSUE-210, parser v58, worktree `sonnet/issue-211-after-year-season-bound`. Follow-on item (5) of `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md`'s six proposals — the largest single unimplemented soft-decline vocabulary family it found.
- **Evidence-first inventory:** the two retained host artifacts the issue brief named (`/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v1.csv`, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v58-validation/results.jsonl`) are not present on this Windows workstation (confirmed by `ls`/`find` before any implementation work). Per the issue's own instruction, the rough "~1,200+" estimate from `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md` (`after` alone 829 term-frequency rows among the 15,275 soft-decline rows, plus combinations) is **not** treated as a verified affected-row count here — it is a term-frequency read, not a classification separating genuine `after YEAR` temporal wording from `after the siren`/other non-temporal `after`. That classification requires an operator run against the retained host artifacts (commands in `AFLDB-ISSUE-211.md`) and is outstanding, not assumed.
- **Source-verified before implementation:** `extractSeasons` (`parser.ts:379-449`) is the single season extractor (`in YEAR`/decades/`between`/`since`/`before`/bare-year all live inside it, called once at `parser.ts:2100`) — no second competing season parser. `SINCE_RE`/`BEFORE_RE`/`BETWEEN_RE`/`BARE_YEAR_RE` (`vocab.ts:714-726`) are all anchored to a literal `\d{4}` immediately after the keyword. The after-siren family and the achievement-clause connective `AFTER_THE_ACHIEVEMENT` (`vocab.ts:1131`, `after|following|since` + a determiner) are the only other places `after` has meaning, and neither ever puts a literal year immediately after the word — `AFTER_THE_ACHIEVEMENT`'s own comment (`vocab.ts:1127-1129`) explicitly calls `"after 1950"` a *different* clause "with its own owner", independent pre-existing confirmation a year-anchored `after` extractor cannot collide with either family.
- **Fix:** new `AFTER_RE = /\bafter (\d{4})\b/` (`vocab.ts`), anchored exactly like `SINCE_RE`/`BEFORE_RE` — structurally cannot match `after the siren`, `after their`, `after that`, or `after round 12` (none has a literal year immediately after the word). In `extractSeasons` (`parser.ts`), checked in an `else` branch alongside the existing unconditional `since` check: if `since` didn't already claim the lower bound, try `after`, and on a match set `seasonMin = Number(after[1]) + 1` (exclusive lower bound — AFL seasons are whole years), push to `consumed`, strip from `working`. Same three-step pattern `since`/`before` already use; `before`/`between`/decades/bare-year fallback completely unchanged. `PARSER_VERSION` 58 → 59.
- **Files changed:** `src/search/nl/vocab.ts` (new `AFTER_RE`), `src/search/nl/parser.ts` (import + new `else` branch in `extractSeasons`), `src/search/nl/plan.ts` (`PARSER_VERSION` bump + history entry), `tests/nl-parser.test.ts` (new `describe('AFLDB-ISSUE-211: after YEAR season bound', ...)` block, 14 tests). No change to `semantic-intents.ts`, `STOPWORDS`, after-siren vocabulary, stage ordering, or `since`/`before`/`between`/exact-year/decade logic.
- **RED evidence:** 7 grain-diverse pairs each mirroring an already-supported `since YEAR` form (`player_season` bare metric x2, `team_match` club result, `player_game` venue-scoped, `club_season`, named-player composition, opponent-club composition) plus a direct `after 2000`->2001 vs `since 2000`->2000 contrast; 3 negative controls (`after the siren`, `after the siren to win`, and a composed control proving after-siren club scoping and a trailing `after 2000` coexist in one question); 3 boundary-year cases (`after 1896`->1897 first-legal-season, `after 2026`->2027 within `NL_LIMITS.maxSeason`, `after 9999`->10000 refused by `validatePlan`, not by `parseNlQuestion` itself — corrected during RED after discovering `parseNlQuestion` has no season-range gate of its own, matching how an equally out-of-range `since`/`before` value is already handled). Two other RED-phase corrections, both caught by running against the real implementation rather than assumed: the two bare-metric grain tests were written expecting `player_career` and corrected to the actual, pre-existing `player_season` reading (confirmed identical for `most goals since 2019`/`most brownlow votes since 2010` via a disposable probe) — no implementation defect, a wrong initial test assumption.
- **Negative-control evidence:** `AFTER_RE` requires a literal 4-digit year immediately after the word; every other `after` usage found in source (`after the siren`, `after their`, `after that`, `after round 12`) has no digit there, so it cannot match regardless of extractor ordering. Verified by full-source grep audit of every `after` occurrence in `vocab.ts`/`semantic-intents.ts` plus the three passing negative-control tests above.
- **Focused validation (worktree-local `npm ci`):** `tests/nl-parser.test.ts` 497/497 (14 new), `tests/nl-semantic-mapping.test.ts` + `tests/nl-regression-corpus.test.ts` + `tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` 390/390 combined, no regressions; `-t "AFLDB-ISSUE-211"` focused selection 14/14; `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen` + `tsc --noEmit`) clean.
- **Operator validation (streamanator, commit `c113e6a`, `PARSER_VERSION` 59):** frozen V5 stable-corpus rerun (`/home/arm/nl-stress-corpus-v5.csv`) = **12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed**, no regression. ISSUE-206 exploratory corpus: direct structured-plan comparison between retained pre-fix (v58, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v58-validation/results.jsonl`) and post-fix (v59, `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v59-validation/results.jsonl`) runs (both 29,030 rows / 29,030 unique IDs) found exactly **1406 changed plans**, all genuine `after <4-digit year>` temporal wording, 0 unrelated — the real row-level affected family, superseding the earlier unverified `~1,200+`/term-frequency estimates. Full reconciliation of all 1406: **1262 `soft_fail → clean`** (the direct usability improvement — `after` moves from unsupported token to a parsed `scope.seasonMin = YEAR + 1` letting the already-supported query underneath succeed); **136 `soft_fail → soft_fail`** (95 `career_boundary` / 23 `head_to_head` / 18 `unsupported_composition` — `failureReason` moves from `unsupported_term` to `coverage_unavailable` with the temporal clause now correctly parsed and preserved, but the composition still correctly rejected by the existing compiler/coverage contract; compiler coverage not broadened here); **8 `audit → audit`** (`category = malformed_input`, e.g. "Suns tackles 200 40 after 1999" — now a typed `player_season` plan but remains intentionally manual-audit by corpus design, exploratory V1 not reclassified); **0 `soft_fail → fail`**. The raw aggregate scorer totals (v58 `12439 clean / 13913 soft / 1178 failed / 1500 audit-required` → v59 `13571 clean / 12651 soft / 1308 failed / 1500 audit-required`) show a +130 aggregate hard-failure movement that is **not** attributable to any of the 1406 changed rows and is not an ISSUE-211 regression. 118 changed rows contain `after the siren` composed with a separate genuine `after YEAR` clause; the after-siren semantic intent is preserved in every one, and no row containing only `after the siren` changed.
- **Resolution:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17. Both required host checks confirmed the fix — the frozen V5 stable corpus is unaffected, and the full 1406-row exploratory changed-plan family reconciles to 1262 genuine usability improvements, 136 correctly-declined coverage-gate rows, 8 unchanged manual-audit rows, and 0 unrelated or newly-hard-failing rows. Known follow-up, not opened as its own issue in this closeout: the 136 `soft_fail → soft_fail` rows are correctly declined under the current compiler/coverage contract and would need separate compiler-coverage work to progress further. ## AFLDB-ISSUE-212 — Exploratory V2: correct three confirmed V1 corpus/scorer oracle defects

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17. Local (DB-free) implementation, generator/scorer contract, RED/GREEN test authorship, and streamanator host generation/validation are all complete on `sonnet/issue-212-exploratory-v2-scoring`. Not a parser-feature issue: `PARSER_VERSION` unchanged at `59`; no `src/search/nl/parser.ts`, `vocab.ts`, `semantic-intents.ts` file touched. Follow-on item (4) of `AFLDB-ISSUE-206.md`'s six proposals.
- **Baseline:** clean `main` after ISSUE-211, `PARSER_VERSION` 59, worktree `sonnet/issue-212-exploratory-v2-scoring`.
- **Confirmed V1 root causes (re-verified from current source, not re-asserted from ISSUE-206's text):** (1) 496 rows — `extractClubs` (`src/search/nl/parser.ts:220-268`) treats a literal `ClubA <v|vs|versus> ClubB` adjacency as the unordered `scope.matchup` unconditionally, checked before and independent of the `for`/`against` role-assignment branch; the V1 `team_match_result` generator's template 3 ("... margin for Sydney versus Richmond ...") nonetheless asserted directional `expected_club`/`expected_opponent`, and `tools/nl/corpus.ts`'s scorer had no path to check `scope.matchup` at all. (2) 283 rows — `answerAchievementSummary` (`src/db/queries/nl/achievement-summary.ts`) groups entirely on `plan.achievementSummary.kind` with no reference to `plan.agg` anywhere in the file; the parser's own aggregation default for this grain's cue-free templates is `{kind:'max'}` (`parser.ts:3756-3791`), not the `'count'` V1 asserted. (3) 351 rows — Gary Ablett Jnr (id 4701) and Snr (id 4700) share the canonical display name "Gary Ablett"; the scorer's player slot had no `wantId`/`gotId` pair at all (unlike the adjacent club/venue slots), so it always fell back to a plain string comparison that a qualified name can never win against a shared canonical one.
- **V2 design:** new file `tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus-v2.mjs` (forked from the V1 generator, which is untouched), `generatorVersion` `issue-212-exploratory-v2`, same seed `2060542026`. Question generation is deliberately unchanged — no RNG-consuming call or equivalence-grouping input differs — so V1 and V2 ids/questions are bit-identical; only the expectation fields for the two affected families differ. Two new, optional CSV columns (`expected_scope_kind=matchup`, `expected_achievement_kind`) are read by the same `tools/nl/corpus.ts` that already scores the frozen V1 12,000-row corpus; both are blank on every existing row, so no version flag is needed and V1 scoring is unchanged except for the documented player-identity exception below. Player-identity id-preference is a scorer-only, non-version-gated fix (`EntityIndex.playerId`, wired in `tools/nl/stress-test.ts` from the corpus's own distinct player names via the same `ctx.resolvePlayer` the parser uses) — generic, no player id/name/suffix string appears in `corpus.ts` itself.
- **Files changed:** `tools/nl/corpus.ts` (scorer: `StressExpectation.scopeKind`/`achievementSummaryKind`, `EntityIndex.playerId`, matchup-set check, achievement_summary-specific aggregation branch, id-preferring player slot); `tools/nl/stress-test.ts` (`buildPlayerIndex`, `entity-index.json` gains `players`, unindexed-player warning); `tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus-v2.mjs` (new); `tools/nl/triage-exploratory-corpus.mjs` (its own independent diagnostic comparison updated to recognise `expected_scope_kind=matchup` so it stays valid for a V2 corpus; the achievement-summary case needed no change since its generic `expected_plan_json` comparison and the now-blank `expected_aggregation` already handle it); `tools/nl/README.md` (documents the two new columns and player-identity comparison); `tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` (three new RED/GREEN `describe` blocks with negative controls, detailed below). `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v1.csv`/`.manifest.json` not read or modified (no host access from this workstation this session).
- **RED/GREEN test evidence (local, DB-free):** symmetric matchup — passes with both expected clubs present in `scope.matchup` in either order, fails (`DROPPED_FILTER`) against a directional-shaped plan, fails (`WRONG_CLUB`) when one expected club is missing; negative control confirms an expectation with no `scopeKind` (genuinely directional wording) still fails on a swapped `clubFor`/`clubAgainst` plan. Achievement summary — passes with the generic default `agg:{kind:'max'}` when `achievementSummary.kind` is correct, fails on a wrong `kind`; negative control confirms an ordinary grain's `expected_aggregation` mismatch still fails (the generic check is not globally weakened). Player identity — a correct distinct id (Jnr 4701 vs. Snr 4700, both `name:'Gary Ablett'`) passes, the wrong distinct id fails; an ordinary uniquely-named player with no index entry is unaffected; with no player index at all the exact pre-ISSUE-212 name-only comparison is reproduced.
- **V1 compatibility:** every new field/branch is gated on a column absent from both the frozen V1 12,000-row corpus and the V1 exploratory corpus, so their scoring is unchanged with one documented, allowed exception: player-identity id-preference is not version-gated (it only activates when an id can be resolved, and cannot regress a row that already passed by name). **Confirmed on streamanator:** the frozen V1 12,000-row corpus rerun with the updated scorer stayed 12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed — no regression.
- **Host validation (streamanator, 2026-09-17):** V2 generated — 29,030 rows, seed `2060542026`, SHA256 `bb75e4b5067942117c60f8eab6cfd01de4d8fc1e0c4fee07e10650fae97edb4a`, deterministic replay confirmed (two runs, identical SHA256), V5 exact/normalized overlap 0/0, 1,500 audit-required. Exploratory V2 against parser v59: 27,530 scored / 14,878 clean / 12,651 soft / **1 failed** / 1,500 audit-required / 55 diagnostic groups. V1-v59 → V2-v59 hard-failure reconciliation (same corpus rows and current parser, scored under the pre- vs. post-ISSUE-212 oracle — not V1's original v54 figures): **1,308 old (false) hard failures removed, 1 newly exposed genuine hard failure, net failed count change -1307** — two separate, opposite-direction movements, not "1307 fixed". Removed-failure breakdown: 545 `team_match_result` (matchup fix), 320 `achievement_summary` (aggregation fix), 213 `player_game_scope_collision` + 118 `player_game_scoped_total` + 112 `player_game_single` = 443 player-identity fix (225 Gary Ablett Snr, 218 Gary Ablett Jnr). These exceed AFLDB-ISSUE-206's original v54 figures (496/283/351) because AFLDB-ISSUE-207 through 211 landed between v54 and v59 and moved previously-*declined* rows into scored plans for the first time, exposing more instances of the same three pre-existing oracle/scorer defects — none of those five fixes touched `extractClubs`'s matchup detection, achievement aggregation, or player-identity resolution themselves. Full detail and exact commands in `AFLDB-ISSUE-212.md` §8-9.
- **Newly discovered, distinct parser defect surfaced by (not caused by) the V2 oracle — confirmed, one row:** row `#20609919` ("... margin for North Melbourne versus Melbourne at Adelaide Oval ...") has an identical parser plan in V1 and V2 (`clubFor=North Melbourne`, `clubAgainst=Melbourne`, `scope.matchup` absent) — the plan is unchanged; only V2's corrected, correctly-strict oracle now hard-fails it, where V1's directional assertion coincidentally matched, and it is the sole genuine hard failure in the 27,530-row V2 host run. Root cause traced to source: `phrasePosition`/`phraseEnd` (`parser.ts:162-170`) re-find each club by a bare `\b<matchedText>\b` search of the whole original text, so when the second club's display text ("Melbourne") is also a word-bounded substring of the first club's own text ("North Melbourne"), that search returns the embedded occurrence instead of the real, later, standalone mention, and the unordered-matchup check silently fails to form — a genuine, pre-existing `extractClubs` defect, not a corpus/scorer artifact and not introduced by this issue. Deliberately **not** suppressed in the V2 oracle (`AFLDB-ISSUE-212.md` §6a): asserting `matchup` uniformly for every `team_match_result` "versus" row is correct, and this hard failure is exactly the "cleaner evidence for future parser work" this issue exists to produce. **Two more club pairs share the identical structural shape by source inspection only** (`Port Adelaide`/`Adelaide`, `Greater Western Sydney`/`Sydney`, in that draw order) **and remain unreproduced hypotheses** — the actual V2 host run found exactly one failure total, so neither pair is confirmed to have been drawn by this seed or, if drawn, to reproduce the mechanism. Recorded as a follow-up finding for a possible separate future issue; **no issue number allocated in this closeout**, per this repository's convention for an out-of-scope discovery made while resolving a different issue.
- **Resolution:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17. Both required host checks confirmed the fix: the three corrected oracle/scorer defects (496/283/351 at v54, 545/320/443 at v59) are gone from the hard-failure count, the frozen V1 corpus is unaffected (12000/12000/0/0), and the corpus is reproducible (SHA256-verified deterministic replay, 0 duplicates, 0/0 V5 overlap). One genuine, distinct, pre-existing parser defect was exposed rather than hidden (row `#20609919`) and is intentionally left unfixed and unopened as its own issue in this closeout, per §6a above.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-213 — `extractClubs` overlapping club-name position bug breaks unordered matchup detection

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator). Implementation commit `4f0be951` ("Fix overlapping club matchup parsing"), `sonnet/issue-213-overlapping-club-matchup`.
- **Baseline:** clean `main` after ISSUE-212, `PARSER_VERSION` 59, worktree `sonnet/issue-213-overlapping-club-matchup`.
- **Confirmed genuine defect (from AFLDB-ISSUE-212's closeout, §6a there):** row `#20609919`, "Largest winning margin for North Melbourne versus Melbourne at Adelaide Oval", produces the identical parser plan under both the V1 and V2 exploratory oracle (`clubFor=North Melbourne`, `clubAgainst=Melbourne`, `scope.matchup` absent) — a pre-existing `extractClubs` defect masked until ISSUE-212 corrected the V1 directional oracle to assert `expected_scope_kind=matchup` for symmetric "versus" wording. Not an ISSUE-212 scorer/generator defect and not a new regression; not opened as its own issue in ISSUE-212's closeout.
- **Root cause, re-verified from current source (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`, `extractClubs`/`phrasePosition`/`phraseEnd`, lines ~161-269 pre-fix):** the two helper functions re-derived each matched club's position by running a bare, non-global `\b<matchedText>\b` regex against the ORIGINAL question text and taking the first hit. `findClub`'s `findLongestMatch` (`src/search/nl/entities.ts`) picks the longest available directory name that exists anywhere in the (progressively-stripped) working text, without regard to position, so for "North Melbourne versus Melbourne" the first iteration always matches the longer "North Melbourne" first regardless of where it sits. On the second iteration the shorter club's own name, "Melbourne", is also a word-boundary match *embedded inside* "North Melbourne" itself (the space before it is a word boundary too) — and since it is the FIRST `\bMelbourne\b` in the string, the old position search bound the second club to that embedded occurrence instead of the real, later, standalone mention after "versus". The computed gap between the two (wrongly-positioned) club spans came out empty/negative, so the exact `versus`/`vs`/`v` separator check between them never matched, `scope.matchup` was never formed, and the parser fell through to the directional `clubFor`/`clubAgainst` role-assignment branch, which happened to reproduce the exact plan shape recorded above. Order-sensitive: the reverse wording ("Melbourne versus North Melbourne") was already correct before this fix, because the real standalone "Melbourne" happens to be the first `\bMelbourne\b` in that string too (see Tests below).
- **Candidate pairs investigated (ISSUE-212 named these as unreproduced, source-derived hypotheses only):** `Port Adelaide`/`Adelaide` and `Greater Western Sydney`/`Sydney` share the identical structural shape (the shorter club's name is the literal tail word of the longer club's own name). Manually traced against the current, pre-fix source logic (character-by-character simulation of `findLongestMatch`, `phrasePosition`, and the `between`/`byPosition` matchup check) rather than executed, because this fresh worktree has no installed dependencies to run the parser against; both traces reproduce the identical failure mechanism as the confirmed row, forward order only (reverse order unaffected, same reasoning as North Melbourne/Melbourne). Recorded as confirmed-by-trace, pending the operator's actual host/local test run for empirical confirmation.
- **Fix (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`):** replaced `phrasePosition`/`phraseEnd` with a single `firstUnclaimedOccurrence(text, phrase, claimed)` helper that scans ALL word-boundary occurrences of a matched club's display text in the original question (not just the first) and returns the first one that does not overlap a span an earlier club match in the same `extractClubs` call has already claimed. `extractClubs`'s per-club loop now tracks claimed spans in `found` and passes them to the new helper instead of taking the bare first match. Generic: no club name, alias, or the specific row is referenced in the fix itself; the exclusion is purely by already-claimed character span, so it applies identically to any pair of club names in this embedding relationship. `nearestGoverningPreposition`, the `for`/`against` role-assignment logic, and the exact-`versus`/`vs`/`v`-only matchup check are all unchanged.
- **Parser version:** `PARSER_VERSION` 59 → 60 (`src/search/nl/plan.ts`), with a new dated entry in the existing version-history comment block above the constant, matching the repository's established convention (see v55-v59 entries there).
- **Tests (`tests/nl-parser.test.ts`), all DB-free:** a new `AFLDB-ISSUE-213` describe block, plus new club fixtures (`Melbourne` org 8, `North Melbourne` org 9, `Sydney` org 10, `Essendon` org 11, `Hawthorn` org 12) and one new venue fixture (`Adelaide Oval` id 3). Covers: (1) the confirmed row's exact wording, asserting `scope.matchup` with both clubs and no `clubFor`/`clubAgainst`, plus its reverse order as a documented already-correct control; (2) both candidate pairs, forward and reverse order; (3) three non-overlapping symmetric "versus"/"vs"/"v" regression controls (Sydney/Richmond, Collingwood/Carlton, Essendon/Hawthorn) proving the fix does not turn every club pair into a special case; (4) two directional-wording regression controls for an overlapping-name pair ("North Melbourne biggest win against Melbourne", "biggest win by Port Adelaide against Adelaide"), proving directional wording stays directional and does not collapse into `matchup`; (5) one partial-text, non-collision control (Adelaide/Greater Western Sydney) as a sanity check outside the fix's overlap branch entirely.
- **Fixture-only correction found on first execution:** once `npm ci` installed dependencies, the first real run found one failure — the pre-existing, parser-v15-era negative control `'a rivalry whose clubs are not in the directory declines instead of guessing'` (`describe('16. marquee matches...')`) asserted `'players who played in a sydney derby'` declines because its comment recorded the shared `CLUBS` fixture had no `Sydney`; this issue's new fixtures added `Sydney` to that same shared array, so `RIVALRY_WORDS`'s `sydney derby → ['sydney', 'greater western sydney']` mapping could now resolve both clubs and the question produced a plan instead of declining. Confirmed as a fixture-assumption conflict, not a parser regression: the parser behaved correctly given the changed fixture. **Fix (test-only, `tests/nl-parser.test.ts`):** swapped the negative control's question to `'players who played in a western derby'` (`RIVALRY_WORDS` → `['west coast', 'fremantle']`, neither present in the fixture and neither touched by this issue), preserving exactly the same proof (decline when a rivalry's clubs are absent from the directory) via a different, still-genuinely-absent rivalry pair, and rewrote the comment to name the mechanism rather than a specific missing club. No other pre-existing test in the file was found to depend on the absence of `Melbourne`/`North Melbourne`/`Essendon`/`Hawthorn`/`Adelaide Oval` (checked by search: MCG-venue tests use the `mcg`/`the g` aliases, not the literal word "melbourne"). `Adelaide`/`Port Adelaide`/`GWS` predate this issue, unaffected. No production code (`parser.ts`/`plan.ts`) changed for this correction.
- **Local verification (this session):** `npx vitest run tests/nl-parser.test.ts` → 509/509 passed; `npx vitest run tests/nl-regression-corpus.test.ts tests/nl-semantic-mapping.test.ts tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` → 402/402 passed; `npm run typecheck` → clean. `PARSER_VERSION` confirmed still 60 (not bumped again).
- **Guardrails honoured:** no club name special-cased in the fix itself (spans are compared generically); symmetric matchup semantics not weakened; ISSUE-212's V2 corpus/scorer files untouched; no directional club query converted to matchup; row `#20609919` not special-cased; production parser code not touched for the fixture correction.
- **Host validation (streamanator, 2026-09-17), commit `4f0be951`, `PARSER_VERSION = 60`:** frozen V5 stable corpus stayed **12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed** — no stable-corpus regression. Exploratory V2 (the same frozen 29,030-row corpus from ISSUE-212, not regenerated) moved from v59 baseline **27530 scored / 14878 clean / 12651 soft / 1 failed / 1500 audit-required** to v60 candidate **27530 scored / 14879 clean / 12651 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required** — net clean +1, soft 0, fail -1, audit 0; row `#20609919` confirmed absent from v60's failures. A direct plan-level reconciliation of the full 29,030-row `results.jsonl` (v59 vs. v60, saved as `/home/arm/issue-213-v59-v60-plan-diff.json`) found **exactly 1 changed plan across the entire corpus** — row `#20609919` moving from `clubFor=North Melbourne/clubAgainst=Melbourne/matchup=absent` to `matchup.clubA=North Melbourne/matchup.clubB=Melbourne/clubFor,clubAgainst=absent`, with every other field on that row and every field on all 29,029 other rows unchanged — confirming the fix is exactly isolated to the known defect, zero unrelated movement. `npm run nl:stress:compare` could not produce a row-severity table because the stored `results.jsonl` files carried no findings (including with `--report-only`); this is a tooling limitation against these run directories, not a validation gap — each run's own summary/run metadata plus the direct plan diff gave stronger, sufficient row-level evidence.
- **Resolution:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17. All required outcomes met: frozen V5 unaffected, V2 hard failures 1 → 0, row `#20609919` corrected, and the direct 29,030-row plan comparison confirms exactly one changed plan with zero unrelated changes. See `AFLDB-ISSUE-213.md` §8/§11 for the full record.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-214 — `club_season_rank` "what season had..."/"...seasonal..." phrasing declines with `unsupported_term: season`/`seasonal`

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator). Implementation commit `731edd8` ("Support club season rank phrasing"), `sonnet/issue-214-club-season-rank-phrasing`.
- **Baseline:** clean `main` after ISSUE-213, `PARSER_VERSION` 60. Exploratory V2 (parser v60): 29030 input / 27530 scored / 14879 clean / 12651 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required. Two soft-failure clusters targeted: `club_season_rank/3` (642 rows, `UNEXPECTED_DECLINE`) and `club_season_rank/1` (614 rows, `UNEXPECTED_DECLINE`), combined 1256 rows.
- **Scope proof (`tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus-v2.mjs`, `club_season_rank` generator, lines ~361-373):** both failing template indices and the two already-passing ones (0, 2) build the IDENTICAL expected plan shape — `temporal({ grain: 'club_season', metric, aggregation: min/max })`, with `e.club` set for templates 1 and 3 only. The four templates are four English phrasings of one semantic construction (club-season ranking by wins/losses/draws/percentage), not two separate mechanisms: template 0 ("Which club had the most wins in a season") and template 2 ("Rank teams by their largest losses season") already pass via the existing `clubSubjectPresent`/leading "teams"/"clubs" cue; templates 1 ("`<club>`'s highest/lowest seasonal `<metric>`") and 3 ("For `<club>`, what season had the highest/lowest `<metric>`") fail only because the literal words "season" (template 3) and "seasonal" (template 1) were never claimed by any extractor, so they survived to `report.unsupportedTerms` as leftover tokens and declined a question the parser otherwise understood completely. Confirmed both clusters share one root cause and belong in one fix.
- **Root cause, verified from current source:**
  - `src/search/nl/vocab.ts`'s `IN_ONE_SEASON` (`/\bin (?:a|one|any|(?:a )?single|the same) season\b/`) has no form for the adjective "seasonal", and no vocabulary entry anywhere reads "what/which season had" as a club-season cue — the closest existing pattern, `ACHIEVEMENT_SUMMARY_CUES`'s `by_season` (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts` line 1054), belongs to the unrelated `achievement_summary` grain and is never consulted by `club_season`.
  - `src/search/nl/parser.ts`'s `clubSeasonCuePresent` (previously: `clubSubjectPresent || clubSeasonConditionResult.conditions.length > 0 || (clubFor && !teamMetricResult.metric && clubSeasonMetricWordPresent && seasonWorded)`) has no branch for either phrasing, so for "North Melbourne's highest seasonal losses" (no explicit year) the grain was never even elected as `club_season` — `seasonWorded` requires `inOneSeason`/an explicit season, neither present.
  - Even where the grain WAS already reachable via the existing `clubFor && seasonWorded` branch (e.g. "For Suns, what season had the lowest wins during the 2010s", where the decade already sets `seasonWorded`), the bare word "season" from "what season had" was still never stripped from `text`, so it survived to `leftoverTokens` (`what`/`had` are `STOPWORDS`, "season" is not) and triggered the final leftover-token decline gate regardless of grain election succeeding.
  - The separate AFLDB-ISSUE-189 single-season guard (`grain === 'club_season' && metric !== null && ... && !(clubFor && seasonWorded)`, `src/search/nl/parser.ts` ~line 3480) would ALSO have declined the no-explicit-year cases ("North Melbourne's highest seasonal losses") even after grain election, since none of its existing allowances (`inOneSeason`, a single explicit year, `clubFor && seasonWorded`) are satisfied by "seasonal" alone.
- **Corpus expectation verified correct:** the generator's own `e` object is identical in shape to the already-supported templates (see Scope proof above); no generator/scorer defect found, none touched.
- **Fix (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `src/search/nl/parser.ts`), smallest generic change, no club/corpus-ID special-casing:**
  - `vocab.ts`: two new exports next to `CLUB_SEASON_METRIC_WORDS` — `CLUB_SEASON_RANK_SEASON_CUE_RE = /\b(?:what|which)\s+season\s+had\b/` (an unambiguous club-season cue in its own right, matched as one phrase) and `CLUB_SEASON_SEASONAL_ADJECTIVE_RE = /\bseasonal\b/` (read only once a `CLUB_SEASON_METRIC_WORDS` match is already present in the text — the same gating `CLUB_SEASON_METRIC_WORDS` itself requires).
  - `parser.ts`: computes `clubSeasonRankSeasonCueMatch`/`clubSeasonSeasonalCueMatch` (the latter gated on `clubSeasonMetricWordPresent`) immediately before `clubSeasonCuePresent`, folds both into a `clubSeasonPerSeasonPhrasing` boolean that (a) is OR'd into `clubSeasonCuePresent` alongside the existing three cues, (b) is OR'd into the ISSUE-189 single-season guard's existing allowances so a club named alongside either phrasing with no explicit year still passes, and (c) consumes the matched phrase from `text`/`consumedTokens` immediately, so "season"/"seasonal" never reach `leftoverTokens`. No other cue, guard, or grain touched.
- **Semantic checks satisfied (issue requirements 1-8):** (1) "what season had the highest losses" elects `club_season` via the new cue, not filler-only consumption of "season" — proven by the new tests asserting `p.grain`/`p.metric`/`p.agg` together, not merely a non-decline. (2) "highest seasonal losses" reads as the identical ranking operation (same `grain`/`metric`/`agg` assertions). (3) club ownership preserved (`p.scope.clubFor?.name` asserted in every new positive test). (4) explicit year/decade constraints preserved (`p.scope.seasonMin`/`seasonMax` asserted for the decade and explicit-year cases). (5) `highest`→max / `lowest`→min mapping unchanged (asserted via `p.agg`). (6) wins/losses/draws stay distinct metrics (a `draws` case included). (7)-(8) unsupported-term validation not weakened: `CLUB_SEASON_SEASONAL_ADJECTIVE_RE` is gated on a metric word being present (new regression test: "richmond seasonal vibes" still declines), and bare "season" is still NOT globally ignorable — the rank-season cue requires the specific "what/which season had" phrase, not any occurrence of the word; a season-less, cue-less "which team has the most wins" still declines with its pre-existing "ranked one season at a time" message (new regression test added).
- **Parser version:** `PARSER_VERSION` 60 → 61 (`src/search/nl/plan.ts`), with a new dated entry in the existing version-history comment block above the constant.
- **RED tests added (`tests/nl-parser.test.ts`, new describe block inside "13. club_season queries", all DB-free):** the six representative failures from the issue brief (substituting `Suns`→`Richmond`, `Swans`→`Sydney` kept, `West Coast`→`Carlton` where the shared test-fixture `CLUBS` directory has no Gold Coast/West Coast entries — same semantic construction, no corpus wording special-cased in the fix itself): "for Richmond, what season had the lowest wins during the 2010s", "for Swans, what season had the highest losses", "for Carlton, what season had the highest losses in 2017", "north melbourne's highest seasonal losses", "sydney's highest seasonal draws in 2017", "greater western sydney's highest seasonal losses in 2023".
