## AFLDB-ISSUE-215 — `career_numeric_binding` "plus"/"among" phrasing declines with `unsupported_term`

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator, two host-validation rounds). Round-1 host validation (commit `5eca839`) fully fixed `/2` and cleared 491 of 700 `/3` rows to a valid parsed plan; the remaining 209 `/3` rows were a residual "plus" ownership gap, fixed the same session under the same `PARSER_VERSION` 62, and confirmed by round-2 host validation (commit `6a341fd`) -- all 700 `/3` rows now produce structurally valid plans, declining only at the legitimate `coverage_unavailable` execution boundary.
- **Worktree:** `sonnet/issue-215-career-numeric-binding-phrasing`, base `origin/main` after AFLDB-ISSUE-214 (`6a224dde`).
- **Baseline:** clean `main` after AFLDB-ISSUE-214, `PARSER_VERSION` 61. Exploratory V2 (parser v61): 29030 input / 27530 scored / 15925 clean / 11605 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required. Two soft-failure clusters targeted: `career_numeric_binding/3` (700 rows) and `career_numeric_binding/2` (552 rows), combined 1252 rows.
- **Scope proof (`tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus-v2.mjs`, `career_numeric_binding` generator, lines ~284-299):** five templates share one pool of two numeric career conditions; `/2` is template 2 ("who has the most career S among players with A and B"), `/3` is template 3 ("for CLUB, find players with A plus B"); templates 0/1/4 (joined by "and"/comma) already score clean. Debug-traced every representative row directly against the current parser before writing any fix: for all three `/3` rows, both numeric conditions were ALREADY binding correctly, and the only leftover tokens were `"find plus"` — pure wrapper vocabulary. For `/2`, two of three rows failed on `"among"` alone with both conditions already correct underneath; the first representative row ("... most career goals among players with at least 200 games and zero goals") additionally lost its "zero goals" condition entirely to a second, independent defect. **Conclusion: `/2` and `/3` do NOT share one single root mechanism** — they share the same CATEGORY of gap (an unrecognised wrapper word around an otherwise-fully-supported construction), but `/2` additionally carries a genuine predicate-loss defect `/3`'s template cannot exhibit at all (no ranked metric to collide with).
- **Root cause, verified from current source:**
  - Wrapper vocabulary (shared category): `LEADING_REQUEST_PREFIX_RE` (AFLDB-ISSUE-210) only strips a leading imperative verb at the very start of the string; "For Adelaide, find players with ..." puts "find" one clause later, behind a leading "for" scope clause whose own comma is already gone (turned into a space) by the time either prefix regex runs. Nothing in the vocabulary reads the English word "plus" as a conjunction (`NUMBER_PLUS_RE` matches the digit+`+` SYMBOL, unrelated). Nothing reads "among"/"amongst" as belonging to the numeric-binding construction — the one existing consumer, `CROSS_DOMAIN_CONSUME_RE`, is gated on the unrelated played-and-coached cross-domain reading.
  - Predicate loss (`/2` only): `extractCareerConditions` (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`) resolved a stat column's EARLIEST occurrence in the sentence to decide processing order (an AFLDB-ISSUE-196 fix), but that same earliest occurrence was also the ONLY occurrence ever inspected for an adjacent number — if it had none, the column was abandoned outright, with the stat already removed from `pending`. A stat word occurring twice (once as the ranking subject, once inside its own later numeric condition) silently lost the condition rather than declining on it. Confirmed independent of the "among" gap: reproduces on "most career goals **with** at least 200 games and zero goals" too (no "among" at all). Reordering so the metric mention comes AFTER the conditions (template 4) does not trigger it.
- **Corpus expectation verified correct:** the generator's `e` object for templates 2/3 follows the identical shape every other template uses; no generator/scorer defect found, none touched.
- **Fix (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `src/search/nl/parser.ts`), smallest generic change, no club/corpus-ID/metric-pair special-casing:**
  - `vocab.ts`: new `LEADING_FOR_CLAUSE_REQUEST_PREFIX_RE = /^(for\s+(?:\S+\s+){1,4})(?:give me|find(?!\s+the\s+(?:big\s+)?sticks\b)|show|list)\b\s*/`, applied in `canonicalise()` right after the existing top-anchored strip, replacing the match with its own captured leading-clause group so the clause itself is put back, never deleted.
  - `parser.ts` `extractCareerConditions`: "plus" folded into the same clause-boundary computation "and"/comma already use (a new `lastPlus`/`plusBoundarySpan`), pushed into a clause's `spans` for removal ONLY once that clause has gone on to bind a real value — never added to global `STOPWORDS`. A new gated block (`conditions.length > 0 || predicates.length > 0`) consumes `/\bamong(?:st)?\b(?=\s+(?:the\s+)?players?\b)/` only once a real condition/predicate was actually found. The per-column processing loop now retries successive occurrences of the SAME stat word via a small inner `while (!bound)` loop (bounded to `candidateRe` with a fresh `'g'` flag and advancing `lastIndex`) until one has an adjacent comparator/number, or none do — the outer `best`-selection ordering logic is unchanged.
- **Semantic checks satisfied (issue requirements 1-6):** (1) `/2`/`/3` are the same OPERATION through different wrappers, not the same end-to-end mechanism. (2) `/3` was wrapper-only; `/2` was wrapper PLUS (for a subset of rows) genuine predicate loss. (3) confirmed and fixed — a predicate was parsed as far as its stat word, then silently discarded. (4) no metric misbinding found, only loss; every RED test asserts the exact `careerConditions` array, not `toContainEqual`, so misassignment/duplication would fail loudly. (5) zero-valued phrases needed no new handling (AFLDB-ISSUE-203 already covers them); they were simply the condition most often caught by the collision since `goals` is in both `CAREER_STATS` and `CONDITIONS`. (6) club scope in `/3` is unaffected — only which characters survive canonicalisation changed, never how a club is matched.
- **Parser version:** `PARSER_VERSION` 61 → 62 (`src/search/nl/plan.ts`), with a new dated entry in the existing version-history comment block above the constant.
- **RED tests added (`tests/nl-parser.test.ts`, new top-level `describe('19. AFLDB-ISSUE-215 ...')`, all DB-free):** `St Kilda`/`Suns` (not in the shared `CLUBS` fixture) substituted with `Richmond`; `Adelaide` kept verbatim where the brief already used it — same construction, no production logic special-cased. Three `/3`-style RED cases, two plain `/2`-style RED cases, and two metric/condition-collision RED cases (one per colliding field, `goals` and `games`, proving the fix is generic). Regression controls: existing `career_numeric_binding` wordings (and-joined, comma-joined, trailing-metric, single condition, "most flags") unchanged; "plus" still declines beside an unsupported clause, with no preceding bound clause, and entirely outside the construction; "among" still declines with no numeric condition present; bare "find" behind a non-"for" leading clause still declines.
- **Local verification (initial implementation, after `npm install` in this previously dependency-less worktree, operator-authorised):** `npx vitest run tests/nl-parser.test.ts` → 536/536 passed. `npx vitest run tests/nl-regression-corpus.test.ts tests/nl-semantic-mapping.test.ts tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` → 402/402 passed (163/163 + 174/174 + 65/65, no regression). `npm run typecheck` → clean. `PARSER_VERSION` confirmed 62.
- **Guardrails honoured:** no club name, corpus ID, exact metric pair, or sample string special-cased in `parser.ts`/`vocab.ts`; "plus"/"among" not added to `STOPWORDS` or any blanket-ignore list, both gated to the specific supported construction with regression controls proving they still decline outside it; "find" only additionally stripped behind a literal leading "for ..." clause, never any leading clause generically; no unrelated NL family touched; exploratory V2 generator/scorer untouched.
- **Round-1 host validation (streamanator, commit `5eca839`, `PARSER_VERSION 62`):** frozen V5 stayed 12000/12000/0/0. Exploratory V2 moved 15925 → 16477 clean (+552), 11605 → 11053 soft (-552), 0 failed. `career_numeric_binding/2`: 552 → 0, fully fixed. `career_numeric_binding/3`: 700 split into 491 `coverage_unavailable` + 209 `unsupported_term: plus`. Direct v61-vs-v62 plan comparison: 1043 changed plans (552 + 491), 0 missing — the 209 residual rows stay `plan: null` in both versions, so they never enter the diff.
- **Follow-up investigation, 491 `coverage_unavailable` (`AFLDB-ISSUE-215.md` §11):** the exact guard is `validatePlan`'s `raw.grain === 'player_career' && raw.scope.clubFor` branch (`src/search/nl/plan.ts` ~line 2366), which requires either every condition to be `games` or a club-scopable ranked metric — neither is ever true for `career_numeric_binding/3` (always two DISTINCT condition fields, `metric` always `null`). Traced into `conditionSql`/`metricValueExpr` (`src/db/queries/nl/player-career.ts`): only `games` (via `clubAppearanceCount`) and, for the RANKED METRIC only, `goals` (via a live per-match per-club sum) have any per-club SQL path anywhere in this codebase; the other five possible condition fields (`premierships`/`brownlow_votes`/`clubs_played`/`finals`/`losses`) have none. **Classified a legitimate, currently-real coverage limitation, not a parser/guard defect** — the guard fails closed exactly as AFLDB-ISSUE-110 finding B requires (never silently answer a club-scoped question with a whole-career total). A genuine, narrower asymmetry was found and documented but NOT fixed: `conditionSql` doesn't reuse `metricValueExpr`'s already-proven per-club-sum shape for a `goals` CONDITION (only for the ranked metric), so even the one CONDITIONS-pool pair fully answerable today (`games`+`goals`) currently fails too — flagged as future SQL-compiler work, outside this issue's parser-ownership charter, guard not weakened, no corpus/scorer file touched.
- **Follow-up correction, 209 `unsupported_term: plus` (`AFLDB-ISSUE-215.md` §12), same `PARSER_VERSION` 62:** two more "plus" ownership gaps in `extractCareerConditions`, both reproduced locally (RED) before fixing. (a) The clause-boundary lookback that finds "plus"/"and"/"," was fixed at 20 characters — too short once a long comparator phrase like "no more than " (13 chars) sits on the far side; widened to a separate 40-character boundary-probe span (still returns the NEAREST boundary, proven safe by a new three-clause "and" + "plus" regression control, so it cannot reach past the nearest boundary into an earlier clause). (b) The `negativeTargets` ("no X") loop matched and stripped only the "no X" phrase itself with no awareness of a neighbouring "plus"; a LEADING "plus" is now checked and consumed there too, gated on that clause having actually bound (a TRAILING "plus" needed no fix — already covered by the pending-loop's own boundary search from the other direction). RED tests added reproducing all three host examples verbatim (Sydney, Port Adelaide already in the shared fixture; `Fremantle` substituted with `Essendon`).
- **Local verification after the correction:** `npx vitest run tests/nl-parser.test.ts` → 540/540 passed. Broader gates → 402/402 passed. `npm run typecheck` → clean. `PARSER_VERSION` confirmed still 62 (correction, not a new semantic feature).
- **Round-2 host validation (streamanator, commit `6a341fd`, `PARSER_VERSION 62`):** frozen V5 stayed 12000/12000/0/0, second confirmation. Exploratory V2 aggregate held at 16477 clean / 11053 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required — unchanged from round 1 by construction, since the 209 corrected rows moved between two `soft` classifications (`unsupported_term` → `coverage_unavailable`), not into `clean`. `career_numeric_binding/3` final triage: 700 `coverage_unavailable`, 0 `unsupported_term` — **all 700 `/3` rows now produce structurally valid plans**. A direct round-1-vs-round-2 plan comparison found exactly 209 changed plans, 0 missing, zero unrelated movement elsewhere in the 29,030-row corpus, confirming the correction took effect exactly as intended.
- **Final accounting:** `career_numeric_binding/2` 552 parser failures → 0 (clean). `career_numeric_binding/3` 700 parser failures → 700 valid parsed plans (491 in round 1, 209 in round 2), all reaching the same legitimate `coverage_unavailable` execution-coverage boundary (§11/§15 of `AFLDB-ISSUE-215.md`) — a pre-existing, unrelated SQL-compiler limitation outside this issue's parser-ownership charter, recorded as a future capability candidate and not opened as a new tracked issue. Net exploratory V2 clean improvement attributable to this issue: +552 clean / -552 soft / 0 hard regression (round 1; unchanged by round 2 as expected). Separately, 209 rows moved from a parser-ownership decline (`unsupported_term`) to an execution-coverage decline (`coverage_unavailable`) — a real, proven fix not visible in the top-line clean/soft aggregate since both are `soft`.
- **Resolution:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17. Both host-validation rounds complete and reconciled; `PARSER_VERSION` bumped exactly once (61 → 62); frozen V5 unaffected across both rounds; all `/2` and `/3` parser-ownership defects fixed; remaining `/3` declines confirmed legitimate coverage limitations, not parser defects. See `AFLDB-ISSUE-215.md` §19 and `CHANGELOG.md` for the full record.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-216 — `player_season_leaderboard` "posted...season tally..."/"...seasonal...total" phrasing declines with `unsupported_term`

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator). Implementation commit `8de4a96` ("Fix player season leaderboard phrasing"), `sonnet/issue-216-player-season-leaderboard-phrasing`.
- **Baseline:** clean `main` after AFLDB-ISSUE-215 (`fcfa76ae`), `PARSER_VERSION` 62. Exploratory V2 (parser v62, assumed unchanged since ISSUE-215's round-2 host validation; not regenerated this session): 29030 input / 27530 scored / 16477 clean / 11053 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required. Two soft-failure clusters targeted: `player_season_leaderboard/0` (576 rows) and `player_season_leaderboard/3` (559 rows), combined 1135 rows.
- **Scope proof (`tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus-v2.mjs`, `player_season_leaderboard` generator, lines ~262-271):** all four templates share one expected-plan shape — `temporal({ grain: 'player_season', metric, aggregation: 'max', club })` — differing only in wrapper wording: `/1` ("For `<club>`, who led the `<stat>` in a season `<time>`") and `/2` ("Most `<stat>` by a `<club>` player in one season `<time>`") already score clean via the existing "no player named + season named + club-only scope" `player_season` grain-election branch (`src/search/nl/parser.ts` ~line 3350, the ISSUE-2-era comment beginning "No player named, a season WAS named..."). `/0` ("Which player posted the highest season tally of `<stat>` for `<club>` `<time>`") and `/3` ("Find the `<club>` player with the best seasonal `<stat>` total `<time>`") are the same semantic construction phrased around their own answer shape (a single season's tally) instead of "in a season" filler — confirmed by direct source trace, not assumed from the shared family name.
- **Root cause, verified from current source (two related but distinct defects, NOT one mechanism):**
  1. **Wrapper vocabulary (both `/0` and `/3`):** none of "posted", "season" (as in "season tally", distinct from the already-consumed "in a season" idiom), "tally", or "seasonal" was ever claimed by any extractor, so each survived to `report.unsupportedTerms`/`leftoverTokens` and forced a decline (`src/search/nl/parser.ts` ~line 4105, the leftover-token gate) even on rows where grain election was already correct.
  2. **Grain-election defect (`/3` only, independent of the wrapper gap):** `/3`'s own "total" (in "seasonal `<stat>` total") is the identical bare word `AGGREGATE_TOTAL_WORDS` (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `/\b(?:total|combined|overall|cumulative|aggregate)\b(?!\s+(?:score|points))/`) reads everywhere else as the "dusty TOTAL goals against Carlton" scoped-running-total cue. With `aggregateTotal` true, the no-player/season-named `player_season` branch's `!aggregateTotal` guard (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`, grain election) failed, and the unnamed-player question fell through to the `scoped || inOneGame` fallback branch instead — `clubFor` alone makes `scoped` true, so `/3` silently misrouted to `grain = 'player_game', mode = 'sum'` (a club-scoped career sum across every game in range) rather than `player_season` (the best single season). `/0` has no "total"/"combined"/"overall"/"cumulative"/"aggregate" word anywhere in its template text, so `aggregateTotal` is already false there and grain election was already correct — confirmed by direct trace, not assumed. `/0` and `/3` therefore do **not** share one root mechanism: `/0` is a pure wrapper-vocabulary gap; `/3` carries that same wrapper gap PLUS this independent grain-election defect.
- **Corpus expectation verified correct:** the generator's `e` object is identical in shape across all four templates (see Scope proof above); no generator/scorer defect found, none touched.
- **Fix (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `src/search/nl/parser.ts`), smallest generic change, no club/corpus-ID/metric special-casing:**
  - `vocab.ts`: three new exports next to `CLUB_SEASON_SEASONAL_ADJECTIVE_RE` — `PLAYER_SEASON_LEADERBOARD_TALLY_RE = /\bseason tally\b/` (matched as one phrase, mirroring `CLUB_SEASON_RANK_SEASON_CUE_RE`'s ISSUE-214 precedent, so "season" never survives alone), `PLAYER_SEASON_LEADERBOARD_SEASONAL_RE = /\bseasonal\b/` (read only once an actual player_match_stats `METRIC_WORDS` match is already present in the text — the same gating discipline `CLUB_SEASON_SEASONAL_ADJECTIVE_RE` uses for the disjoint `CLUB_SEASON_METRIC_WORDS` vocabulary, so the two "seasonal" cues can never both fire on the same word), and `PLAYER_SEASON_LEADERBOARD_POSTED_RE = /\bposted\b/` (read only once one of the two cues above has already matched, so "posted" is never a universal request wrapper).
  - `parser.ts`: immediately after the existing `IN_ONE_GAME`/`IN_A_FINAL`/`IN_A_GRAND_FINAL`/`IN_ONE_SEASON`/`OVER_CAREER`/`AGGREGATE_TOTAL_WORDS` cue-consumption loop, a new block probes `METRIC_WORDS` (not yet consumed — `extractPlayerMetric` runs later) to positively identify the construction, then consumes `PLAYER_SEASON_LEADERBOARD_TALLY_RE`/`PLAYER_SEASON_LEADERBOARD_SEASONAL_RE`/`PLAYER_SEASON_LEADERBOARD_POSTED_RE` under that gate into a `playerSeasonLeaderboardCue` boolean. Grain election's no-player/season-named `player_season` branch condition changes from `!aggregateTotal` to `(!aggregateTotal || playerSeasonLeaderboardCue)` — the override applies ONLY when the player-season leaderboard construction was positively identified from a real metric word plus "season tally"/"seasonal", never generally. No other branch, guard, or grain touched; `aggregateTotal` itself (used unchanged by the named-player branch's `sum`/`single` mode choice) is untouched.
- **Semantic checks satisfied (issue requirements 1-7):** (1)/(2) expected plans for `/0` and `/3` confirmed correct by direct source trace against the generator (Scope proof above). (3) current extraction already gets player/club/time/metric correct in both clusters; only wrapper words were the residual defect for `/0`, plus the independent `aggregateTotal` misroute for `/3`. (4) `/0` never failed grain election; `/3` did (traced above) — the two clusters are NOT symmetric. (5) `/0` and `/3` do not reach the same internal branch by default (`/3` fell through to the `player_game/sum` fallback without the fix) — they are made to reach the same `player_season` branch only via the new, narrowly-gated override. (6) `seasonal` remains scoped to this construction (gated on a player metric word being present), never globally consumed — the existing ISSUE-214 `CLUB_SEASON_SEASONAL_ADJECTIVE_RE` regression ("north melbourne's highest seasonal losses") is unchanged and re-asserted by a new regression test. (7) "season tally" and "seasonal ... total" are synonyms for the identical supported operation (both consumed into the identical `playerSeasonLeaderboardCue` flag, no distinct-ownership logic needed since the two phrasings never co-occur and neither collides with the disjoint club-season vocabulary).
- **Parser version:** `PARSER_VERSION` 62 → 63 (`src/search/nl/plan.ts`), with a new dated entry in the existing version-history comment block above the constant.
- **RED tests added (`tests/nl-parser.test.ts`, new describe block inside "11. player-season queries", all DB-free):** the three representative `/0` cases and three representative `/3` cases from the issue brief (`Fremantle`→`Geelong` substituted, not in the shared `CLUBS` fixture; `Collingwood`, `Richmond`, `Port Adelaide`, `Sydney` kept verbatim), each asserting `p.grain`/`p.metric`/`p.agg`/`p.scope.clubFor?.name`/`p.scope.seasonMin`/`p.scope.seasonMax` together, not merely a non-decline — the `/3` "Port Adelaide" case additionally asserts `p.grain` is `player_season` and NOT `player_game`, the exact grain-election defect this issue fixes. Plus seven regression controls: existing player-season leaderboard wording (`most goals by a richmond player in 2017`) unchanged; the pre-existing named-player scoped-running-total reading (`dusty total goals against carlton` → `player_game`/`sum`, proving `aggregateTotal`'s other use is untouched) unchanged; bare "seasonal" with no player metric word still declines (`richmond seasonal vibes`); bare "tally" without a preceding "season" still declines as an unsupported term; bare "posted" with no season-tally/seasonal construction does not become a universal request wrapper (still declines, `"posted big"` in `unsupportedTerms`); the ISSUE-214 club-season "seasonal" cue (`north melbourne's highest seasonal losses`) is unchanged; career leaderboard wording (`who has the most career goals`) stays `player_career`; single-game leaderboard wording (`most disposals in a final`) stays `player_game`/`single`.
- **Local verification (this session, after `npm install` in this previously dependency-less worktree, operator-authorised):** `npx vitest run tests/nl-parser.test.ts` → 554/554 passed (541 pre-existing + 13 new). `npx vitest run tests/nl-regression-corpus.test.ts tests/nl-semantic-mapping.test.ts tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` → 402/402 passed (163/163 + 174/174 + 65/65, no regression). `npm run typecheck` → clean. `PARSER_VERSION` confirmed 63.
- **Guardrails honoured:** no club name, corpus ID, player name, or exact metric special-cased in `parser.ts`/`vocab.ts`; "posted"/"season"/"tally"/"seasonal"/"total" not added to `STOPWORDS` or any blanket-ignore list — all three new cues gated on a real `METRIC_WORDS` match, and "total" itself received no new consumption logic at all (only the pre-existing `aggregateTotal` flag's effect on one grain-election branch was narrowed); no unrelated NL family touched; exploratory V2 generator/scorer untouched (corpus expectation verified correct, not changed).
- **Hygiene (implementation session):** `git status --short` showed exactly the four intended files (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`, `src/search/nl/plan.ts`, `src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `tests/nl-parser.test.ts`); no stray/zero-byte artefacts found.
- **Host validation (streamanator, 2026-09-17), commit `8de4a96`, `PARSER_VERSION = 63`:** frozen V5 stable corpus stayed **12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed** — no stable-corpus regression. Exploratory V2 (same frozen 29,030-row corpus, not regenerated) moved from v62 baseline **27530 scored / 16477 clean / 11053 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required** to v63 candidate **27530 scored / 17612 clean / 9918 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required** — net clean +1135, soft -1135, failed 0, audit-required 0.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-217 — `player_game_single` "haul"/"peak single-game"/"which match saw...collect" phrasing declines with `unsupported_term`

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on streamanator). Implementation commit `879b0e1` ("Fix player game single match phrasing"), `sonnet/issue-217-player-game-single-phrasing`.
- **Baseline:** clean `main` after AFLDB-ISSUE-216 (`19e6dc68`), `PARSER_VERSION` 63. Frozen V5: 12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed. Exploratory V2 under v63: 29030 input / 27530 scored / 17612 clean / 9918 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required. Target clusters: `player_game_single/0` (423 rows, "...biggest `<metric>` haul in one match..."), `/4` (422 rows, "...peak single-game `<metric>`..."), `/3` (409 rows, "which match saw `<player>` collect the most `<metric>`..."), combined 1254 rows. Optional adjacent cluster inspected: `player_game_scope_collision/3` (555 rows, "find the single-match `<metric>` record for `<player>` against `<club>` at `<venue>`...").
- **Scope proof (`tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus-v2.mjs` lines 229-238, `player_game_single` generator):** all five `player_game_single` templates share one expected-plan shape — `temporal({ grain: 'player_game', mode: 'single', metric: s[1], aggregation: 'max', player: p }, t)` — differing only in wrapper wording. Templates `/1` ("Show the highest `<stat>` game for `<player>`...") and `/2` ("`<player>` record `<stat>` in a game...") already score clean: `/1` via the pre-existing `STAT_GAMES_IDIOM_WORDS` "`<stat>` game(s)" idiom (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts` ~line 934), `/2` via the pre-existing `AGG_WORDS` "record" → `max` entry (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts` line 214) plus the named-player default (`src/search/nl/parser.ts` ~line 3312: "A named player's per-game stat defaults to their single-game peak"). `/0`, `/3`, `/4` never reach a plan at all.
- **Root cause, verified from current source — ONE shared mechanism, not three or wrapper-only:** grain/mode election was ALREADY correct in every failing row before this fix — a named player's per-game stat question defaults to `grain = 'player_game', mode = 'single'` (`src/search/nl/parser.ts` line 3320-3321) whenever `aggregateTotal`/`overCareer` are absent, which they are in all three templates. The actual defect is upstream of grain election, in player-mention resolution (step 12, `candidatePlayerSpan`, `src/search/nl/parser.ts` line 2037): it takes the first four remaining non-`STOPWORDS` alpha tokens in `text` with **no notion of "stop at a non-name word"**, and joins them into one candidate string handed to `ctx.resolvePlayer`. "haul" (`/0`), "peak"/"single-game" (`/4`), and "match"/"saw"/"collect" (`/3`, "which" itself is a `STOPWORDS` entry so it alone is excluded) had no vocabulary entry anywhere in the pipeline, so each survived in `text` until step 12 and was swept into the candidate span alongside the real player name — e.g. "dustin martin" + "haul" → `candidateRaw = "dustin martin haul"`, "match" + "saw" + "patrick" + "dangerfield" → `candidateRaw = "match saw patrick dangerfield"` (the fifth token, "collect", overflows the four-token cap and surfaces separately in `leftoverTokens`). The polluted multi-word span then fails `ctx.resolvePlayer` outright (the extra word depresses the match score below `PLAYER_ACCEPT_SCORE`), producing `unresolvedPlayerMention = candidateRaw` — which is exactly the reported `unsupported_term` string in every representative failure in the issue brief (`"dustin martin haul"`, `"lance franklin peak single-game"`, `"match saw patrick dangerfield collect"`), confirmed by direct trace against `report.unsupportedTerms`'s construction (`src/search/nl/parser.ts` lines 4133-4150), not merely inferred from the failure message shape. `player_game_scope_collision/3` (`tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus-v2.mjs` lines 240-248, template 3: "Find the single-match `<stat>` record for `<player>` against `<club>` at `<venue>`...") shares the **identical** mechanism: bare "single-match" was the unconsumed word, always positioned immediately before the player name, so it always polluted the candidate span the same way (`"single-match shane crawford"` etc., matching the issue's representative failures exactly) — confirmed included, not merely "structurally similar", per the issue's inclusion test.
- **Corpus expectation verified correct:** the generator's `e` object for `player_game_single` and `player_game_scope_collision` is identical in shape across all templates within each family (Scope proof above); no generator/scorer defect found, none touched.
- **Fix (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `src/search/nl/parser.ts`), smallest generic change, no player/club/venue/metric/corpus-ID special-casing:**
  - `vocab.ts`: `IN_ONE_GAME` gains a second alternative, `\bsingle[- ](?:game|match)\b`, reading the bare compound adjective ("peak single-game clearances", "the single-match disposals record") as the same single-game cue "in a single game" already is — narrowly anchored (requires "single" immediately adjacent to "game"/"match", nothing between), so it cannot fire on an unrelated "single" elsewhere ("his single greatest game"). Four new exports: `WHICH_MATCH_SAW_RE = /^which match saw\b\s*/` (anchored to the very start of the string, the same discipline `LEADING_REQUEST_PREFIX_RE` uses); `PLAYER_GAME_SINGLE_COLLECT_RE = /\bcollect(?:s|ed|ing)?\b/` (read only once `WHICH_MATCH_SAW_RE` has already matched); `PLAYER_GAME_SINGLE_HAUL_RE = /\bhaul\b/` and `PLAYER_GAME_SINGLE_PEAK_RE = /\bpeak\b/` (read only once the single-game cue AND an actual `METRIC_WORDS` match are both already present in the text — the same two-part gating discipline `PLAYER_SEASON_LEADERBOARD_SEASONAL_RE` uses).
  - `parser.ts`: `whichMatchSawCue` computed before the existing `IN_ONE_GAME`/`IN_A_FINAL`/.../`AGGREGATE_TOTAL_WORDS` cue-strip loop and OR'd into `inOneGame`'s own election (so the leading phrase is itself a valid single-game cue, not just consumed text). Immediately after that loop: if `whichMatchSawCue`, consume the leading phrase and, separately, `collect` wherever it sits after the player mention (both gated on the same boolean, so `collect` can never fire without the leading phrase). Then, gated on `inOneGame && METRIC_WORDS.some(...)`, consume `haul`/`peak` if present. No grain-election branch touched — grain/mode were already correct; only the text pollution reaching step 12 was fixed.
- **Semantic checks satisfied (issue requirements 1-9):** (1)/(2) expected plans for `/0`/`/3`/`/4` confirmed correct by direct source trace against the generator (Scope proof above). (3) player names ARE resolved by the existing resolver but the text span handed to it was NOT the player's name alone — confirmed by trace, not the "leftover alias" hypothesis. (4) possessive (`/0`, `/4`) and non-possessive (`/3`) forms fail through the identical mechanism — `canonicalise`'s `'s\b` strip (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts` line 145) already normalises "Dustin Martin's" to "dustin martin" cleanly before any extractor runs, so possessive normalisation was never the defect; the two forms are NOT distinct mechanisms. (5) grain already lands on `player_game` in every case (traced above). (6) mode already lands on `single` in every case via the existing named-player default. (7) `max` aggregation is already present via existing `AGG_WORDS` entries ("biggest"/"most") and the `{ kind: 'max' }` default when none matches — untouched. (8) player identity ownership happens in `candidatePlayerSpan`/`resolvePlayer` (step 12), strictly AFTER wrapper-word interpretation would need to happen (step 6) to keep them out of the span — this ordering is exactly why the wrapper words must be consumed before step 12, which the fix does. (9) `player_game_scope_collision/3` shares the exact same mechanism (confirmed above, not assumed from name similarity) and is included.
- **RED tests added (`tests/nl-parser.test.ts`, new top-level describe block "AFLDB-ISSUE-217", DB-free):** the three representative `/0` cases, three `/4` cases, and three `/3` cases from the issue brief (Dustin Martin, Chris Judd, Lance Franklin, Nat Fyfe, Patrick Dangerfield — six new `PLAYERS` fixture entries — each asserting `p.grain`/`p.mode`/`p.metric`/`p.agg`/`p.player?.name`/`p.scope.seasonMin`/`p.scope.seasonMax` together, not merely a non-decline. Both representative `player_game_scope_collision/3` cases (Shane Crawford vs Brisbane Lions at Gabba; Jason Akermanis vs Port Adelaide at Optus Stadium — two new `PLAYERS` entries, one new club `Brisbane Lions`, two new venues `Gabba`/`Optus Stadium`), additionally asserting `p.scope.clubAgainst?.name`/`p.scope.venue?.name`. Plus ten regression controls: existing single-game wording (`dusty most disposals`) unchanged; "haul" in unrelated text (no single-game cue) still declines; "peak" in unrelated text (no single-game cue) still declines; bare "single-game" with no supported player/stat construction still declines; bare "record" with no metric/player still declines (existing `AGG_WORDS` behaviour untouched); "collect" outside the "which match saw...collect" construction still declines; named-player scoped totals (`dusty total goals against carlton`) stay `player_game`/`sum`; career record wording (`who has the most career goals`) stays `player_career`; the AFLDB-ISSUE-216 player-season leaderboard wording stays `player_season`; club/team match records (`richmond biggest win in a final`) are not hijacked by the new player-game cues, staying `team_match`.
- **Local verification (this session, after `npm install` in this previously dependency-less worktree, operator-authorised):** `npx vitest run tests/nl-parser.test.ts` → 575/575 passed (554 pre-existing + 21 new). `npx vitest run tests/nl-regression-corpus.test.ts tests/nl-semantic-mapping.test.ts tests/nl-stress-corpus.test.ts` → 402/402 passed (163/163 + 174/174 + 65/65, no regression). `npm run typecheck` → clean. `PARSER_VERSION` bumped 63 → 64 (`src/search/nl/plan.ts`), production parser semantics changed exactly once.
- **Guardrails honoured:** no player, club, venue, metric, or corpus ID special-cased in `parser.ts`/`vocab.ts`; "haul"/"peak"/"collect"/"match"/"saw"/"record" not added to `STOPWORDS` or any blanket-ignore list — `haul`/`peak` gated on single-game cue AND a real `METRIC_WORDS` match, `collect` gated on the anchored `whichMatchSawCue`, and the `single-game`/`single-match` adjective extension requires the words to be immediately adjacent (no determiner-list interaction with `SCOPE_GOVERNS_MATCH_TYPE`'s separate final/grand-final concern, `src/search/nl/parser.ts` lines 495-517, confirmed by direct inspection — that gate governs match-TYPE words only, not the `game`/`match` noun `IN_ONE_GAME` itself reads); `record` received no new consumption logic (pre-existing `AGG_WORDS` entry, untouched); no unrelated NL family touched; exploratory V2 generator/scorer untouched (corpus expectation verified correct, not changed).
- **Hygiene (implementation session):** `git status --short` showed the four intended files (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`, `src/search/nl/plan.ts`, `src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `tests/nl-parser.test.ts`); one zero-byte stray artefact (`2`, a shell-redirect-parsing artefact from an earlier command this session, `ls`/`wc -c` confirmed 0 bytes) was found and deleted, positively identified as session-created, not pre-existing work.
- **Host validation (streamanator, 2026-09-17), commit `879b0e1`, `PARSER_VERSION = 64`:** frozen V5 stable corpus stayed **12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed** — no stable-corpus regression. Exploratory V2 (same frozen 29,030-row corpus, not regenerated) moved from v63 baseline **27530 scored / 17612 clean / 9918 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required** to v64 candidate **27530 scored / 19421 clean / 8109 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required** — net clean +1809, soft -1809, failed 0, audit-required 0.
- **Target-cluster reconciliation:** primary target at v63 was `player_game_single/0` (423 rows), `/4` (422 rows), `/3` (409 rows) — combined 1254 rows — plus the adjacent same-mechanism target `player_game_scope_collision/3` (555 rows), total 1809 rows. After v64, the explicit target unexpected-decline check returned NONE remaining: `player_game_single/0` 423 → 0, `/4` 422 → 0, `/3` 409 → 0, `player_game_scope_collision/3` 555 → 0. All four clusters fully cleared, exactly matching the aggregate soft→clean movement.
- **Direct plan comparison:** a direct v63 vs. v64 comparison of `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v2-v63-validation/results.jsonl` and `/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v2-v64-validation/results.jsonl` found v63 rows 29030, v64 rows 29030, 0 missing, **1809 changed plans** (structured diff saved as `/home/arm/issue-217-v63-v64-plan-diff.json`) — reconciling exactly to `423 + 422 + 409 + 555 = 1809`. The changed rows are exclusively target-family examples ("Find the single-match disposals record for Shane Crawford against Brisbane Lions at Gabba in 2009", "What was Chris Judd's biggest goals haul in one match in 2009", "What was Dustin Martin's biggest Brownlow votes haul in one match during the 2010s", "Find Lance Franklin's peak single-game clearances in 2017", "Which match saw Patrick Dangerfield collect the most goal assists since 2000"), with zero unrelated movement.
- **Remaining scorer-identity artifacts (not this issue):** the v64 triage still shows `WRONG_PLAYER` groups within the affected template families (`player_game_scope_collision/0-3`: 76/70/67/77 rows; `player_game_single/0-4` excluding `/4`'s own 59: 49/54/58/53 rows) — classified `bucket = scorer_identity_artifact`, the pre-existing Gary Ablett Jnr/Snr canonical-display-name mismatch already tracked from AFLDB-ISSUE-206/210 (player ID resolves correctly; only the scorer's display-name string comparison is wrong). Not `UNEXPECTED_DECLINE`, appears across templates this issue did not modify as well as ones it did, and is independent of the player-span-pollution mechanism fixed here — left as separate, already-tracked scorer/entity-identity work, not touched in this closeout.
- **Resolution:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17. All required outcomes met: all four targeted clusters cleared (`player_game_single/0` 423→0, `/4` 422→0, `/3` 409→0, `player_game_scope_collision/3` 555→0); frozen V5 unaffected; V2 gains exactly 1809 clean rows with 0 hard failures; the direct 29,030-row plan comparison confirms exactly 1809 changed plans with zero unrelated changes; and the remaining Gary Ablett Jnr/Snr `WRONG_PLAYER` rows are confirmed independent, pre-existing scorer-identity artifacts. ## AFLDB-ISSUE-218 — `team_match_result` "widest"/"how much...lose"/"lopsided meeting" phrasing declines with `unsupported_term`

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on `streamanator` across two host-validation rounds). Implementation commits `5bcc957` (parser fix) and `6ed227d` (exploratory oracle correction) on `sonnet/issue-218-team-match-result-phrasing`, unmerged.
- **Baseline:** clean `main` after AFLDB-ISSUE-217 (`19e6dc68`), `PARSER_VERSION` 64. Frozen V5: 12000 scored / 12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed. Exploratory V2 under v64: 29030 input / 27530 scored / 19421 clean / 8109 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required. Target clusters: `team_match_result/2` (569 rows, "by how much did X lose to Y in their most lopsided meeting..."), `/1` (522 rows, "at V, find the widest X win/loss to Y..."), `/0` (56 rows, "what was X' biggest victory against Y...").
- **Scope proof (`tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus-v2.mjs` lines 300-316, `team_match_result` generator):** all four templates share one expected-plan shape — `temporal({ grain: 'team_match', metric, aggregation: 'max', club: c[1], opponent: o[1], venue: v[1] }, t)`, where `metric` is `win_margin`/`loss_margin` depending on the row's `lose` flag. Only template 3 ("Largest margin for C versus O...") sets `expected_scope_kind: 'matchup'` — a separate, already-resolved defect (AFLDB-ISSUE-212/213), out of scope here and unaffected by this fix.
- **Root cause(s), verified from current source — `/1` and `/2` share ONE mechanism, `/0` is a genuinely distinct, already-known defect:**
  - **`/1` and `/2` (root cause: wrapper vocabulary only, never a semantic misread).** Direct trace confirmed both templates already extract `clubFor`/`clubAgainst` correctly via the existing `extractClubs`/`nearestGoverningPreposition` machinery (`src/search/nl/parser.ts`), and the correct win/loss direction was already latent in the existing noun vocabulary (`loss`/`win` in `TEAM_METRIC_WORDS`, `src/search/nl/vocab.ts`) for every wording that used a noun. Three independent, purely-additive wrapper gaps, no grain/direction defect:
    1. **`/1`'s "widest"** was absent from `AGG_WORDS`'s max-aggregation word list (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`) — every other superlative synonym ("biggest"/"largest"/"greatest"/...) was already there.
    2. **`/1`'s leading "At V, find..."** — `LEADING_REQUEST_PREFIX_RE` (AFLDB-ISSUE-210) only reaches a request verb at the very start of the string, and AFLDB-ISSUE-215's `LEADING_FOR_CLAUSE_REQUEST_PREFIX_RE` widened that to a leading "for" scope clause only. A leading VENUE scope clause ("At Kardinia Park, find...") is the identical shape one preposition later — `at` was simply never added to that clause's leading-preposition set.
    3. **`/2`'s "by how much did X lose/beat Y..."** used the VERB forms of the existing win/loss nouns. Neither `lose`/`lost`/`beat` existed anywhere in `TEAM_METRIC_WORDS`, so the sentence's win/loss cue never matched at all (confirmed distinct from `extractHavingClause`'s existing `lose`/`lost` entry, which only fires when a NUMBERED threshold follows — "by how much did Pies lose to Carlton" has no count nearby, so that extractor leaves the text untouched and the bare verb was never claimed by anything). `/2` additionally leaves "how much" and "most lopsided meeting" as decorative wrapper text around the now-correctly-elected construction once the verb is recognised — "most" already yields `max` via the pre-existing `AGG_WORDS` entry, so "lopsided meeting" changes no semantics, exactly as required-semantics item 4 anticipated.
    Confirmed by direct trace that whichever club is the grammatical subject of `lose`/`beat` is always the ungoverned mention `extractClubs` already binds to `clubFor` (no new position-reading logic needed) — "lose"/"lost" means `clubFor` is the losing side, "beat"/"beats" means `clubFor` is the winning side, mirroring the noun forms exactly. Added regression test explicitly distinguishes "Pies lose to Carlton" (Collingwood loses) from "Pies beat Carlton" (Collingwood wins), same subject club, opposite metric, per the runbook's explicit request.
  - **`/0` (root cause: a distinct, already-known possessive-alias defect, NOT a team-match-result mechanism).** `canonicalise()`'s only possessive-stripping rule (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `/['’]s\b/g`) matches an apostrophe immediately BEFORE a trailing "s" ("richmond's" → "richmond"); "Bombers'" is an already-plural noun with the apostrophe AFTER the "s" ("bombers'"), which that regex does not touch at all, and the punctuation-strip step deliberately leaves apostrophes alone ("o'brien" needs its own). The trailing apostrophe survives as a literal character glued to "bombers", failing every club-alias match and surfacing as the sole leftover token, `bombers'` — exactly the reported failure. This is the identical mechanism AFLDB-ISSUE-214 already found and deliberately left unfixed for `club_season_rank` ("Suns'"/"Pies'"/"Bulldogs'"), and per that issue's own residual-pattern list the same defect plausibly recurs across `team_streak` ("Tigers' longest unbeaten streak") and checkpoint/team-record wording — a genuinely cross-family, generic possessive-alias defect, not specific to team-match-result construction. **Deferred, not fixed here**, per the runbook's explicit instruction to keep it out of this issue rather than shoehorn a one-family fix onto a cross-family defect.
- **Corpus expectation verified correct:** the generator's `e` object is identical in shape across templates 0-2 (Scope proof above); no generator/scorer defect found, none touched.
- **Fix (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`, `src/search/nl/parser.ts`), smallest generic change, no club/venue/year/corpus-ID special-casing:**
  - `vocab.ts`: `AGG_WORDS`'s max-aggregation entry gains `widest` alongside the existing synonyms. `LEADING_FOR_CLAUSE_REQUEST_PREFIX_RE` (AFLDB-ISSUE-215) renamed `LEADING_SCOPE_CLAUSE_REQUEST_PREFIX_RE` and widened from a leading `for` clause to `(?:for|at)` — `at` is the same generic, already-recognised venue-scoping preposition venue extraction reads anywhere else it appears; `on` deliberately left out, no corpus wording ever needs it. `TEAM_METRIC_WORDS` gains two verb entries, `/\b(?:lose|loses|lost)\b/ → 'loss_margin'` and `/\bbeats?\b/ → 'win_margin'`, immediately after the existing noun forms. Two new exports, `TEAM_MATCH_RESULT_HOW_MUCH_RE = /\bhow much\b/` and `TEAM_MATCH_RESULT_LOPSIDED_RE = /\blopsided (?:meeting|match|game|contest|encounter)s?\b/`, documented as consumed only once the construction is positively recognised (mirroring the existing `PLAYER_SEASON_LEADERBOARD_*`/`allowBare` gating discipline elsewhere in this file), never added to `STOPWORDS` or any blanket-ignore list.
  - `parser.ts`: at the existing point where a matched `teamMetricResult` word is stripped from `text` (step 11), a new gated block fires only when `teamMetricResult.metric` is `win_margin`/`loss_margin` **and** both `clubFor` and `clubAgainst` have already resolved — i.e. only after the sentence is already a confirmed directional two-club result construction — consuming `TEAM_MATCH_RESULT_HOW_MUCH_RE` and `TEAM_MATCH_RESULT_LOPSIDED_RE` if present. No grain-election branch touched, no club-role assignment logic touched (word-order fallback in `extractClubs` already handles "beat"'s non-prepositional object correctly with zero new code).
- **Semantic checks satisfied (issue requirements 1-7):** (1) expected plans for `/0`-`/2` confirmed correct by direct source trace against the generator (Scope proof above). (2) `/1`/`/2` already extracted both clubs correctly before this fix (traced above). (3) `/2` preserves direction correctly when the subject club is the loser — confirmed by the explicit "lose to" vs "beat" distinguishing test, same `clubFor`, opposite metric. (4) "most lopsided meeting" is confirmed pure wrapper wording, not a semantic change — `max` aggregation comes entirely from "most" (pre-existing `AGG_WORDS`), "lopsided meeting" contributes nothing once consumed. (5) `/1`/`/2` already elected the correct grain/metric before this fix; only wrappers were missing (traced above). (6) `/0` fails specifically because "bombers'" (a trailing-apostrophe plural possessive) is never consumed by `canonicalise`'s possessive-stripping rule, confirmed by direct regex trace, not inferred. (7) `/0` shares its mechanism with the already-documented `club_season_rank` possessive-alias defect (AFLDB-ISSUE-214) and is deferred to a future cross-family issue rather than fixed here.
- **RED tests added (`tests/nl-parser.test.ts`, new top-level describe block "AFLDB-ISSUE-218", DB-free, all fixtures reused from the existing `CLUBS`/`VENUES` directories, no new fixtures needed):** three representative `/2` cases (Collingwood loses to Carlton at Adelaide Oval after 1999; Hawthorn loses to Geelong at the MCG since 2000; Richmond loses to Carlton in 2017 with no venue), each asserting `p.grain`/`p.metric`/`p.agg`/`p.scope.clubFor`/`p.scope.clubAgainst`/`p.scope.venue`/`p.scope.seasonMin`(`/seasonMax`) together; the explicit "lose to" vs "beat" direction-distinguishing test; three representative `/1` cases (Collingwood's widest win to North Melbourne at the MCG in 2023; Greater Western Sydney's widest loss to Sydney at Docklands in 2017, exercising the ISSUE-213 GWS/Sydney overlapping-name pair directionally; Richmond's widest win to Carlton at Adelaide Oval since 2000); one `/0` deferral control proving "Bombers' biggest victory against Pies" still declines on the unresolved "bombers'" token, unchanged by this fix. Plus regression controls: an already-supported directional win query (`richmond biggest win since 2000`) and loss query (`adelaide worst loss to gws giants`) unchanged; an ordinary head-to-head query stays `head_to_head`, not hijacked into a result-record reading; symmetric "versus" matchup parsing (AFLDB-ISSUE-213) unaffected; venue ownership intact alongside the new wrapper consumption; a bare mid-sentence "find" with no leading "for"/"at" clause still declines (not a blanket strip); "widest" contributes aggregation only and does not rescue an otherwise-unsupported question, and generalises correctly beyond this issue's two templates ("Richmond's widest lead against Carlton"); a bare "meeting" with no "lopsided" adjacent still declines (only the specific idiom is consumed, not a blanket stopword); an unrelated "lost" usage still declines on its own genuinely unsupported term ("hair"), not rescued by the new verb reading; team score/crowd record queries and team streak queries remain unaffected.

## AFLDB-ISSUE-219 — cross-family trailing-apostrophe plural club-alias possessive fails resolution (`unsupported_term: bombers'`/`suns'`/`pies'`/etc.)

- **Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, operator-validated on `streamanator`), reconciled the same day after the worktree was rebased onto `origin/dev` (which carries AFLDB-ISSUE-218).
- **Baseline:** rebased onto `origin/dev` after AFLDB-ISSUE-218 (resolved, operator-validated, see above), `PARSER_VERSION` 65 (not 64 — the original implementation was written before the worktree carried ISSUE-218 and has been reconciled onto this baseline; see the Reconciliation note below).
- **Origin:** a task brief citing `AFLDB-ISSUE-214` and `AFLDB-ISSUE-218` as prior residual evidence. `AFLDB-ISSUE-214` §10c (line ~34669 of this file) documents the residual directly: after that issue's fix, 210 `club_season_rank/1` rows remained declining, representative examples `20600206` "Suns' lowest seasonal losses before 2019" → `unsupported_term: suns'`, `20600323` "Pies' highest seasonal wins in 2017" → `unsupported_term: pies'`, `20600424` "Western Bulldogs' highest seasonal percentage since 2000" → `unsupported_term: bulldogs'`, explicitly deferred as "a separate, pre-existing possessive-club-alias defect ... not opened as its own tracked issue." **`AFLDB-ISSUE-218` independently found and deliberately deferred the identical mechanism**, for `team_match_result/0` (56 rows, "What was Bombers'/Dogs'/Brisbane Lions' biggest victory/defeat...") — see its entry immediately above, root-cause bullet "`/0` (root cause: a distinct, already-known possessive-alias defect...)" and its Resolution bullet, both naming this as a future cross-family issue candidate. (An earlier draft of this entry, written before this worktree was rebased onto `origin/dev`, incorrectly stated that `AFLDB-ISSUE-218` did not exist anywhere in the repository — that was true only of the pre-rebase branch state; it is now corrected.) Between AFLDB-ISSUE-214 and AFLDB-ISSUE-218 independently finding and deferring the same defect, and the direct trace of the exploratory-corpus generator below, this issue has ample residual evidence without needing anything further from either issue.
- **Reconciliation note (this session):** the original AFLDB-ISSUE-219 implementation was written against a stale baseline (`main` after AFLDB-ISSUE-217, `PARSER_VERSION` 64) before this worktree was rebased onto `origin/dev`. The rebase produced merge conflicts in `issues.md`, `src/search/nl/plan.ts` and `tests/nl-parser.test.ts` between AFLDB-ISSUE-218's now-landed changes and this issue's stashed changes. All three were resolved by keeping AFLDB-ISSUE-218's content verbatim and re-applying AFLDB-ISSUE-219's changes on top of it, re-numbered onto the correct baseline (`PARSER_VERSION` 65 → 66, not 64 → 65). The root-cause finding, fix, and test coverage described below were re-verified against the current `dev` source (AFLDB-ISSUE-218's `canonicalise()`/`extractClubs`/leftover-token-reconciliation code, none of which AFLDB-ISSUE-218 touched) and still hold exactly as originally found — see the trace below.
- **Trace of the canonicalisation/entity-resolution path for `Bombers`/`Bombers'`, `Dogs`/`Dogs'`, `Lions`/`Lions'` (step 1 of the pipeline, `canonicalise()`, `src/search/nl/vocab.ts` ~line 142), re-verified against current `dev`:**
  - `Bombers`, `Dogs`, `Lions` (no trailing punctuation): lowercased, untouched by either possessive strip, reach `meaningfulTokens`/club matching as plain words. Club matching (`extractClubs`, `src/search/nl/parser.ts`) finds them via a `\bname\b` word-boundary regex against the club/nickname directory and resolves correctly — already supported, unaffected by AFLDB-ISSUE-218.
  - `Bombers'`, `Dogs'`, `Lions'`: lowercased to `bombers'`/`dogs'`/`lions'`. `canonicalise()`'s existing possessive strip, `.replace(/['’]s\b/g, '')`, requires a literal `s` immediately after the apostrophe (it matches `richmond's` → `richmond`, `dusty's` → `dusty`) — here the apostrophe is immediately followed by whitespace/end-of-string, not `s`, so it does **not** match and the apostrophe survives attached to the word. This rule is byte-identical to before AFLDB-ISSUE-218 — that issue touched `AGG_WORDS`, `LEADING_SCOPE_CLAUSE_REQUEST_PREFIX_RE`, `TEAM_METRIC_WORDS` and two new gated wrapper regexes, none of which are the possessive strip.
  - **First point of divergence, confirmed unchanged:** `extractClubs`'s `\bbombers\b` (etc.) word-boundary regex still matches *inside* `bombers'` (a `\b` boundary exists between the word-char `s` and the non-word-char `'`), so the club itself resolves correctly (`scope.clubFor`/`clubAgainst` set) — the defect is NOT in club matching, and AFLDB-ISSUE-218 did not touch `extractClubs`'s matching logic (only its already-existing word-order fallback was *read*, not modified, in that issue's `/2` investigation). It is in the final leftover-token reconciliation at the end of `parseNlQuestion` (`src/search/nl/parser.ts` ~line 4123/4177, also untouched by AFLDB-ISSUE-218): `totalTokens = meaningfulTokens(normalised)` splits the (still apostrophe-bearing) normalised text on whitespace, producing the token `"bombers'"` verbatim, while `consumedSet = meaningfulTokens(allConsumed)` is built from the matched club's plain name/alias, `"bombers"` (no apostrophe) — pushed by `extractClubs`'s own `consumed` array, which carries the matched vocabulary string, not a copy of the exact substring found in `text`. `"bombers'" !== "bombers"`, so `consumedSet.has("bombers'")` is false, and it survives as a `leftoverToken`, reported verbatim as `unsupported_term: "bombers'"` even though the club had already resolved. This reproduces the exact residual evidence in AFLDB-ISSUE-214 §10c and AFLDB-ISSUE-218's own `team_match_result/0` deferral.
- **Cross-family scope, confirmed by direct source trace of `tools/nl/generate-exploratory-corpus-v2.mjs` rather than by running the (host-only) generated corpus, re-verified against current `dev` (AFLDB-ISSUE-218's own round-2 correction touched only `team_match_result` template 2's expectation columns, not the `possessive()` helper or any other template):** the generator's `possessive()` helper (line 178, `(name) => name + (/s$/i.test(name) ? "'" : "'s")`) is used across five distinct grain families, not one: `team_match_result` (line 304, "What was `<Club>'` biggest `<victory/defeat>` against `<opp>` at `<venue>` ..." — template 0, the same template AFLDB-ISSUE-218 identified as `team_match_result/0` and deferred), `team_checkpoint_collision` (line 333), `q3_comeback_near_miss` (lines 342, 344), `club_season_rank` (line 366, the AFLDB-ISSUE-214 residual family) and `team_streak` (line 389, "What is `<Club>'` longest `<kind>` streak against `<opp>` ..."). Every one of these families' template shares the identical defect mechanism traced above — confirming this is a shared `canonicalise()`/entity-resolution defect, not something owned by `team_match_result`, `club_season`, `team_streak` or any other individual builder, exactly as both AFLDB-ISSUE-214 and AFLDB-ISSUE-218 independently concluded when they each deferred it. (`unsupported_composition`, line 508, also uses `possessive()` but is a deliberately-unsupported feature-gap family for an unrelated reason — not part of this issue's target surface.)
- **Fix (`src/search/nl/vocab.ts`), smallest shared-layer change, no club/venue/alias special-casing — unchanged from the original implementation, still the narrowest correct layer on current `dev`:** `canonicalise()` gains one new generic replace, applied immediately after the existing punctuation-to-space pass (so any other punctuation has already become whitespace and a word-final apostrophe is reliably followed by a boundary): `text.replace(/(\w)['’](?=\s|$)/g, '$1')` — strips a trailing apostrophe immediately before whitespace/end-of-string, mirroring the existing `'s\b` rule (which already applies to every word generically, not just club names) rather than adding a club-specific pattern. A mid-word apostrophe (`o'brien`, followed by another letter, never a boundary) is untouched, so this is not a blanket apostrophe deletion — see the guardrail checks below.

  - Multi-word club names remain correct: `North Melbourne` (no possessive) and the combined `GWS Giants'` alias (possessive on the second word of a two-word alias) both tested.

  - Unknown words ending in apostrophes still fail closed: `Glorbins'` (not a club, not a player, not any vocabulary word) still declines — the new rule strips the apostrophe generically (exactly as the pre-existing `'s\b` rule already does for every unrecognised word ending in `'s`), it does not add "unknown-word" as a special case; the unrecognised word still surfaces as a leftover/unresolved token and the question still declines. A second regression (`"Richmond's supporters' favourite ground"`, no metric/cue at all) confirms stripping does not manufacture a plan out of an unsupported sentence.
  - Cross-family proof: `team_match_result`, `club_season_rank` and `team_streak` — three distinct grains, exceeding the required two.

Not opened as its own tracked issue in this closeout — the same category of defect AFLDB-ISSUE-199/201/204 each corrected with a small, self-verifying correction script; recorded as a candidate for that treatment separately. **Corrected 2026-09-17 (Fable 5.1, final Fable NL code review acceptance pass, operator-validated):** adjudicated `STALE/INVALID EXPECTATION` from current canonical data, not from the v65/v66 control alone — stored `player_career_stats` (Dane Rampe finals 24 / premierships 0, final season 2026; Nick Dal Santo finals 24 / premierships 0, final season 2016), an independent recount from `player_match_stats` ⋈ `matches` under `rebuild_derived.py`'s own rule (Rampe 24 finals, 4 Grand Finals played, 0 won, last final 2026-09-05; Dal Santo 24 / 3 / 0, last final 2016-09-10), and the production `premierships = 0 ORDER BY finals DESC, display_name` leaderboard (Rampe 24, Dal Santo 24, then Len Thompson / Ray Byrne / Rene Kink 22) all agree: a genuine two-way tie, nobody else at 24. Corrected V5 → V6 (`/home/arm/nl-stress-corpus-v6.csv`) by a new checked-in, fail-closed script `tools/nl/fix-stale-finals-without-premiership-tie.ts` (unit tests `tests/nl-finals-without-premiership-corpus-fix.test.ts` 10/10, `typecheck` clean): rows 41/42/43 only, `expected_answer_primary` "Nick Dal Santo" → "Dane Rampe|Nick Dal Santo" (the corpus's own any-of-these lead form, in the query's deterministic tie order), `expected_tie_count` 1 → 2, `expected_answer_value` 24 preserved, 0 non-target rows touched. Final V6 parse+execute on parser v66 against `afldb_dev`: **12000/12000 clean / 0 soft / 0 failed / 0 errors**. V6 supersedes V5 as the stable regression-corpus baseline. Known volatility recorded in the script header: Rampe is active and the 2026 finals were in progress (latest loaded match 2026-09-13), so another Rampe final would make the true answer "Dane Rampe, 25, tie 1" and re-stale these rows for the same honest reason.
- **Host exploratory V2 (29,030 rows / 27,530 scored), parse+execute against current `afldb_dev`, using the AFLDB-ISSUE-218-corrected corpus (`/home/arm/nl-exploratory-v2-corrected.csv`, not the pre-correction file, which still carries ISSUE-218's own 569-row oracle defect):**
  ```text
  v65: 27530 scored / 20512 clean / 7018 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required
  v66: 27530 scored / 20876 clean / 6654 soft / 0 failed / 1500 audit-required
  net: +364 clean / -364 soft / 0 failed / 0 hard regressions
  ```
  Manual row-ID reconciliation from `failures.csv` (`nl:stress:compare` could not perform its own row-severity comparison against these V1-shape runs even after `--report-only` — a harness limitation, not a validation failure; the aggregate totals plus this manual reconciliation, both from the runs' own output files, substitute as the direct proof): v65 7018 finding rows → v66 6654; **364 improved, 0 regressed, 6654 still soft** (unchanged, unrelated). Improvement clusters, summing exactly to 364: `club_season_rank` 210 (the AFLDB-ISSUE-214 §10c residual, exactly), `team_streak` 75, `team_match_result` 56 (the AFLDB-ISSUE-218 `/0` cluster, exactly), `team_checkpoint_collision` 16, `q3_comeback_near_miss` 7. **Scope proof:** all 364 improved questions contain a trailing-apostrophe token; 0 improved questions lack one. Aliases represented (summing to 364): Giants' 51, Bombers' 48, Pies' 45, Dogs' 45, Swans' 44, Suns' 42, Tigers' 34, Bulldogs' 33, Lions' 22.
- **Resolution:** **RESOLVED 2026-09-17.** All required outcomes met: implementation and own tests fully correct (local 605/605, host-reconfirmed 605/605); broader gates 402/402 both locally and on host; cross-family fix confirmed on real host/runtime/database across five families (exceeding the required minimum of two), with an explicit scope proof that every improved row carries a trailing-apostrophe alias and none lack one; zero hard regressions in either corpus (the three V5 failures proven pre-existing via decisive control); zero unrelated movement in the exploratory V2 diff. `PARSER_VERSION` 66 final. ## AFLDB-ISSUE-220 — Web service credential boundary contradicts the application's `afldb_import` requirement; owner-role code-test DSN and a complete `.env` copy reach the internet-facing process

- **Status:** Open (opened 2026-09-17). Implemented 2026-09-17 (Sonnet 5, worktree `afldb-issue-220`,
  uncommitted) — see Implementation below; pending operator DEV/PROD verification before resolution.
- **Severity:** High. Security posture (a documented credential isolation that does not hold, and
  an owner-role DSN live in the public web process) and, depending on the open runtime question,
  availability of the entire Admin Centre write path.
- **Area:** Deployment / runtime — `deploy/afldb.service`, `docs/deployment.md` §9,
  `tools/build/prepare-standalone.mjs`, the Next.js standalone build output.
- **Found:** 2026-09-17, Fable 5.1 code review of AFLDB outside NL search (Pass 4, deployment and
  runtime safety). Host facts below were gathered by the operator on streamanator (DEV) with
  read-only commands that printed variable names and source line numbers only; no credential
  value was displayed or recorded anywhere.
- **Key files:** `deploy/afldb.service:35-44` (`UnsetEnvironment=` and its comment),
  `docs/deployment.md:1093-1097` (§9 "The service process holds only `DATABASE_URL`, which
  cannot write") and `docs/deployment.md:245` (`AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is the **owner**
  DSN for `code_test_db`, `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL` the import DSN),
  `tools/build/prepare-standalone.mjs` (copies static/public/coming-soon into
  `.next/standalone`, never inspects `.env`), `.gitignore:11,25-28` (`.next/` and `.env*`
  ignored), the twenty-one `process.env.AFLDB_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL` readers:
  `src/db/queries/admin-{awards,brownlow,club-leadership,coaches,draft,fixtures,season-lists,special-records}.ts`,
  `src/db/queries/{awards-admin,data-edits,match-admin,match-sheet,player-links,players}.ts`,
  `src/lib/ingest/pipeline.ts:257`, `src/lib/external-afl/current-season-import.ts:376`;
  `tests/current-season-import.test.ts:4801-4802` (pins the *settle* unit's DSN list only),
  `tests/settle-season-revalidation.test.ts:1073` (the only test reading `deploy/afldb.service`).

### Trigger
Install `deploy/afldb.service` as tracked on any host, or build with `output: 'standalone'` on a
host whose project `.env` holds the full credential set, then (a) inspect the web process's
credentials and (b) invoke any `afldb_import`-backed admin mutation (data editor, awards,
coaches, draft, season lists, fixtures, Brownlow, special records, player links, match sheet,
legacy submission promotion, current-season refresh).

### Expected
The unit, `docs/deployment.md` §9 and the application agree on the DSN set the web process holds;
the stated isolation ("a compromise there cannot reach a role that can write, migrate or dump")
is true; every credential the process holds is one it needs; the build output carries no
credential file.

### Actual (confirmed)
1. **Boundary claim vs application requirement (source, current tree).** The unit removes
   `AFLDB_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL` from the service environment and its comment says the website
   needs only the read-only app role. Since migration 066 (AFLDB-ISSUE-027, 2026-08-22) every
   Admin Centre statistical mutation opens an `afldb_import` connection from
   `process.env.AFLDB_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL` and fails closed without it. The docs still describe
   the pre-066 contract. Nothing in `src/`, `deploy/server-cluster.mjs` or
   `tools/build/prepare-standalone.mjs` reads `.env` for the web process.
2. **Owner-role DSN in the internet-facing process (DEV host evidence, 2026-09-17).** The running
   service's initial environment contains `DATABASE_URL`, `AFLDB_AUTH_DATABASE_URL`,
   `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` and `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL`. The last two were
   introduced by AFLDB-ISSUE-146 (code-test rebuild rehearsal) after the unit's unset list was
   written and were never added to it. `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is an owner-role DSN, so
   the public web process can create, alter and drop objects in `code_test_db`, and
   `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL` gives it a second import-role credential. The unit's
   hand-typed deny list therefore fails open for every DSN added after it was written — the same
   shape as the `privileges.sql` hand-typed `afldb_auth` list already known to silently miss new
   tables.
3. **Complete `.env` copy inside the build output (DEV host evidence, 2026-09-17).**
   `/home/arm/projects/afldb/.next/standalone/.env` exists and carries the same variable names as
   the project `.env`: import, owner, backup, test, SMTP and API credentials included. No
   repository code copies it there; `.next/` and `.env*` are both git-ignored; the only writer of
   `.next/standalone/` other than `prepare-standalone.mjs` is `next build`, so the copy is the
   framework's own file tracing of the env file it loaded at build time. That file sits inside a
   directory the unit grants `ReadWritePaths=` to, is deployed with every build, and is outside
   the unit's `UnsetEnvironment=` mechanism entirely.

### Runtime branch — SETTLED 2026-09-17: branch (a), from Next.js source on the DEV host
The operator read the control flow in the installed Next.js (`node_modules/next/dist/server/`)
and the generated `.next/standalone/server.js` on streamanator (source lines only, no values):
- `.next/standalone/server.js` sets its directory to `__dirname` (the standalone root) and
  `chdir`s into it, so the server's `dir` is the directory that holds the copied `.env` (E6).
- `BaseServer`'s constructor calls `this.loadEnvConfig()`; `NextServer.loadEnvConfig()` calls
  `@next/env`'s `loadEnvConfig(this.dir, …)`. That call is unconditional on the production
  start-up path.
- The `__NEXT_PRIVATE_STANDALONE_CONFIG` early return in `config.js` bypasses only
  `loadConfig`'s own env-loader call; it does not reach or skip the `BaseServer` call.
**Consequence (branch (a)).** Every variable in `.next/standalone/.env` — import, owner, backup,
test, SMTP and API credentials — is loaded into the web process at start-up. `UnsetEnvironment=`
in `deploy/afldb.service` removes those names from the exec-time environment and nothing else;
the framework puts them straight back. The Admin Centre's `afldb_import` writes work on DEV only
because the documented boundary is bypassed, which reconciles the AFLDB-ISSUE-155/165/167 DEV
acceptances with AFLDB-ISSUE-107's exec-time `/proc/<pid>/environ` view (E8), and makes the
"cannot reach a role that can write, migrate or dump" claim false on any host built this way.
Branch (b) (admin mutations failing closed) is ruled out for DEV.

**Kept separate, not established:** *how* `.env` comes to be in `.next/standalone/`. The
build-trace lines the operator displayed did not establish the copying mechanism. The evidence is
only that no repository code writes it (E7) and that it is present after `next build`. The
implementation task must identify the mechanism from the installed Next's build code or
`node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before choosing how to exclude it (runbook §5, §6 step 4).

**Independently observed, separate from the loading path:** the two code-test DSNs (E5),
including the owner-role `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, are present in the service's *initial*
(exec-time) environment because the unit's deny list never names them. That gap exists whether
or not the standalone `.env` is loaded, and is fixed by the unit alone.

### First wrong layer
Deployment contract. `deploy/afldb.service` and `docs/deployment.md` §9 were written for the
pre-066 world and never revised when admin writes moved onto `afldb_import`; the deny list was
never extended when AFLDB-ISSUE-146 added the code-test DSNs; and no test pins the web unit's
credential set against the application's requirement (the existing contract test pins only the
settle unit).

### Root cause (as far as established)
- Findings 1 and 2: a hand-maintained deny list (`UnsetEnvironment=`) as the sole credential
  boundary, with no allow-list, no test, and no review step when new DSN names are introduced.
- Finding 3 (corrected 2026-09-17, implementation §4b): **not** ordinary output-file-tracing.
  `writeStandaloneDirectory` in the installed Next 16.3.1's own `next/dist/build/index.js`
  (lines 321–345) copies any file whose loaded env path is exactly `.env` or `.env.production`
  into `.next/standalone/` unconditionally, in a hardcoded loop entirely separate from
  `copyTracedFiles`/output file tracing. No `next.config.ts` knob (`outputFileTracingExcludes`
  included) reaches or suppresses this loop — confirmed by reading the loop itself, not inferred.
  The project's build wrapper never checked for the resulting file.

### Reproduction (read-only, names only)
1. `ssh arm@10.0.40.100 "tr '\0' '\n' </proc/$(systemctl show afldb -p MainPID --value)/environ | grep -oE '^[A-Z_]*DATABASE_URL' | sort"` — expect the two `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_*` names beside `DATABASE_URL` and `AFLDB_AUTH_DATABASE_URL`.
2. `ssh arm@10.0.40.100 "grep -oE '^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=' ~/projects/afldb/.next/standalone/.env | sed 's/=$//' | sort"` — expect the full project variable-name set.
3. Runtime branch: read the control flow at the reported `loadEnvConfig` / `STANDALONE_CONFIG` lines (runbook §4).

### Implementation (Sonnet 5, 2026-09-17, worktree `afldb-issue-220`, uncommitted)

**§4b established.** Read `node_modules/next/dist/build/index.js` (Next 16.3.1, via a sibling
worktree's `node_modules` — this worktree has none) — `writeStandaloneDirectory` (lines 321–345)
copies `requiredServerFiles.files` plus, separately, any `loadedEnvFiles` entry whose path is
`.env` or `.env.production`, unconditionally, for every `output: 'standalone'` build. This is a
hardcoded file copy, not output-file-tracing, so `next.config.ts` is correctly left untouched
(runbook §5's "only if" does not apply — recorded, not guessed). `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`
has no page describing this copy either way. Fix has to live in the build wrapper, which the
runbook's §5 already anticipated (the `prepare-standalone.mjs` assertion item).

**Runbook refinement (not a contradiction of established facts):** §5/§6 step 6 said to derive the
web unit's expected DSN set from `docs/deployment.md`'s §9 table "so a future DSN cannot be missed
again." That table was itself missing five real, code-referenced DSN names (`AFLDB_AUTH_DATABASE_URL`,
`AFLDB_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL`, `AFLDB_TEST_AUTH_DATABASE_URL`, `AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`,
`AFLDB_CODE_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL`) — deriving the contract test from it as written would have
reproduced this issue's exact mechanism inside the new test. Derived the test from `.env.example`
instead (the tracked, complete, git-versioned template `docs/deployment.md:1069` already calls
authoritative) and brought the §9 table up to the same completeness as part of the same doc-alignment
step, rather than opening a separate issue for a doc gap discovered while fixing this one.

**Changes:**
- `deploy/afldb.service` — `UnsetEnvironment=` now denies `AFLDB_OWNER_DATABASE_URL
  AFLDB_TEST_DATABASE_URL AFLDB_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL AFLDB_TEST_AUTH_DATABASE_URL
  AFLDB_CODE_TEST_DATABASE_URL AFLDB_CODE_TEST_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL AFLDB_BACKUP_DATABASE_URL
  AFLDB_PROD_DATABASE_URL` (F-A: added the two code-test names and the two test-role names that
  were never in the list; F-C: removed `AFLDB_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL`, which the process genuinely
  needs since migration 066). Kept: `DATABASE_URL`, `AFLDB_AUTH_DATABASE_URL`,
  `AFLDB_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL`. Comment rewritten to state the three-DSN contract and point at the
  new test.
- `tools/build/env-in-standalone.mjs` (new) — `findEnvFiles`/`removeEnvFiles`, pure functions
  isolated from `prepare-standalone.mjs`'s top-level side effects so a test can exercise real
  removal behaviour against a scratch directory instead of the real build output.
- `tools/build/prepare-standalone.mjs` — calls `removeEnvFiles(standalone)` right after confirming
  `.next/standalone` exists; `process.exit(1)` if any `.env*` survives (F-B).
- `docs/deployment.md` §9 — added the five missing DSN rows; rewrote the "does not receive them
  all" paragraph for the three-DSN contract and named the new test; added a paragraph on the build
  output no longer carrying `.env*`, citing this issue's §4b.
- `tests/deploy-web-unit.test.ts` (new; no existing suite fit — the one deploy-contract suite,
  `tests/settle-season-revalidation.test.ts`, pins the reverse-proxy/HOSTNAME contract, not
  credentials) — three `describe` blocks: (1) derives the full `*_DATABASE_URL` name set from
  `.env.example` and asserts the unit keeps exactly the three and denies every other one by name,
  so a future addition to `.env.example` fails this test until the unit is updated; (2) exercises
  `removeEnvFiles`/`findEnvFiles` against a real scratch directory (creates `.env` + `.env.production`
  + unrelated files, asserts only the env files are removed) and pins that `prepare-standalone.mjs`
  calls it and exits 1 if anything survives; (3) pins `docs/deployment.md` against the stale
  "holds only `DATABASE_URL`" sentence and checks every `.env.example` DSN name is documented.

**Not changed:** `next.config.ts` (no knob applies, see above); the settle unit and its own
`AFLDB_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL`-only contract (`tests/current-season-import.test.ts:4801-4802`, a
different file, unaffected); `.env`/`.env.example` values (no secret touched).

### Validation

**Local, operator-run 2026-09-17 (worktree `afldb-issue-220`):**
- `npx --no-install vitest run tests/deploy-web-unit.test.ts` — **15/15 passed.**
- `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit` — **clean** (confirms the new `tests/deploy-web-unit.test.ts` →
  `tools/build/env-in-standalone.mjs` `.mjs`-by-extension import resolves correctly under
  `moduleResolution: bundler` + `allowJs`, the one open risk noted at implementation time).

**Still outstanding** (runbook §8 steps 2–6, this issue's acceptance criteria, §9): DEV unit
reinstall + restart, the two DEV names-only checks (running process holds exactly
`AFLDB_AUTH_DATABASE_URL AFLDB_IMPORT_DATABASE_URL DATABASE_URL`; no `.env*` under
`.next/standalone/`), one `afldb_import`-backed Admin Centre write + revert on DEV, `npm run build`
on DEV with the new `prepare-standalone.mjs` assertion passing, then PROD read-only steps 2–3
before any PROD unit change (PROD still not inspected for this issue) and steps 2–3 again after.
Status stays **Open** until that evidence is in hand — no further implementation changes pending
this validation.

### Follow-up
- Related closed issues: AFLDB-ISSUE-027 (migration 066 moved admin writes to `afldb_import`),
  AFLDB-ISSUE-107 (exec-time environment evidence, 2026-08-29), AFLDB-ISSUE-122 (settle unit
  precedent for keeping exactly one writing DSN), AFLDB-ISSUE-146 (introduced the code-test DSNs).
- PROD has not been inspected; the runbook requires the same names-only checks there before any
  unit change.
